Qui licet dixerint se quærere Dei honorem, tamen mentiti sunt: nam quæsierunt se ipsos, cupientes ab hominibus honorari. Vel sic: Qui a semetipso loquitur, hoc est ex proprio spiritu, non ex inspiratione divina, propriam gloriam quærit, quamvis prædicet vera ac sancta. Tales sunt modo innumerabiles, qui quærunt videri, reputari, promoveri, præesse, et ad hee obtinenda laborant, studendo, docendo, et multa specie tenus bona agendo. Est enim qui nequiter se humiliat, et interiora ejus plena sunt dolo. Verumtamen tales primo et maxime fallunt se ipsos.
paras.en: [[7:18|He that speaketh of himself|Qui a semetipso loquitur]], that is, teaches and preaches his own inventions, not truths revealed from above, [[7:18|seeketh his own glory|gloriam propriam quærit]]. For he works out of private love, not divine, and is vain and proud. Such were the heretics, and the teachers of evil laws, like Mahomet: who, though they said they sought God's honour, yet lied: for they sought themselves, desiring to be honoured by men. Or thus: *He that speaketh of himself*, that is, from his own spirit, not from divine inspiration, seeks his own glory, though he preach true and holy things. Such are now countless men, who seek to be seen, esteemed, promoted, to be over others, and who labour to obtain these things by studying, teaching, and doing many things good in appearance. For [[Ecclus 19:23|There is one that humbleth himself wickedly, and his interior is full of deceit|Est enim qui nequiter se humiliat, et interiora ejus plena sunt dolo]]. Yet such men deceive themselves first and most.

paras.t: Qui autem quærit gloriam ejus qui misit illum, hoc est ego et qui mea sectantur vestigia, qui quærimus gloriam Dei Patris, hic verax est veritate doctrinæ et vitæ, quia Deo instruente profatur; et injustitia, hoc est mala intentio, seu peccatum reprehensione dignum, in illo non est. Hoc certum est quantum ad Christum. Sed quantum ad famulos ejus, non est sic intelligendum quod sint omnino a culpa immunes; sed sunt sine peccato mortali, et quantum ad hoc quod gloriam Dei quærunt, injustitia carent. Soli etenim Deo debetur honor et gloria. Idcirco, qui quærit gloriam propriam, furtum committit, subripiens Deo quod ejus est. Per hæc ergo probat Christus suam doctrinam esse a Deo. Non enim quæsivit gloriam propriam inordinate, sed totius paupertatis et humilitatis præbuit se in exemplum, nemini blandiens, neminem palpans, sed usque ad mortem pro justitia certans, ita quod verissime dicere potuit illud beati Job: Donec deficiam, non recedam ab innocentia mea. Justificationem meam quam cœpi tenere, non deseram.
paras.en: [[7:18|but he that seeketh the glory of him that sent him|Qui autem quærit gloriam ejus qui misit illum]], that is, I, and those who follow my footsteps, who seek the glory of God the Father, [[7:18|he is true|hic verax est]], with the truth of doctrine and of life, since he speaks as God teaches him; [[7:18|and there is no injustice in him|et injustitia in illo non est]], that is, evil intention, or sin worthy of rebuke. This is certain as to Christ. But as to his servants, it is not to be understood that they are altogether free from fault; but they are without mortal sin, and in so far as they seek God's glory they are free of injustice. For [[1 Tim 1:17|to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory|Soli … Deo … honor et gloria]] is due. Therefore he who seeks his own glory commits theft, stealing from God what is his. By these things, then, Christ proves his doctrine to be from God. For he did not seek his own glory inordinately, but gave himself as an example of all poverty and humility, flattering no one, fawning on no one, but [[Ecclus 4:33|even unto death fight for justice|usque ad mortem pro justitia certans]], so that he could most truly say that of blessed Job: [[Job 27:5|Till I die I will not depart from my innocence|Donec deficiam, non recedam ab innocentia mea]]. [[Job 27:6|My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake|Justificationem meam quam cœpi tenere, non deseram]].

paras.t: Sed quia Judæi objecerunt Christo quod legem Moysis non servaret (dictum est enim quinto capitulo, quod persequebantur Christum eo quod paralyticum curasset in sabbato), ideo subdit: Nonne Moyses dedit vobis legem, tanquam minister Dei, non sicut principalis legislator, quomodo Christus dedit nobis evangelicam legem, et nemo ex vobis facit, hoc est observat, /egem in omnibus? Hoc asserit Christus cordium judex et cognitor, vel quia in turba quam alloquebatur, nullus fuit justus legisque factor, vel quia tam pauci fuerunt quod comparatione aliorum quasi nulli videbantur. Per hoc innuit Christus, quod digni non erant eum arguere de sabbati transgressione, quamvis sic fuisset: quia qui in majoribus vel paribus culpis sunt, non habent faciem alios increpandi, præsertim si ex officio eis non incumbat. Caritas enim debet esse ordinata, ut unusquisque in primis corrigat semetipsum, deinde et proximum. Quid me quæritis interficere, quod est contra legem, qua prohibet innocentes occidi? Hoc Christus dixit, ut ostenderet se illorum machinationes cognoscere, et eos ad emendationem induceret, non tamen ut mortem imminentem evaderet.
paras.en: But since the Jews had charged Christ with not keeping the law of Moses (for it was said in the fifth chapter that they persecuted Christ because he had healed the paralytic on the sabbath[[John 5:16||]]), he adds: [[7:19|Did not Moses give you the law|Nonne Moyses dedit vobis legem]], as God's minister, not as the principal lawgiver, as Christ gave us the law of the Gospel, [[7:19|and yet none of you keepeth the law|et nemo ex vobis facit legem?]], that is, observes the law in all things? Christ, the judge and knower of hearts, asserts this either because in the crowd he was addressing no one was just and a doer of the law, or because they were so few that in comparison with the others they seemed as none. By this Christ implies that they were not worthy to accuse him of breaking the sabbath, even had it been so: since those who are in greater or equal faults have no face to rebuke others, above all if it is not their office. For charity must be ordered, so that each man corrects himself first, and then his neighbour. [[7:20|Why seek you to kill me|Quid me quæritis interficere]], which is against the law, which forbids the innocent to be killed? Christ said this to show that he knew their plots, and to lead them to amendment, not in order to escape the death that awaited him.

paras.t: Respondit ei turba, id est multitudo illa turbata, et dixit: Dæmonium habes, hoc est, quasi insensatus et malitiosus loqueris, malum suspicando de nobis. Quis vestrum te quærit interficere ? quasi dicant, Nullus. Et utrumque mentiti sunt, imponentes Filio Dei insaniam atque mendacium. Nam in principio hujus capituli dixit Evangelista, quod Judæi quærebant Jesum occidere. Et quid tam irrationale, ut Christo qui est sapientia et veritas Patris, qui et dæmones expulit verbo, regnumque diaboli dissipavit idololatriam destruendo, imponere tantam dementiam et falsitatem ?
paras.en: [[7:20|The multitude answered and said: Thou hast a devil|Respondit … turba … et dixit: Dæmonium habes]], the crowd, that is, that disturbed multitude, that is, you speak like a senseless and malicious man, suspecting evil of us. [[7:20|Who seeketh to kill thee|Quis vestrum te quærit interficere]]? as though they said, No one. And in both they lied, charging the Son of God with madness and falsehood. For at the beginning of this chapter the Evangelist said that the Jews sought to kill Jesus[[7:1||]]. And what is so unreasonable as to charge with such madness and falsehood Christ, who is the wisdom and truth of the Father, who also drove out demons with a word[[Matt 8:16||]], and scattered the kingdom of the devil by destroying idolatry?

paras.t: Respondit Jesus, et dixit eis: Unum opus feci: non unum dumtaxat, quoniam omnia facta sunt per me. Pater quoque meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor. Sed unum opus feci, cujus occasione contra me. murmuratis, mihique legis transgressionem imponitis. Opus istud est curatio paralytici, cui jussit Jesus ferre grabatum suum et ambulare: quod factum est sabbato, quemadmodum dictum est quinto capitulo. Et omnes miramini admiratione turbante, ex malitia procedente: miramini, inquam, quod ego qui videor religiosus, et zelum Dei me habere ostendo, hoc feci in sabbato. Qui enim odit alium, facta illius faciliter interpretatur in pejus, et ea qua vel in se bona sunt vel modice culpabilia, adeo magni pendit ac reprobat, ut apud se miretur quod ille talia operatur. Hoc modo Manichæus atque Montanus mirabantur quod Deus legis et Prophetarum præcepit plebi Israel spoliare /Egyptum.
paras.en: [[7:21|Jesus answered and said to them: One work I have done|Respondit Jesus, et dixit eis: Unum opus feci]]: not one only, since [[John 1:3|All things were made by him|omnia facta sunt per me]] [Denis: “by me”]. And [[John 5:17|My Father worketh until now; and I work|Pater quoque meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor]]. But I have done one work, on account of which you murmur against me and charge me with breaking the law. This work is the healing of the paralytic, whom Jesus bade take up his bed and walk[[John 5:8||]]: which was done on the sabbath[[John 5:9||]], as was said in the fifth chapter. [[7:21|and you all wonder|Et omnes miramini]], with a troubled wonder proceeding from malice: you wonder, I say, that I who seem religious, and show that I have zeal for God, did this on the sabbath. For he who hates another readily interprets his deeds for the worse, and makes so much of, and so condemns, the things that are either good in themselves or slightly blameworthy, that he wonders within himself that the other does such things. In this way Manichæus and Montanus wondered that the God of the law and the Prophets commanded the people of Israel to spoil Egypt[[Ex 3:22||]].

paras.t: In verbis istis commendatur nobis ineffabilis patientia, mansuetudo atque tranquillitas Christi, qui ad tantam contumeliam, tam benigne mititerque respondit. Discamus ergo Christi exemplo injurias verborum æquanimiter ferre, adversa tranquillo animo sustinere, non reddere malum pro malo, nec vinci a malo, sed vincere malum in bono. Ideo nempe dicit Psalmista: Posui ori meo custodiam, dum consisteret peccator adversum me. Et Salomon in Proverbiis: Non respondeas stulto juxta stultitiam suam, ne efficiaris ei similis. Alibi quoque hortatur: Ne dicas: Reddam malum pro malo; exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te; et, Ne dicas, Quomodo fecit mihi, sic faciam ei. — Denique induratis istis Judæis, qui tam faciliter proruperunt in verba contumeliosa atque blasphema, assimilantur homines passionati, vitiosi et impatientes, qui licet foris aliquid boni agere videantur, intus tamen languoribus anima pleni sunt, præcipue morbo qui dicitur, Noli me tangere. Unde quum parum pulsantur, tanguntur vel exercitantur, evomunt quo replentur. Prorumpunt enim in verba malitiæ et nequitiæ, in verba fœtida, pungitiva et inordinatissima.
paras.en: In these words is commended to us the ineffable patience, meekness and calm of Christ, who answered so great an insult so kindly and gently. Let us learn, then, by Christ's example, to bear insults in words with an even mind, to endure adversities with a calm mind, not to render evil for evil, [[Rom 12:21|Be not overcome by evil: but overcome evil by good|nec vinci a malo, sed vincere malum in bono]]. For this is why the Psalmist says: [[Ps 38:2|I have set a guard to my mouth, when the sinner stood against me|Posui ori meo custodiam, dum consisteret peccator adversum me]]. And Solomon in Proverbs: [[Prov 26:4|Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou be made like him|Non respondeas stulto juxta stultitiam suam, ne efficiaris ei similis]]. Elsewhere too he exhorts: [[Prov 20:22|Say not: I will return evil: wait for the Lord, and he will deliver thee|Ne dicas: Reddam malum pro málo; exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te]]; and, [[Prov 24:29|Say not: I will do to him as he hath done to me|Ne dicas, Quomodo fecit mihi, sic faciam ei]]. Further, to these hardened Jews, who broke out so readily into insulting and blasphemous words, are likened passionate, vicious and impatient men, who, though outwardly they seem to do some good, are yet within full of the sicknesses of the soul, above all the disease called *Noli me tangere* [“Touch me not”, the name of a malignant ulcer; here, touchiness]. Hence when they are struck a little, touched or tried, they vomit out what they are full of. For they break out into words of malice and wickedness, into foul, stinging and most disordered words.

paras.t: Propterea, hoc est ad præfigurandum opera mea, quin spiritualiter circumcido. Moyses, Deo jubente, dedit, hoc est, in scriptis redegit atque proposuit, vobis circumcisionem, hoc est præceptum circumcisionis masculorum in præputio, dicens: Masculus cujus præputii caro circumcisa non est, delebitur anima illa de populo suo. Non quia ex Moyse est, hoc est, circumcisio originaliter data ac jussa non est Moysi, sed ex patribus, hoc est, Patriarchis data est primo. Primo enim data est Abrahæ, ut patet in Genesi; deinde Isaac, Jacob et duodecim Patriarchis. Propter quod ad Romanos testatur Apostolus: Dico Jesum Christum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis, ad confirmandas promissiones patrum. Hoc Christus adjecit, ad declarandum magnitudinem præcepti circumcisionis. Et in sabbato, hoc est septima die, quæ celebris est, circumciditis hominem infantem. Preceptum equidem fuit, ut infans octavo die circumcideretur. Dum ergo nascebatur in sabbato, circumcidebatur sabbato subsequenti.
paras.en: [[7:22|Therefore, Moses gave you circumcision|Propterea … Moyses … dedit … vobis circumcisionem]], *therefore*, that is, to prefigure my works, who circumcise spiritually; Moses, at God's command, *gave*, that is, put into writing and set before you, circumcision, that is, the precept of the circumcision of males in the foreskin[[Lev 12:3||]], saying: [[Gen 17:14|The male whose flesh of his foreskin shall not be circumcised, that soul shall be destroyed out of his people|Masculus cujus præputii caro circumcisa non est, delebitur anima illa de populo suo]]. [[7:22|not because it is of Moses|Non quia ex Moyse est]], that is, circumcision was not originally given and commanded to Moses, [[7:22|but of the fathers|sed ex patribus]], that is, it was first given to the Patriarchs. For it was given first to Abraham, as appears in Genesis[[Gen 17:10||]]; then to Isaac, Jacob and the twelve Patriarchs. For which reason the Apostle testifies to the Romans: [[Rom 15:8|For I say that Christ Jesus was minister of the circumcision|Dico Jesum Christum ministrum fuisse circumcisionis]], [[Rom 15:8|to confirm the promises made unto the fathers|ad confirmandas promissiones patrum]]. Christ added this to declare the greatness of the precept of circumcision. [[7:22|and on the sabbath day you circumcise a man|et in sabbato circumciditis hominem]], that is, on the seventh day, which is solemn, a male infant. For it was commanded that the infant be circumcised on the eighth day[[Lev 12:3||]]. When, then, he was born on a sabbath, he was circumcised on the following sabbath.

paras.t: Si circumcisionem accipit homo in sabbato, imo quia sic est, ut non solvatur lex Moysis, hoc est absque transgressione præcepti de celebratione sabbati per Moysen dati, mihi indignamini quia totum hominem, hoc est paralytieum illum in corpore et anima, sanum feci in sabbato ? quasi dicat: Hoc valde absurdum est, quum major atque utilior sit curatio totius hominis quam circumcisio corporis. Sed et curatio illa miraculose facta solo verbo, sine labore, magis confert ad gloriam Dei quam circumcisio. In hoc verbo Salvatoris quo dicit, Totum hominem sanum feci, fundatur illud dictum commune, quod Christus sanavit in anima quos curavit in corpore. Dei namque perfecta sunt opera; et iniquis potius obest sospitas carnis quam prosit, dum exhibent membra sua arma iniquitatis peccato.
paras.en: [[7:23|If a man receive circumcision on the sabbath day|Si circumcisionem accipit homo in sabbato]], nay, since it is so, [[7:23|that the law of Moses may not be broken|ut non solvatur lex Moysis]], that is, without breaking the precept of keeping the sabbath given by Moses, [[7:23|are you angry at me, because I have healed the whole man on the sabbath day|mihi indignamini quia totum hominem sanum feci in sabbato?]], that is, that paralytic in body and soul? as though he said: This is very absurd, since the healing of the whole man is greater and more profitable than the circumcision of the body. And that healing too, done miraculously by a word alone, without labour, contributes more to the glory of God than circumcision. On this word of the Saviour in which he says, *I have healed the whole man*, is founded that common saying, that Christ healed in soul those whom he cured in body. For [[Deut 32:4|The works of God are perfect|Dei namque perfecta sunt opera]]; and to the wicked the health of the flesh does more harm than good, while they yield their members [[Rom 6:13|as instruments of iniquity unto sin|arma iniquitatis peccato]].

paras.t: Nolite judicare secundum faciem, id est superficialiter, secundum solam apparentiam, secundum signa incerta, secundum sensum exteriorem. Tale namque judicium sæpius fallit. Sed justum judicium judicate, hoc est, judicando discernite ac proferte, judicando secundum rationem informatam prudentia, regulatam justitia, procedentem secundum ordinem juris, et veritatem rei diligenter pensantem. Præcipit ergo Christus ut judicemus eo modo quo Isaias prædixit de ipso: Non secundum visionem (inquit) oculorum judicabit, neque secundum auditum aurium arguet; sed judicabit in justitia. Quod igitur in Matthæo ait Salvator, Nolite judicare, ut non judicemini, dictum est de judicio inordinato, videlicet usurpatorio, suspicioso, perverso.
paras.en: [[7:24|Judge not according to the appearance|Nolite judicare secundum faciem]], that is, superficially, by the appearance alone, by uncertain signs, by outward sense. For such judgment very often errs. [[7:24|but judge just judgment|Sed justum judicium judicate]], that is, in judging discern and pronounce, judging according to reason informed by prudence, ruled by justice, proceeding according to the order of law, and carefully weighing the truth of the matter. Christ commands, then, that we judge in the way Isaias foretold of him: [[Is 11:3|He shall not judge according to the sight of the eyes, nor reprove according to the hearing of the ears|Non secundum visionem (inquit) oculorum judicabit, neque secundum auditum aurium arguet]]; [[Is 11:4|But he shall judge the poor with justice|sed judicabit in justitia]]. What the Saviour says in Matthew, then, [[Matt 7:1|Judge not, that you may not be judged|Nolite judicare, ut non judicemini]], was said of disordered judgment, namely usurped, suspicious, perverse.

paras.t: Denique, ad rectitudinem seu veritatem judicii multa exiguntur. Primo, ut procedat ex lumine rationis, non ex impetu passionis. De hoc multa dicuntur in libro Job: ut est illud, Numquid sapiens respondebit quasi in ventum loquens, et implebit ardore stomachum suum ? Et illud, Quid perdis in furore animam tuam? Et, Respondete absque contentione. Passiones quippe actum rationis impediunt. Secundo, ut sit sine personarum acceptione, quemadmodum Moyses loquitur in Deuteronomio: Dixi principibus et judicibus: Quod justum est judicate, sive peregrinus sit ille, sive civis; nulla erit distantia personarum; ita parvum audietis ut magnum, nec accipietis cujusquam personam. Oportet ergo privati amoris affectionem, amorem odiumque abjicere, ne judex sit partialis. Tertio, ut clamori vel favori plurimorum non cedatur, juxta illud Exodi: Ne sequaris turbam ad faciendum malum, nec in judicio acquiescas sententiæ plurimorum, ut a vero devies. Quarto, ut causa ignota seu dubia debite inquiratur, prout Job ait: Causam quam ignorabam diligentissime investigabam. Quinto, ne propter timorem æquitas deseratur. Propter quod scriptum est: Noli quærere fieri judex, nisi valeas virtute irrumpere iniquitates, ne forte extimescas faciem potentis. Sexto, ne in judicando plus quam oportet vel decet judicans alicui compatiatur: secundum quod Dominus præcipit in Exodo, Pauperis non misereberis in judicio; et rursus, Non declinabis in judicio pauperis; in Levitico quoque, Non consideres personam pauperis, nec honores vultum potentis. Septimo, ne dona accipiantur, juxta illud Exodi: Non accipias munera, qua excæcant etiam prudentes, et subvertunt verba justorum. Octavo, ne preces admittantur in præjudicium adversariæ partis. Nono, ut altera pars audiatur, et quilibet æquanimiter suam causam proponere permittatur, juxta quod legitur in Actibus Apostolorum: Non est consuetudo Romanis damnare aliquem hominem priusquam is qui accusatur præsentes habeat accusatores, locumque defendendi accipiat ad abluenda crimina. Decimo, ne pœna excedat mensuram culpæ. Propter quod Moyses dicit: Juxta mensuram culpæ erit quantitas plagarum. Undecimo, ut judicium ordinetur ad bonum ejus qui judicatur. His itaque observatis, erit judicium verum veritate justitiæ et doctrinæ, hoc est equum et sapientiale. De hac materia multa jam dixi Matthæi septimo, et ad Romanos secundo: ideirco celerius atque facilius transeo.
paras.en: Further, many things are required for the rightness or truth of judgment. First, that it proceed from the light of reason, not from the drive of passion. Of this many things are said in the book of Job: as is that, [[Job 15:2|Will a wise man answer as if he were speaking in the wind, and fill his stomach with burning heat?|Numquid sapiens respondebit quasi in ventum loquens, et implebit ardore stomachum suum]]? And that, [[Job 18:4|Thou that destroyest thy soul in thy fury|Quid perdis in furore animam tuam]] [Denis: “Why destroyest thou thy soul in thy fury?”]? And, [[Job 6:29|Answer, I beseech you, without contention|Respondete absque contentione]]. For passions hinder the act of reason. Second, that it be without respect of persons, as Moses says in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 1:16|And I commanded them, saying: Hear them, and judge that which is just: whether he be one of your country, or a stranger|Dixi principibus et judicibus : Quod justum est judicate, sive peregrinus sit ille, sive civis]] [Denis: “I said to the princes and judges: Judge that which is just, whether he be a stranger or a citizen”]; [[Deut 1:17|There shall be no difference of persons, you shall hear the little as well as the great: neither shall you respect any man's person|nulla erit distantia personarum; ita parvum audietis ut magnum, nec accipietis cujusquam personam]]. So the affection of private love, love and hatred, must be cast away, lest the judge be partial. Third, that one not yield to the clamour or favour of the many, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 23:2|Thou shalt not follow the multitude to do evil: neither shalt thou yield in judgment, to the opinion of the most part, to stray from the truth|Ne sequaris turbam ad faciendum malum, nec in judicio acquiescas sententiæ plurimorum, ut a vero devies]]. Fourth, that a cause unknown or doubtful be duly inquired into, as Job says: [[Job 29:16|the cause which I knew not, I searched out most diligently|Causam quam ignorabam diligentissime investigabam]]. Fifth, that equity be not forsaken for fear. For which reason it is written: [[Ecclus 7:6|Seek not to be made a judge, unless thou have strength enough to extirpate iniquities: lest thou fear the person of the powerful|Noli quærere fieri judex, nisi valeas virtute irrumpere iniquitates, ne forte extimescas faciem potentis]]. Sixth, that the judge in judging do not pity anyone more than is right or fitting: according to what the Lord commands in Exodus, [[Ex 23:3|Neither shalt thou favour a poor man in judgment|Pauperis non misereberis in judicio]]; and again, [[Ex 23:6|Thou shalt not go aside in the poor man's judgment|Non declinabis in judicio pauperis]]; in Leviticus also, [[Lev 19:15|Respect not the person of the poor: nor honour the countenance of the mighty|Non consideres personam pauperis, nec honores vultum potentis]]. Seventh, that gifts be not taken, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 23:8|Neither shalt thou take bribes, which even blind the wise, and pervert the words of the just|Non accipias munera, qua excæcant etiam prudentes, et subvertunt verba justorum]]. Eighth, that prayers be not admitted to the prejudice of the opposing party. Ninth, that the other party be heard, and each be allowed to set out his cause with an even mind, according to what we read in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 25:16|it is not the custom of the Romans to condemn any man, before that he who is accused have his accusers present and have liberty to make his answer, to clear himself of the things laid to his charge|Non est consuetudo Romanis damnare aliquem hominem priusquam is qui accusatur præsentes habeat accusatores, locumque defendendi accipiat ad abluenda crimina]]. Tenth, that the punishment do not exceed the measure of the fault. For which reason Moses says: [[Deut 25:2|According to the measure of the sin shall the measure also of the stripes be|Juxta mensuram culpæ erit quantitas plagarum]]. Eleventh, that the judgment be ordered to the good of the one who is judged. When these things are observed, the judgment will be true with the truth of justice and of doctrine, that is, equitable and wise. I have already said much on this matter on Matthew 7[[Matt 7:1||]] and on Romans 2[[Rom 2:1||]]: so I pass over it more quickly and easily.

paras.t: Dicebant ergo (videlicet, quoniam Jesus dixit, Quid me quæritis interficere?) quidam ex Jerosolymis, hoc est cives Jerusalem, qui melius quam alii noverant machinationem sacerdotum, Scribarum ac Pharisæorum, qui maxime morabantur in Jerusalem, contra Jesum: Nonne hic est quem quærunt interficere ? tanquam dicerent: Utique iste est. Ecce palam loquitur contra illos, dicendo: Nemo ex vobis facit legem; et, Quid me quæritis interficere ? Sicque imposuit eis gravissima crimina in templo coram omni frequentia plebis. Et nihil ei dicunt: quod videtur procedere, vel ex timore, quasi timentes Jesum, vel ex scientia, quasi scientes nunc eum esse Christum. Ideo addunt: Nunquid vere cognoverunt principes, hoc est principales in populo, scilicet sacerdotes, Scriba, Pharisæi ac seniores, præsertim pontifices, quia hic est Christus? quasi dicant: Hoc apparet ex eo quod silent.
paras.en: [[7:25|Some therefore of Jerusalem said|Dicebant ergo quidam ex Jerosolymis]] (namely because Jesus had said, *Why seek you to kill me?*), that is, citizens of Jerusalem, who knew better than others the plotting against Jesus of the priests, Scribes and Pharisees, who lived mostly in Jerusalem: [[7:25|Is not this he whom they seek to kill|Nonne hic est quem quærunt interficere]]? as though they said: Certainly it is he. [[7:26|And behold, he speaketh openly|Ecce palam loquitur]] against them, saying: *None of you keepeth the law*[[7:19||]]; and, *Why seek you to kill me?*[[7:20||]] And so he laid on them the gravest charges in the temple before the whole crowd of the people. [[7:26|and they say nothing to him|Et nihil ei dicunt]]: which seems to come either from fear, as fearing Jesus, or from knowledge, as knowing now that he is the Christ. So they add: [[7:26|Have the rulers known for a truth that this is the Christ|Numquid vere cognoverunt principes quia hic est Christus?]], the rulers, that is, the chief men among the people, namely the priests, Scribes, Pharisees and elders, above all the high priests? as though they said: This appears from their silence.

paras.t: Isti cives ignorabant Jesum esse tantæ potentiæ, quod sine ejus virtute ac permissione nemo loqui potest aut agere quidquam. Idcirco, quod principes tacuerunt, retulerunt ad eorum scientiam, quum potius referendum fuerit ad Christi dispensationem ac ordinationem, qui quando voluit seu permisit, persecutionem sustinuit. Ista tamen dixerunt dubitando, non affirmando. Unde mox arguunt ad oppositum.
paras.en: These citizens did not know that Jesus was of such power that without his power and permission no one can speak or do anything. Therefore they referred the silence of the rulers to their knowledge, when it should rather have been referred to the dispensation and ordering of Christ, who suffered persecution when he willed or permitted it. Yet they said these things doubting, not affirming. Hence at once they argue to the contrary.

paras.t: Sed et hunc scimus, hoc est cognoscimus, unde sit, hoc est de qua progenie et de quo loco, videlicet a Nazareth Galilææ. Christus autem quum venerit, nemo scit, hoc est sciet, unde sit. Quomodo verum est hoc, quum vulgatum fuerit apud Judæos Christum nasciturum de tribu Juda per David, in Bethlehem ? Dicendum, quod Judæi propter diversa loca Scripture, ambigui erant de qualitate adventus Christi: et forte quod ideo, quia non intellexerunt ex Scripturis quod in Christo esset duplex natura, puta divina et humana, ideireo non poterant concordare Scripturas. Porro, quod aiunt, Christu: quum venerit, nemo scit unde sit, habere poterant ex eo quod scriptum est apud Isaiam: Generationem ejus quis enarrabit? Et Malachias: Quis, inquit, poterit cogitare diem adventus ejus ? aut quis stabit ad videndum eum? Ipse enim quasi ignis conflans. Jeremias quoque ait quarto decimo capitulo: Quare venturus es quasi vir vagus? Et item: Quare venturus quasi colonus in terra? Verum est ergo, quod nemo scit, hoc est comprehendere potest unde sit Christus, id est eternam atque divinam ejus originem. Sed nee generatio ejus de Virgine comprehendi potest a nobis, quantum ad modum ejus. Quis enim capere queat, qualiter de clauso dulcissimæ Virginis utero exiit verum corpus Christi
paras.en: [[7:27|But we know this man, whence he is|Sed … hunc scimus … unde sit]], that is, we know of what stock and from what place, namely from Nazareth of Galilee. [[7:27|but when the Christ cometh, no man knoweth, whence he is|Christus autem quum venerit, nemo scit, hoc est sciet, unde sit]], *knoweth*, that is, shall know. How is this true, when it was commonly held among the Jews that the Christ was to be born of the tribe of Juda through David, in Bethlehem? It must be said that the Jews, because of various places of Scripture, were uncertain about the manner of Christ's coming: and perhaps for this reason, that they did not understand from the Scriptures that in Christ there would be a twofold nature, namely divine and human, they could not make the Scriptures agree. Further, what they say, *when the Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is*, they could have from what is written in Isaias: [[Is 53:8|who shall declare his generation|Generationem ejus quis enarrabit]]? And Malachias: [[Mal 3:2|And who shall be able to think of the day of his coming? and who shall stand to see him? for he is like a refining fire|Quis, inquit, poterit cogitare diem adventus ejus ? aut quis stabit ad videndum eum? Ipse enim quasi ignis conflans]]. Jeremias too says in the fourteenth chapter: [[Jer 14:9|Why wilt thou be as a wandering man|Quare venturus es quasi vir vagus]] [Denis reads *venturus*, “why wilt thou come”]? And again: [[Jer 14:8|why wilt thou be as a stranger in the land|Quare venturus quasi colonus in terra]]? It is true, then, that no one knows, that is, can comprehend, whence the Christ is, that is, his eternal and divine origin. But not even his birth of the Virgin can be comprehended by us, as to its manner. For who could grasp how the true body of Christ came forth from the closed womb of the most sweet Virgin?

paras.t: Clamabat ergo: quia ex magno affectu salutis Judæorum, et voce sonora, sicut Isaias prædixit: Clama, ne cesses; quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam. Quod S. Hieronymus exponit de Christo ad litteram. Quomodo nunc dicitur Jesus clamasse, quum in Isaia sit prophetatum de eo, Non clamabit, nec audietur foris vox ejus? Et respondendum, hoc dictum esse de immoderata seu passionata vociferatione: de qua dicit Apostolus, Omnis clamor, et amaritudo, et indignatio tollatur a vobis. Porro de ordinato Christi clamore fertur in Psalmis: Deus meus, clamabo per diem, et non exaudies; et, Laboravi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ.
paras.en: [[7:28|Jesus therefore cried out|Clamabat ergo]]: since out of great desire for the salvation of the Jews, and with a ringing voice, as Isaias foretold: [[Is 58:1|Cry, cease not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet|Clama, ne cesses; quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam]]. Which St. Jerome explains of Christ literally. How is Jesus now said to have cried out, when it is prophesied of him in Isaias, [[Is 42:2|He shall not cry, nor have respect to person, neither shall his voice be heard abroad|Non clamabit, nec audietur foris vox ejus?]]? The answer is that this was said of immoderate or passionate shouting: of which the Apostle says, [[Eph 4:31|Let all bitterness and anger and indignation and clamour and blasphemy be put away from you|Omnis clamor, et amaritudo, et indignatio tollatur a vobis]]. But of Christ's ordered crying it is said in the Psalms: [[Ps 21:3|O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear|Deus meus, clamabo per diem, et non exaudies]]; and, [[Ps 68:4|I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse|Laboravi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ]].

paras.t: Docens in templo Jesus, et dicens: Et me scitis. Infra ait Christus Judæis: Neque me scitis; et in Matthæo: Nemo novit Filium, nisi Pater; neque Patrem quis novit, nisi Filius. Quomodo ergo nunc asserit, Et me scitis? Responsio plana est. quoniam aliquo modo noverant eum, videlicet secundum sensitivam cognitionem, et quantum ex illa intellectualiter elicere poterant, noverant eum secundum suam humanitatem quodammodo, sed multum imperfecte. Putabant quippe, quod naturali ordine genitus esset, et in esse creatæ subsisteret. Et unde sim scitis, hoc est ortum et patriam meam. Hoc locutus est Christus, quantum ad id quod dixerunt Judæi, Hunc scimus unde sit. Sed quantum ad id quod dixerunt, Christus quum venerit, nemo scit unde sit, respondit: Et a me ipso non veni, hoc est, originem a vobis ignotam habeo, quia a Patre per generationem æternam egressus sum, et ille me misit. Denique quod ait, me ipso non veni, si sic intelligatur, Propria voluntate non veni, verum erit de Christo secundum quod homo: quia voluntas ejus humana non fuit causa quod venit in mundum per incarnationem, sed in incarnatione voluntas illa creata est; voluntas vero Patris fuit causa hujus adventus. Christus autem ut Deus, habet eamdem numero voluntatem eum Patre. Idcirco, quod ait, me ipso non veni, non est accipiendum de Christo secundum naturam divinam, nisi in hoc sensu: me ipso non veni, hoc est, a Patre voluntatem et potestatem accepi per quam veni in mundum, assumendo naturam humanam. Nihilo minus Christus ut Deus, propria voluntate venit ac potestate, imo et misit se ipsum secundum quod homo est.
paras.en: [[7:28|in the temple, teaching and saying: You both know me|Docens in templo Jesus, et dicens: Et me scitis]]. Below Christ says to the Jews: [[John 8:19|Neither me do you know|Neque me scitis]]; and in Matthew: [[Matt 11:27|And no one knoweth the Son but the Father: neither doth any one know the Father, but the Son|Nemo novit Filium, nisi Pater; neque Patrem quis novit, nisi Filius]]. How then does he now assert, *You both know me*? The answer is plain: since they knew him in some way, namely by sense knowledge, and as far as they could draw out from it by the intellect, they knew him in his humanity after a fashion, but very imperfectly. For they thought that he had been begotten in the natural order, and subsisted in created being. [[7:28|and you know whence I am|Et unde sim scitis]], that is, my birth and my country. Christ said this as to what the Jews said, *We know this man, whence he is*. But as to what they said, *When the Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is*, he answered: [[7:28|And I am not come of myself|Et a me ipso non veni]], that is, I have an origin unknown to you, since I came forth from the Father by eternal generation, and he sent me. Further, what he says, *I am not come of myself*, if it is understood thus, I did not come by my own will, will be true of Christ as man: since his human will was not the cause of his coming into the world by the incarnation, but in the incarnation that will was created; whereas the Father's will was the cause of this coming. But Christ as God has numerically the same will as the Father. Therefore *I am not come of myself* is not to be taken of Christ according to the divine nature, except in this sense: I am not come of myself, that is, I received from the Father the will and power by which I came into the world, taking human nature. Nonetheless Christ as God came by his own will and power; nay, he sent himself, as man.

paras.t: Sed est verus qui misit me, hoc est Deus Pater, qui est substantialiter verus veritate essentiæ in se ipso, et verax in verbis atque operibus; quem vos nescitis. Certum est quod Judæi non sciebant Deum Patrem per speciem, sicut Beati in patria, nee per comprehensionem plenariam, quia sic non cognoscitur Deus nisi ab intellectu infinite virtutis et capacitatis, videlicet a se ipso dumtaxat. Sed quæstio est, an sciebant eum per fidem. Et respondendum, quod non omnes Judæi habuerunt explicitam fidem de superbenedicta Trinitate: ideireo nee Patrem noverunt per fidem explicite. Noverunt tamen eum secundum esse absolutum, in quantum est Deus, per fidem, vel etiam per naturalem rationem. Si vero loquamur de notitia formata, non informi, sic mali Judæi non noverant eum, sicut nee ceteri impii, quantumcumque subtiles et eruditi. Qui enim se dicit nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est.
paras.en: [[7:28|but he that sent me is true, whom you know not|sed est verus qui misit me, quem vos nescitis]], that is, God the Father, who is substantially true with the truth of essence in himself, and truthful in words and works. It is certain that the Jews did not know God the Father by sight, as the Blessed in the fatherland do, nor by full comprehension, since God is not known so except by an intellect of infinite power and capacity, namely by himself alone. But the question is whether they knew him by faith. The answer is that not all the Jews had explicit faith in the superblessed Trinity: so neither did they know the Father explicitly by faith. Yet they knew him in his absolute being, in so far as he is God, by faith, or even by natural reason. But if we speak of formed knowledge, not unformed [that is, knowledge given life by charity], then the wicked Jews did not know him, as neither do the other impious, however subtle and learned. For [[1 John 2:4|He who saith that he knoweth him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar|Qui enim se dicit nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est]] [Denis: “he who saith that he knoweth God …”].

paras.t: Ego autem scio eum: quia ut Deus, comprehendo eum plenarie; secundum naturam vero assumptam, vidi eum per speciem ab incarnationis principio, clariusque quam aliquis Beatorum. Et si dixero quia non scio eum, ero similis vobis mendax: quod impossibile est, quum Veritas non possit mentiri, nec Creator creaturis in vitiis conformari. Sed scio eum scientia increata seu comprehensiva, et creata vel fruitiva, qua ab ipso sum, hoc est, ab eo accepi esse, et idem numero, non diversum, per generationem æternam; et ipse me misit, per incarnationis mysterium, hoc est, me incarnari, hominibus apparere mundumque salvare constituit. Scientia autem comprehensionis perfectæ competit Filio, ratione generationis divinæ. Scientia vero infusa, fruitiva, et in genere notitia creatæ summe perfecta, convenit Christo ratione missionis præfatæ. Quoniam enim missus est ad salvandum genus humanum, data est ei omnimoda plenitudo gratiæ atque scientiæ inditæ.
paras.en: [[7:29|I know him|Ego autem scio eum]]: since as God I comprehend him fully; but according to the nature assumed I have seen him by sight from the beginning of the incarnation, and more clearly than any of the Blessed. [[John 8:55|And if I shall say that I know him not, I shall be like to you, a liar|Et si dixero quia non scio eum, ero similis vobis mendax]]: which is impossible, since the Truth cannot lie[[Tit 1:2||]], nor the Creator be conformed to creatures in vices. But I know him with uncreated or comprehensive knowledge, and with created or fruitive knowledge [that is, the knowledge of the blessed who enjoy God], [[7:29|because I am from him|quia ab ipso sum]], that is, I have received being from him, numerically the same, not different, by eternal generation; [[7:29|and he hath sent me|et ipse me misit]], by the mystery of the incarnation, that is, he appointed that I should be made flesh, appear to men and save the world. The knowledge of perfect comprehension belongs to the Son by reason of the divine generation; but infused and fruitive knowledge, the most perfect in the class of created knowledge, belongs to Christ by reason of the said sending. For since he was sent to save the human race, there was given to him every fullness of grace and of infused knowledge.

paras.t: Quærebant ergo principes et fautores eorum eum apprehendere, hoc est capere ad occidendum, non amplecti ad perfruendum, de qua apprehensione loquitur Sponsa in Canticis: Quis mihi det te fratrem meum, ut inveniam te foris, et deosculer ac apprehendam te? Nos quoque, quia non possumus Jesum comprehendere, studeamus saltem apprehendere eum, hoc est per fidem et caritatem attingere eum, eique intime, quantum fieri potest, uniri. Cur voluerunt apprehendere eum? Primo, quia tam dure ac juste corripuit eos; secundo, quia tam magna asseruit de se ipso
paras.en: [[7:30|They sought therefore to apprehend him|Quærebant ergo eum apprehendere]], the rulers and their supporters, that is, to seize him in order to kill him, not to embrace him in order to enjoy him: of which apprehending the Bride speaks in the Canticle: [[Cant 8:1|Who shall give thee to me for my brother, sucking the breasts of my mother, that I may find thee without, and kiss thee|Quis mihi det te fratrem meum, ut inveniam te foris, et deosculer]] [Denis: “… that I may find thee without, and kiss thee, and lay hold of thee”]. Let us too, since we cannot comprehend Jesus, at least be eager to apprehend him, that is, to reach him by faith and charity, and to be united to him inwardly as far as may be. Why did they want to seize him? First, because he rebuked them so hard and so justly; second, because he asserted such great things of himself.

paras.t: Et nemo misit in illum manus violentas, quia nondum venerat hora ejus, hoc est tempus suæ passionis, in quo mori decrevit, non antea nec postea. Hoc quoc nondum venit hora ejus, fuit signum non causa efficiens quod non capiebatur. Divina vero voluntas atque potentia, erat causa efficiens quod captus non fuit, quia refrenavit malitiam Judæorum, non permittens eam in actum procedere. — Preterea, quia in Evangelio sæpius legitur, Nondum venit hora ejus, vel aliquid simile, quidam hæreticorum dicere ausi sunt, quod Jesus natus est sub certo fato, vel constellatione, cujus virtute fecit quæ fecit. Sed quam falsum sit hoc, non oportet probare, quum certum sit ipsum supernaturaliter esse conceptum ac natum. h
paras.en: [[7:30|and no man laid hands on him|Et nemo misit in illum manus]], violent hands, [[7:30|because his hour was not yet come|quia nondum venerat hora ejus]], that is, the time of his passion, in which he had decreed to die, not before nor after. That his hour had not yet come was a sign, not the efficient cause, of his not being seized. The divine will and power was the efficient cause of his not being taken, since it held back the malice of the Jews, not allowing it to go forth into act. Further, because in the Gospel it is often read, *His hour was not yet come*, or something like it[[John 2:4||]][[John 8:20||]][[John 12:23||]][[John 13:1||]][[John 17:1||]][[Matt 26:45||]][[Mark 14:41||]][[Luke 22:53||]], some heretics dared to say that Jesus was born under a certain fate or constellation, by whose power he did what he did. But how false this is there is no need to prove, since it is certain that he was conceived and born supernaturally.

paras.t: De turba autem multi crediderunt in eum, quod esset Messias, et dicebant: Christus quum venerit, numquid plura signa faciet, quam quæ hic facit ? Ex quo hi qui ita dixerunt, erant credentes in Jesum, videtur sic exponendum: Christus quum venerit, hoc est, si ponatur, secundum aliorum æstimationem, quod Christus nondum advenit, tamen quum et si venerit, prout illi exspectant, non faciet plura miracula quam efficit iste: ideo est credendum quod sit Christus, in cujus adventu dixerunt Prophete multa signa esse fienda. Unde habetur apud Isaiam: Ecce Deus vester veniet, et salvabit vos: tunc aperientur oculi cæcorum, et aures surdorum patebunt; tune saliet sicut cervus claudus, et aperta erit lingua mutorum. Nullus quippe ante adventum Christi tanta fecit miracula sicut Christus, et omnes qui post eum fecerunt vera miracula, non nisi in nomine ejus ea fecerunt. Imo, qui scire desiderat quam innumerabilia, præclara et gloriosa prodigia operatus est Christus, aliorum trium Evangelistarum evangelia legat. Verum, quoniam fides istorum non fuit multum perfecta, ideireo quod aiunt, Christus quum venerit, numquid plura signa faciet? intelligi potest per modum cujusdam inquisitionis. Quantitas enim miraculorum fiendorum a Christo in ejus adventu, non fuit in Scripturis determinata: ideo inquirebant inter se, anne plura signa fierent in Christi adventu, quam quæ viderunt a Jesu produci.
paras.en: [[7:31|But of the people many believed in him|De turba autem multi crediderunt in eum]], that he was the Messias, [[7:31|and said: When the Christ cometh, shall he do more miracles than this man doth|et dicebant: Christus quum venerit, numquid plura signa faciet, quam quæ hic facit]]? Since those who said this were believers in Jesus, it seems it should be explained thus: *When the Christ cometh*, that is, if it be supposed, according to the opinion of others, that the Christ has not yet come, yet when and if he shall come, as they expect, he will not do more miracles than this man does: so it is to be believed that he is the Christ, at whose coming the Prophets said many signs would be done. Hence it is had in Isaias: [[Is 35:4|behold your God will bring the revenge of recompense: God himself will come and will save you|ecce Deus vester ultionem adducet retributionis; Deus ipse veniet, et salvabit vos]]; [[Is 35:5|Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped|tunc aperientur oculi cæcorum, et aures surdorum patebunt]]; [[Is 35:6|Then shall the lame man leap as a hart, and the tongue of the dumb shall be free|tunc saliet sicut cervus claudus, et aperta erit lingua mutorum]]. For no one before the coming of Christ did such miracles as Christ, and all who after him did true miracles did them only in his name. Nay, whoever wishes to know how countless, splendid and glorious were the wonders Christ worked, let him read the gospels of the other three Evangelists. But since the faith of these men was not very perfect, what they say, *When the Christ cometh, shall he do more miracles?* can be understood by way of a certain inquiry. For the number of miracles to be done by Christ at his coming was not fixed in the Scriptures: so they asked among themselves whether more signs would be done at the coming of the Christ than those they had seen worked by Jesus.

paras.t: Audierunt Pharisæi, præcipui æmuli Christi, turbam credentium murmurantem, hoc est, suppressa voce dicentem, de illo hæc bona. Non enim audebant palam confiteri magnificentiam Jesu, timore Pharisæorum, Scribarum atque pontificum.
paras.en: [[7:32|The Pharisees heard|Audierunt Pharisæi]], Christ's chief rivals, [[7:32|the people murmuring these things concerning him|turbam murmurantem de illo hæc]] [Denis: “the believing people murmuring”], that is, saying with lowered voice these good things of him. For they did not dare to confess openly the greatness of Jesus, for fear of the Pharisees, Scribes and high priests.

7.title: Prosecutio expositionis hujus capituli septimi, ab illo loco quo dicitur: Et miserunt principes et Pharisæi ministros, ut apprehenderent eum.
7.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this seventh chapter, from the place where it is said: “And the rulers and Pharisees sent ministers to apprehend him.”

paras.t: Et miserunt principes et Pharisæi ministros, ut apprehenderent eum. Pharisæi livore contra Christum accensi ac tabefacti, audito quod turba confiterentur glorificarentque Jesum, asserendo quod esset Christus, et plurima faceret signa, timuerunt quod reciperent Jesum pro rege Messia. Idcirco collocuti sunt cum principibus sacerdotum, vel principalioribus Judæorum, de occisione Christi; et inito pacto, miserunt ministros, ut caperent Jesum. Aliqui dicunt, quod personaliter hoc facere non audebant, timore turbæ credentis, sed miserunt legatos viros periculis se tradentes, et quod legati isti fuerunt gentiles. Verum ex consequentibus magis apparet, moxque patebit, quod fuerunt Judi..
paras.en: [[7:32|and the rulers and Pharisees sent ministers to apprehend him|Et miserunt principes et Pharisæi ministros, ut apprehenderent eum]]. The Pharisees, kindled and consumed with envy against Christ, on hearing that the crowd was confessing and glorifying Jesus, asserting that he was the Christ and did very many signs, feared that they would receive Jesus as king Messias. Therefore they conferred with the chief priests, or the chief men of the Jews, about killing Christ; and having made an agreement, they sent ministers to seize Jesus. Some say that they did not dare to do this in person, for fear of the believing crowd, but sent envoys, men who would hand themselves over to dangers, and that these envoys were Gentiles. But from what follows it appears rather, and will soon be plain, that they were Jews.

paras.t: Dixit ergo eis, videlicet ministris ad se capiendum missis, Jesus: Adhuc modicum tempus vobiscum sum, hoc est, non diu ero, nec conversabor sensibiliter inter vos, et vado, hoc est, tempore hoc pauco expleto, ibo per passionem, resurrectionem et ascensionem, ad eum qui me misit, hoc est ad Patrem cœlestem, ut sedeam ad dexteram ejus. Tanquam diceret: Jam nunc non apprehendar a vobis, quia non volo, eo quod tempus meum nondum advenerit. Sed adhuc parumper ambulabo in populo, ad docendum eum, et ad complenda opera quæ Pater dedit mihi ut faciam ea: quo facto, facietis me permittente, quod nunc facere cupitis, sed non potestis me prohibente.
paras.en: [[7:33|Jesus therefore said to them|Dixit ergo eis Jesus]], namely to the ministers sent to seize him: [[7:33|Yet a little while I am with you|Adhuc modicum tempus vobiscum sum]], that is, I shall not be long, nor dwell visibly among you, [[7:33|and then I go|et vado]], that is, when this short time is finished, I shall go by the passion, resurrection and ascension, [[7:33|to him that sent me|ad eum qui me misit]], that is, to the heavenly Father, to sit at his right hand. As though he said: Even now I shall not be seized by you, because I do not will it, since my time has not yet come. But for a little while yet I shall walk among the people, to teach them, and to fulfil [[John 5:36|the works which the Father hath given me to perfect|opera quæ Pater dedit mihi ut faciam ea]] [Denis: “to fulfil the works which the Father gave me to do”][[John 9:4||]]: when this is done, you shall do, with my permission, what you now desire to do, but cannot, since I prevent it.

paras.t: Hæc omnia, utpote modicum manere in mundo, ire ad Patrem et capi, conveniunt Christo secundum naturam assumptam. Nempe secundum divinitatem manet æternaliter in Patre, non recedens neque revertens ad eum, et totum mundum invariabiliter implet, permanens ubique et in omnibus, per essentiam, præsentiam atque potentiam.
paras.en: All these things, namely to stay a little while in the world, to go to the Father and to be seized, belong to Christ according to the nature assumed. For according to his divinity he remains eternally in the Father, neither going away from him nor returning to him, and he fills the whole world unchangeably, abiding everywhere and in all things by essence, presence and power.

paras.t: Quæretis me, et non invenietis. Hoc a diversis, variis modis exponitur. Primo sic: Quæretis me post resurrectionem, hoc est, ad me convertemini per fidem, in die Pentecostes, vel postea, quando videritis per Apostolos tanta mirabilia fieri in nomine meo. Unde in Actibus Apostolorum habetur: Compuncti sunt corde, et dixerunt: Quid faciemus, viri fratres? Juxta hunc sensum infra loquitur Christus: Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum. Et non invenietis me, præsentia corporali atque sensibili, sicut modo. — Secundo sic: Quæretis me, hoc est, auxilium meum implorabitis; et non invenietis me ad libitum vestrum, tempore destructionis Jerusalem a Romanis. Tunc enim, ut dicitur, multi Judæorum noverunt se vastari a Tito propter occisionem Christi, et tunc Christum habere liberatorem optabant, sed non obtinuerunt. Ista expositio modici est valoris, quum sit incerta. — Beda vero exponit sic, quod quæsierunt Jesum post resurrectionem, quando viderunt tot millia converti ad Christum; sed non invenerunt eum spiritualiter, quoniam magnitudinem sui peccati quo Christum occiderunt, pensantes, non vere pœnituerunt, sed barathrum desperationis inciderunt. — Videtur autem sic convenienter posse exponi: Quæretis me, ante passionem, et post hanc vicem, ad capiendum; et non invenietis me corporaliter, usque ad tempus. Ut enim infra habetur: Principes dederunt præceptum, ut si quis sciret ubinam esset Jesus, indicaret. Ex quo elicitur, quod sæpe quæsierunt eum ad capiendum, sed non invenerunt.
paras.en: [[7:34|You shall seek me and shall not find me|Quæretis me, et non invenietis]]. This is explained by different men in various ways. First thus: You shall seek me after the resurrection, that is, you shall turn to me by faith, on the day of Pentecost or afterwards, when you see such wonders done by the Apostles in my name. Hence in the Acts of the Apostles it is had: [[Acts 2:37|they had compunction in their heart and said to Peter and to the rest of the apostles: What shall we do, men and brethren?|Compuncti sunt corde, et dixerunt : Quid faciemus, viri fratres]]? In this sense Christ says below: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]]. *And you shall not find me*, by bodily and visible presence, as now. Second thus: *You shall seek me*, that is, you shall implore my help; *and shall not find me* at your pleasure, at the time of the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans. For then, it is said, many of the Jews knew that they were laid waste by Titus because of the slaying of Christ, and then they wished to have Christ as deliverer, but did not obtain it. This explanation is of little worth, since it is uncertain. But Bede explains thus: that they sought Jesus after the resurrection, when they saw so many thousands converted to Christ; but they did not find him spiritually, since, weighing the greatness of their sin in killing Christ, they did not truly repent, but fell into the abyss of despair. But it seems it can fittingly be explained thus: *You shall seek me*, before the passion, and after this time, to seize me; *and shall not find me* bodily, until the time. For as is had below: [[John 11:56|And the chief priests and Pharisees had given a commandment that, if any man knew where he was, he should tell|Principes dederunt præceptum, ut si quis sciret ubi … esset … indicaret]] [the margin prints Joann. xi, 56; the words are in John 11:57]. From which it is gathered that they often sought him to seize him, but did not find him.

paras.t: Et ubi ego sum nunc secundum divinitatem, videlicet in summo cœlo, in sinu Patris; vel, Ubi sum, hoc est, ubi post passionem mox ibo et ero, videlicet ad dexteram Dei; vos non potestis venire, propter peccata vestra, vel propria potestate; tamen per gratiam meam, si panitentiam veram egeritis, venietis illuc, et eritis mecum.
paras.en: [[7:34|and where I am|Et ubi ego sum]] now according to the divinity, namely in the highest heaven, [[John 1:18|in the bosom of the Father|in sinu Patris]]; or, *where I am*, that is, where after the passion I shall soon go and be, namely at the right hand of God; [[7:34|thither you cannot come|vos non potestis venire]], because of your sins, or by your own power; yet by my grace, if you do true penance, you shall come there and be with me.

paras.t: Dixerunt ergo Judæi, hoc est ministri prædicti, et alii forte qui aderant, ad semetipsos, id est unus ad alium, non intelligentes verba prædicta, sed inter se conquirentes quomodo essent intelligenda: Quo hic iturus est, quia non inveniemus eum? Christus aperte dixit, Vado […] intellexerunt quod prædixit se iturum ad Patrem cœlestem. Numquid in dispersionem gentium iturus est, hoc est ad gentes ubique dispersas, et per sectas ac loca divisas? Sic enim contemptibiliter loquebantur de gentilibus, quos multum spernebant, propter peccata eorum, et electionem suam ac patrum suorum. Et docturus gentes, videlicet corporaliter recessurus a Judæa, et congregaturus multos discipulos ex gentibus. Quis est, hoc est, quomodo intelligendus est, hic sermo quem dixit: Quæretis me, et non […] potestis venire? Hoc forsitan repetebant, ad innuendum quod secundum eorum æstimationem, verba Christi non erant intelligenda de recessu ejus ad gentes, quoniam per verbum de præsenti dixit: Ubi ego sum, vos non potestis venire. Ignorabant itaque quid notavit per hoc.
paras.en: [[7:35|The Jews therefore said among themselves|Dixerunt ergo Judæi ad semetipsos]], that is, the ministers aforesaid, and perhaps others who were present, *among themselves*, that is, one to another, not understanding the words spoken, but asking among themselves how they were to be understood: [[7:35|Whither will he go, that we shall not find him|Quo hic iturus est, quia non inveniemus eum]]? Christ said openly, *I go* […] [a line or two of the scan is unreadable here; the sense seems to be that they did not] understand that he foretold that he would go to the heavenly Father. [[7:35|Will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles|Numquid in dispersionem gentium iturus est]], that is, to the Gentiles scattered everywhere, and divided by sects and places? For so they spoke contemptuously of the Gentiles, whom they greatly despised because of their sins, and because of their own election and that of their fathers. [[7:35|and teach the Gentiles|Et docturus gentes]], namely going away from Judea in body, and gathering many disciples from among the Gentiles. [[7:36|What is this saying that he hath said|quis est hic sermo, quem dixit]], that is, how is it to be understood: [[7:36|You shall seek me and shall not find me|Quæretis me, et non]] […] [[7:36|you cannot come|potestis venire]]? Perhaps they repeated this to suggest that, in their opinion, Christ's words were not to be understood of his going away to the Gentiles, since he said in the present tense, *Where I am, you cannot come*. So they did not know what he meant by it.

paras.t: In novissimo autem die magno, hoc est multum celebri, festivitatis Tabernaculorum durantis septem diebus, ut dictum est. Primus enim et ultimus dies hujus festi fuerant celebriores. Stabat Jesus, tanquam confirmatus in bono, erectus in omni virtute, et paratus ferre subsidium cunctis ad ipsum confugientibus. Potestque per suam stationem, divinitatis ipsius invariabilitas designari. Et clamabat, affectuose, eloquentissime ac secure prædicando, dicens: Si quis sitit, hoc est, spiritualia bona desiderat, gratiam cupit, fluenta doctrinæ, aquam sapientiæ appetit. De qua siti scriptum est in Ecclesiastico: Animæ vestræ sitiunt vehementer. Apud Isaiam quoque ait: Omnes sitientes, venite ad aquas. Veniat ad me: non corporis gressu dumtaxat, sed et mentis humili præparatione; faciendo quod in se est; fide quoque non hæsitanti, et oratione constanti. Unde scriptum est in Jacobo: Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et dabitur ei; postulet autem in fide, nihil hæsitans. Ideo subditur: et bibat, hoc est, […] reficiatur et refrigeretur a me. Omnis quippe qui petit, accipit. Propter quod in Apocalypsi dicitur: Qui sitit, veniat; et qui vult, accipiat aquam vitæ gratis. Quicumque ergo mæstificatus indiget consolatione, qui fatigatus indiget confortatione, qui tribulatus indiget subventione, recurrat integra fide ac humili mente ad Christum, non cessans sperare in eo, et procul dubio auxilium sortietur. Ipse enim verissime ait: Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos.
paras.en: [[7:37|And on the last, and great day of the festivity|In novissimo autem die magno festivitatis]], *great*, that is, very solemn, of the feast of Tabernacles lasting seven days, as has been said[[Lev 23:36||]][[Lev 23:39||]]. For the first and the last days of this feast were the more solemn[[Num 29:12||]][[Num 29:35||]]. [[7:37|Jesus stood|Stabat Jesus]], as one confirmed in good, upright in every virtue, and ready to bring help to all who fled to him. And by his standing the unchangeableness of his divinity can be signified. [[7:37|and cried|Et clamabat]], preaching with affection, most eloquently and fearlessly, [[7:37|saying: If any man thirst|dicens: Si quis sitit]], that is, desires spiritual goods, longs for grace, seeks the streams of doctrine, the water of wisdom. Of which thirst it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 51:32|your souls are exceeding thirsty|Animæ vestræ sitiunt vehementer]]. In Isaias too he says: [[Is 55:1|All you that thirst, come to the waters|Omnes sitientes, venite ad aquas]]. [[7:37|let him come to me|Veniat ad me]]: not by the step of the body only, but also by humble preparation of the mind; by doing what is in him; by faith too that does not waver, and by constant prayer. Hence it is written in James: [[Jas 1:5|But if any of you want wisdom, let him ask of God who giveth to all men abundantly and upbraideth not. And it shall be given him|Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et dabitur ei]]; [[Jas 1:6|But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering|postulet autem in fide, nihil hæsitans]]. So there is added: [[7:37|and drink|et bibat]], that is, […] [a line is unreadable here] be refreshed and cooled by me. [[Matt 7:8|For every one that asketh, receiveth|Omnis quippe qui petit, accipit]]. For which reason it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:17|And he that thirsteth, let him come. And he that will, let him take the water of life, freely|Qui sitit, veniat; et qui vult, accipiat aquam vitæ gratis]]. Whoever, then, saddened, needs consolation, wearied, needs strengthening, troubled, needs help, let him run back to Christ with whole faith and humble mind, not ceasing to hope in him, and without doubt he shall obtain help. For he says most truly: [[Matt 11:28|Come to me all you that labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you|Venite ad me, omnes qui laboratis et onerati estis, et ego reficiam vos]].

paras.t: Qui credit in me fide formata ac plena, […] his qui suo magisterio stabiliter adhærebant usque ad passionem et Pentecosten, sicut patebit.
paras.en: [[7:38|He that believeth in me|Qui credit in me]] with formed and full faith [that is, faith given life by charity], […] [two lines of the scan are unreadable here] to those who clung steadfastly to his teaching until the passion and Pentecost, as will appear.

paras.t: Sicut dicit Scriptura, in Proverbiis, quantum ad sensum, non quantum ad formam verborum. Ista allegatio refertur ad sequentia: Flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ. Quomodo autem intelligendum sit hoc, Evangelista subjecit, nec debemus anticipare expositionem tanti interpretis. Hoc autem dixit de Spiritu quem accepturi erant credentes in eum. Est igitur sensus: Flumina aqua viva, id est dona Spiritus Sancti, fluent, doctrinæ cœlestis et gratiæ copiose ac multiformis, emanabunt de corde ipsius ad alios, vel de habitu et interiori actu. ad opera exteriora. Itaque per flumina designantur dona Spiritus Sancti; per aquam vivam, ipse Spiritus Sanctus (de quo dictum est: Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo, fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam); per ventrem vero, mens ipsa interna, in qua habitat Spiritus Sanctus per dona sua. De hujusmodi etenim ventre, ait Salomon in Proverbiis: Fili, suscipe sapientiam, qua pulchra tibi erit quum servaveris eam in ventre tuo; et Isaias, Venter (inquit) meus quasi cithara ad Moab sonabit. Ex mentibus ergo Apostolorum et aliorum qui cum eis in die Pentecostes Spiritum Sanctum receperunt, fluxerunt prædicta flumina per evangelicam prædicationem ad totum mundum, quoniam gratiam sibi divinitus communicatam, in alios administraverunt, sicut optimi dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei.
paras.en: [[7:38|as the scripture saith|Sicut dicit Scriptura]], in Proverbs[[Prov 5:15||]], as to the sense, not as to the form of the words. This citation refers to what follows: [[7:38|Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water|Flumina de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ]]. How this is to be understood the Evangelist adds, and we must not anticipate the explanation of so great an interpreter. [[7:39|Now this he said of the Spirit which they should receive who believed in him|Hoc autem dixit de Spiritu quem accepturi erant credentes in eum]]. The sense, then, is: *rivers of living water*, that is, the gifts of the Holy Ghost, *shall flow*, of heavenly doctrine and grace, abundant and manifold, from his heart to others, or from habit and inward act to outward works. So by the rivers are signified the gifts of the Holy Ghost; by the living water, the Holy Ghost himself (of whom it was said: [[John 4:13|but he that shall drink of the water that I will give him|Qui biberit ex aqua quam ego dabo]], [[John 4:14|shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into life everlasting|fiet in eo fons aquæ salientis in vitam æternam]]); and by the belly, the inner mind itself, in which the Holy Ghost dwells by his gifts. For of such a belly Solomon says in Proverbs: [[Prov 22:18|Which shall be beautiful for thee, if thou keep it in thy bowels|quæ pulchra tibi erit quum servaveris eam in ventre tuo]] [Denis: “My son, receive wisdom, which shall be beautiful for thee …”]; and Isaias, [[Is 16:11|my bowels shall sound like a harp for Moab|Venter (inquit) meus quasi cithara ad Moab sonabit]]. From the minds, then, of the Apostles and of the others who with them received the Holy Ghost on the day of Pentecost, the said rivers flowed through the preaching of the Gospel to the whole world, since they ministered to others the grace divinely communicated to them, [[1 Pet 4:10|as good stewards of the manifold grace of God|sicut optimi dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei]].

paras.t: Preterea, quod prædicta intelligenda sint de effusione Spiritus Sancti in signo visibili, super Apostolos et cum eis consistentes in die Pentecostes, pandit Evangelista, subdendo: Nondum enim, quando Christus hac prædicavit, erat Spiritus Sanctus datus fidelibus, scilicet in tanta plenitudine tamque evidenter ut post resurrectionem, quando Christus dedit Spiritum Sanctum in signo visibili: primo, per insufflationem, ante ascensionem; secundo, per ignearum apparitionem linguarum, in die Pentecostes. Fuit autem Spiritus Sanctus datus a principio mundi universis electis, quoniam nullus sine gratia ejus, sine donis ejus, sine fide et caritate salvatus est. Et sancti Patriarchæ atque Prophete in magna copia gratiam Spiritus Sancti sortiti sunt, quemadmodum Petrus dicit: Non voluntate humana allata est aliquando prophetia; sed Spiritu Sancto inspirati, locuti sunt sancti Dei homines. Nihilo minus Apostoli primitias Spiritus Sancti receperunt, quia pre ceteris Sanctis antiquis, exuberantius evidentiusque repleti sunt Spiritu Sancto, et de mysteriis Christi excellentissime illustrati.
paras.en: Further, that what has been said is to be understood of the outpouring of the Holy Ghost in a visible sign upon the Apostles and those with them on the day of Pentecost, the Evangelist makes plain by adding: [[7:39|for as yet the Spirit was not given|Nondum enim … erat Spiritus … datus]], when Christ preached these things, the Holy Ghost was not yet given to the faithful, namely in such fullness and so evidently as after the resurrection, when Christ gave the Holy Ghost in a visible sign: first, by breathing on them, before the ascension[[John 20:22||]]; second, by the appearing of fiery tongues, on the day of Pentecost[[Acts 2:3||]]. But the Holy Ghost was given from the beginning of the world to all the elect, since no one has been saved without his grace, without his gifts, without faith and charity. And the holy Patriarchs and Prophets received the grace of the Holy Ghost in great abundance, as Peter says: [[2 Pet 1:21|For prophecy came not by the will of man at any time: but the holy men of God spoke, inspired by the Holy Ghost|Non voluntate humana allata est aliquando prophetia; sed Spiritu Sancto inspirati, locuti sunt sancti Dei homines]]. Nonetheless the Apostles received [[Rom 8:23|the firstfruits of the Spirit|primitias Spiritus]], since beyond the other Saints of old they were filled more abundantly and more evidently with the Holy Ghost, and most excellently enlightened about the mysteries of Christ.

paras.t: Porro, quod subditur advertendum est diligenter. Causam enim cur Spiritus Sanctus nondum datus fuit hoc modo assignans, adjunxit: quia Jesus nondum fuerat glorificatus, id est a morte resuscitatus, atque in corpore gloriosus effectus. In anima enim fuit glorificatus a principio incarnationis, præsertim quantum ad partem animæ superioris.
paras.en: Further, what is added is to be noted carefully. For, giving the cause why the Holy Ghost had not yet been given in this way, he added: [[7:39|because Jesus was not yet glorified|quia Jesus nondum fuerat glorificatus]], that is, raised from death and made glorious in body. For in soul he was glorified from the beginning of the incarnation, above all as to the higher part of the soul.

paras.t: Cur ergo Spiritus Sanctus datus non est plene et in signo visibili ante Christi resurrectionem? Respondet Chrysostomus, quoniam talis communicatio non debuit fieri, nisi per Christi passionem humano genere reconciliato. Augustinus vero dicit quod ideo, ut per tam copiosam Spiritus Sancti receptionem certissime suspiremus ad patriam, ad futuram resurrectionem, ad beatam immortalitatem. Cujus Christus in se ipso monstravit exemplum, apparendo discipulis in vero corpore veraciter glorificato. Sed litteralis (ut arbitror) ratio est, quoniam ad hoc datus est Spiritus Sanctus tam copiose in signo visibili, ut Apostoli omni notitia Scripturarum omnique usu linguarum impleti, Christi Evangelium ubique et constantissime prædicarent; et item, ut per igneas linguas figuraretur quod igneam legem essent prædicaturi, omniumque linguarum nationes docturi. Hæc autem agenda non erant nisi post resurrectionem: nam ante resurrectionem dictum est eis a Christo, In viam gentium ne abieritis. Christus etiam noluit suam majestatem tam evidenter ostendere ante passionem ut postea, ne sua passio impediretur. Potest quoque alia ratio addi, quia non decuit membra tanta gratia decorari, nisi capite totaliter glorificato, omnique gratia accidentalis præmii adornato.
paras.en: Why, then, was the Holy Ghost not given fully and in a visible sign before Christ's resurrection? Chrysostom answers: because such a communication ought not to be made except when the human race had been reconciled through Christ's passion. But Augustine says it was so that through so abundant a receiving of the Holy Ghost we might sigh most surely for the fatherland, for the future resurrection, for blessed immortality. Of which Christ showed in himself an example, by appearing to the disciples in a true body truly glorified[[Acts 1:3||]]. But the literal reason (as I judge) is that the Holy Ghost was given so abundantly in a visible sign so that the Apostles, filled with all knowledge of the Scriptures and all use of tongues, might preach Christ's Gospel everywhere and most steadfastly; and also so that by the fiery tongues it might be figured that they were to preach a fiery law, and teach the nations of all tongues. And these things were not to be done until after the resurrection: for before the resurrection Christ said to them, [[Matt 10:5|Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles|In viam gentium ne abieritis]]. Christ also did not will to show his majesty so evidently before the passion as afterwards, lest his passion be hindered. Another reason too can be added: that it was not fitting for the members to be adorned with such grace until the head had been wholly glorified and adorned with all the grace of accidental reward.

paras.t: Ex illa ergo turba, quum audissent hos sermones ejus, qui erant pulcherrimi atque vehementer notabiles, dicebant quidam: Hic est vere propheta. Secundum Lyram, per prophetam intellexerunt Prophetam illum antonomastice dictum, de quo Moyses scripsit: Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus de fratribus vestris tanquam me. Sed quum hoc dictum sit de Christo ad litteram, et Evangelista nunc subdat, Alii dicebant, Hic est Christus, sequitur quod illi per prophetam, non intellexerunt Christum Dominum Prophetarum, sed prophetam simpliciter, quem vocabant vere prophetam, id est divinitus illuminatum. Qui autem dixerunt, Hic est Christus, melius consideraverunt verba et opera Jesu. Qui vero dixerunt, Hic est vere propheta, erraverunt, si prophetam sumpserunt in specie, distinguendo Prophetam contra Dominum Prophetarum Christum Jesum, qui fuit propheta et comprehensor, Salvator et finis Prophetarum.
paras.en: [[7:40|Of that multitude therefore, when they had heard these words of his|Ex illa ergo turba, quum audissent hos sermones ejus]], which were most beautiful and exceedingly remarkable, [[7:40|some said: This is the prophet indeed|dicebant quidam: Hic est vere propheta]]. According to Lyra, by *the prophet* they understood that Prophet called so by antonomasia, of whom Moses wrote: [[Acts 3:22|A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me|Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus de fratribus vestris tanquam me]][[Deut 18:15||]]. But since this was said of Christ literally, and the Evangelist now adds, [[7:41|Others said: This is the Christ|Alii dicebant: Hic est Christus]], it follows that by *the prophet* they did not understand Christ the Lord of the Prophets, but simply a prophet, whom they called truly a prophet, that is, divinely enlightened. Those who said *This is the Christ* considered the words and works of Jesus better. But those who said *This is the prophet indeed* erred, if they took *prophet* in the narrow sense, distinguishing the Prophet from the Lord of the Prophets, Christ Jesus, who was prophet and one who had attained [*comprehensor*], Saviour and end of the Prophets.

paras.t: Quidam autem increduli, volentes probare testimonio Scripturarum quod Jesus non esset Christus, dicebant: Numquid a Galilea venit Christus? quasi dicant: provincia Galilææ Christus non est descensurus, nasciturus, seu adventurus. Nonne Scriptura dicit, quia ex semine David et de Bethlehem castello, id est modica urbe; vel, Castello, id est domo, ubi erat, id est habitavit et ortus est, David, venit Christus? Christum nasciturum esse de semine David, prænuntiatum fuit in Psalmo: De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam; et apud Jeremiam, Suscitabo David germen justum; apud Isaiam quoque, Egredietur virga de radice Jesse, etc. Certum est enim quod Christus non descendit de stirpe Jesse nisi per David. Preterea, quod Christus nasceretur in Bethlehem, per Michæam prædictum erat. Et tu, Bethlehem Ephrata, ex te mihi egredietur qui sit dominator in Israel. Quoniam ergo noverant Jesum nutritum in Nazareth urbe Galilææ, putabant quod ibi natus fuisset, et per consequens non esset Christus.
paras.en: [[7:41|But some said|Quidam autem dicebant]], unbelievers, wishing to prove by the testimony of the Scriptures that Jesus was not the Christ: [[7:41|Doth the Christ come out of Galilee|Numquid a Galilæa venit Christus]]? as though they said: The Christ is not to come down, be born or arrive from the province of Galilee. [[7:42|Doth not the scripture say|Nonne Scriptura dicit]], that [[7:42|Christ cometh of the seed of David and from Bethlehem the town where David was|ex semine David, et de Bethlehem castello, ubi erat David, venit Christus]]? *the town*, that is, a small city; or *town*, that is, house; *where he was*, that is, dwelt and was born. That the Christ would be born of the seed of David was foretold in the Psalm: [[Ps 131:11|of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne|De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam]]; and in Jeremias, [[Jer 23:5|I will raise up to David a just branch|Suscitabo David germen justum]]; in Isaias also, [[Is 11:1|And there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse|Egredietur virga de radice Jesse]], etc. For it is certain that Christ did not descend from the stock of Jesse except through David. Further, that Christ would be born in Bethlehem had been foretold by Micheas: [[Mich 5:2|And thou Bethlehem Ephrata|Et tu, Bethlehem Ephrata]] … [[Mich 5:2|out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be the ruler in Israel|ex te mihi egredietur qui sit dominator in Israel]]. Since, then, they knew that Jesus was brought up in Nazareth, a city of Galilee, they thought he had been born there, and consequently was not the Christ.

paras.t: Dissensio itaque facta est in turba propter eum, diversis diversa sentientibus atque dicentibus. Quidam autem ex ipsis volebant apprehendere eum, putantes quod nec propheta nee Christus esset, sed seductor. Erant enim obstinati et pessimi, luminique rebelles. Sed nemo misit super illum manus, quia noluit Christus, et eorum pravitatem repressit.
paras.en: [[7:43|So there arose a dissension among the people because of him|Dissensio itaque facta est in turba propter eum]], divers men thinking and saying divers things. [[7:44|And some of them would have apprehended him|Quidam autem ex ipsis volebant apprehendere eum]], thinking that he was neither prophet nor Christ, but a seducer. For they were obstinate and most wicked, and rebels against the light[[Job 24:13||]]. [[7:44|but no man laid hands upon him|Sed nemo misit super illum manus]], since Christ did not will it, and held back their wickedness.

paras.t: Venerunt ergo ministri qui missi erant ut caperent Jesum, ad pontifices et Phariseos, a quibus fuerant missi, et dixerunt eis, id est ministris, illi: Quare non adduxistis eum captum et vinctum? Responderunt ministri: Nunquam sic locutus est homo, sicut hic loquitur: id est, tanta est sapientia atque facundia oris sui, tam prompte, ordinate et doctrinaliter loquitur, quod nemo ei similis fuit. Nec mirum, quum ipse sit unicum Dei Verbum, quod non laborat in verbo. Hinc ait Psalmista: Diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis. Et in Luca legitur: Omnes mirabantur in verbis gratiæ quæ procedebant de ore ejus.
