See how great a perversity and madness! For what consequence is there in: He goes where we cannot follow him, therefore he will kill himself? Nay, they could have followed one who killed himself, by inflicting a wicked death on themselves. For the passionate and envious interpret everything for the worse.

paras.t: Et dicebat eis: Vos deorsum estis, id est de massa originali peccato infecta, de semine libidinoso, de conversatione terrena, et infimis rebus inhæretis. Vel, Deorsum estis, id est ex diabolo nati, non per creationem vel susceptionem naturæ ab illo, sed per imitationem suæ malitiæ. Unde in prima Joannis Canonica dicitur: Qui peccat, ex diabolo est; et per Sapientem: Imitantur autem illum qui sunt ex parte illius. Ipse nempe est pater super omnes filios superbiæ. Ego de supernis sum, id est natus a Deo Patre, et per incarnationis mysterium descendi a summo cœlo; corpus quoque meum supernaturaliter a Spiritu Sancto formatum est ex purissimis Virginis sanctæ sanguinibus. Vos de mundo hoc estis, id est de numero hominum mundanorum, de generatione malorum, et pertinetis ad corpus diaboli. De quo mundo Jacobus dicit: Amicitia hujus mundi inimica est Deo; et Joannes, Mundus (inquit) totus in maligno positus est. Noverat enim Christus quod hi pertinebant ad vasa iræ, non ad numerum electorum, secundum quod infra testatur: Ego scio quos elegerim. Ego non sum de hoc mundo, id est, ad sæcularium hominum societatem non pertineo, nec aliquid mundanæ vanitatis aut pravitatis in me habeo. Denique Christus secundum quod Deus, non est de mundo, sumendo mundum pro toto universo creato, quum non sit pars ejus, sed conditor. Sed et secundum humanitatem Verbo unitam, non est de mundo, id est aliqua naturali virtute conceptus et genitus, sed de Spiritu Sancto. Ceteri quoque electi non sunt de mundo, ita quod ad mundanorum ac reproborum non pertinent sortem, secundum quod infra loquitur Christus: Quia de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus. 24
paras.en: [[8:23|And he said to them: You are from beneath|Et dicebat eis: Vos deorsum estis]], that is, from the mass infected with original sin, from lustful seed, from an earthly way of life, and you cling to the lowest things. Or, *you are from beneath*, that is, born of the devil, not by creation or the receiving of nature from him, but by imitation of his malice. Hence in the first Canonical Epistle of John it is said: [[1 John 3:8|He that committeth sin is of the devil|Qui peccat, ex diabolo est]]; and by the Wise Man: [[Wis 2:25|And they follow him that are of his side|Imitantur autem illum qui sunt ex parte illius]]. For he is [[Job 41:25|king over all the children of pride|pater super omnes filios superbiæ]] [Denis: “father over all the children of pride”]. [[8:23|I am from above|Ego de supernis sum]], that is, born of God the Father, and by the mystery of the incarnation I came down from the highest heaven; my body too was formed supernaturally by the Holy Ghost from the most pure blood of the holy Virgin. [[8:23|You are of this world|Vos de mundo hoc estis]], that is, of the number of worldly men, of the generation of the wicked, and you belong to the body of the devil. Of which world James says: [[Jas 4:4|the friendship of this world is the enemy of God|Amicitia hujus mundi inimica est Deo]]; and John, [[1 John 5:19|the whole world is seated in wickedness|Mundus (inquit) totus in maligno positus est]]. For Christ knew that these belonged to [[Rom 9:22|vessels of wrath|vasa iræ]], not to the number of the elect, according to what is testified below: [[John 13:18|I know whom I have chosen|Ego scio quos elegerim]]. [[8:23|I am not of this world|Ego non sum de hoc mundo]], that is, I do not belong to the company of worldly men, nor have I anything of worldly vanity or wickedness in me. Further, Christ as God is not of the world, taking the world for the whole created universe, since he is not part of it, but its maker. And according to the humanity united to the Word he is not of the world either, that is, conceived and begotten by any natural power, but of the Holy Ghost[[Matt 1:20||]]. The other elect too are not of the world, in that they do not belong to the lot of the worldly and the reprobate, according to what Christ says below: [[John 15:19|but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you|Quia de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus]].

paras.t: Diai ergo vobis, quia moriemini in peccatis vestris, id est, quia ad reprobos pertinetis, dixi quia in peccatis finaliter perseverabitis atque peribitis. Quod dictum est quantum ad certitudinem prædestinationis, per quam non aufertur libertas hominibus. Unde nei omnem spem eis auferret conditionalem, adjecit: Si enim non credideritis fide per dilectionem operante, quia ego sum qui verum plenumque esse habeo, id est Deus verus, cujus præcipuum ac proprium nomen est esse, vel qui est: qui olim dixi ad Moysen: Ego sum qui sum; hæc dices filiis Israel, Qui est, misit me ad vos. Deus namque est unum esse ideale ac separatum, in quo est omnis plenitudo, perfectio nobilitasque essendi. Moriemini in peccato vestro, quoniam sine fide impossibile est placere Deo. Vel sic: Si non credideritis quia ego sum quem me esse dico, videlicet Christus vobis promissus, moriemini in peccatis vestris; quemadmodum Moyses ait, Omnis qui non audierit Prophetam illum, exterminabitur de populo suo.
paras.en: [[8:24|Therefore I said to you, that you shall die in your sins|Dixi ergo vobis, quia moriemini in peccatis vestris]], that is, because you belong to the reprobate, I said that you will persevere in your sins to the end and perish. This was said as to the certainty of predestination, by which freedom is not taken from men. Hence, lest he take from them all conditional hope, he added: [[8:24|For if you believe not|Si enim non credideritis]], with [[Gal 5:6|faith that worketh by charity|fide per dilectionem operante]], [[8:24|that I am he|quia ego sum]], who have true and full being, that is, true God, whose chief and proper name is *Being*, or *He who is*: who once said to Moses: [[Ex 3:14|I AM WHO AM. He said: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: HE WHO IS, hath sent me to you|Ego sum qui sum ; hæc dices filiis Israel, Qui est, misit me ad vos]]. For God is one ideal and separate being, in which is all fullness, perfection and nobility of being. [[8:24|you shall die in your sin|moriemini in peccato vestro]], since [[Heb 11:6|without faith it is impossible to please God|sine fide impossibile est placere Deo]]. Or thus: If you do not believe that I am he whom I say I am, namely the Christ promised you, you shall die in your sins; as Moses says, [[Acts 3:23|And it shall be, that every soul which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people|Omnis qui non audierit Prophetam illum, exterminabitur de populo suo]] [Denis: “Every one who will not hear that Prophet shall be destroyed from his people”][[Deut 18:19||]].

paras.t: Dicebant ergo ei: Tu quis es, id est cujus auctoritatis, qualis et quantus, ut in te credamus? Non enim omnin spiritui est credendum. Et qui cito credit, levis est corde, falliturque frequenter. Dixit eis Jesus: Principium, qui et loquor vobis, id est, ego sum primum universorum principium secundum naturam divinam, tanquam Creator omnipotens, qui cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto sum unum principium, unus Creator, unusque finis omnium rerum. Qui loquor in Apocalypsi: Ego sum Alpha et Omega, primus et novissimus, principium et finis. Qui loquor vobis per humanitatem assumptam. Quamvis enim Pater sit principium Filii, Filius quoque principium Spiritus Sancti, sumendo principium personaliter; Pater tamen, Filius et Spiritus Sanctus sunt unum principium totius creaturæ, sumendo principium essentialiter seu absolute: quia in tribus Personis, est una natura, quæ est operationis origo, et una potentia, quæ elicit actum. His verbis ostendit Christus apertam suam veram divinitatem. Et quia ratione divinitatis competit Christo judiciaria potestas, ac judicare per auctoritatem; ratione vero assumptæ humanitatis, per sententiæ prolationem seu judiciariæ potestatis exsecutionem: ideo addit :
paras.en: [[8:25|They said therefore to him: Who art thou|Dicebant ergo ei: Tu quis es]], that is, of what authority, what sort and how great, that we should believe in you? For [[1 John 4:1|believe not every spirit|Non … omni spiritui … credendum]]. And [[Ecclus 19:4|He that is hasty to give credit, is light of heart|qui cito credit, levis est corde]], and is often deceived. [[8:25|Jesus said to them: The beginning, who also speak unto you|Dixit eis Jesus: Principium, qui et loquor vobis]], that is, I am the first beginning of all things according to the divine nature, as almighty Creator, who with the Father and the Holy Ghost am one beginning, one Creator, and one end of all things. Who say in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:8|I am Alpha and Omega|Ego sum Alpha et Omega]], [[Apoc 22:13|the first and the last, the beginning and the end|primus et novissimus, principium et finis]]. *Who speak unto you* through the humanity assumed. For though the Father is the beginning of the Son, and the Son the beginning of the Holy Ghost, taking *beginning* personally, yet the Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost are one beginning of the whole creation, taking *beginning* essentially or absolutely: since in the three Persons there is one nature, which is the origin of operation, and one power, which brings forth the act. By these words Christ shows openly his true divinity. And since by reason of the divinity judicial power belongs to Christ, and to judge with authority, but by reason of the assumed humanity, to judge by pronouncing sentence or carrying out judicial power, he therefore adds:

paras.t: Multa habeo de vobis loqui, opera vestra increpando et publicando, et judicare, vos ipsos reprobando, nisi conversi fueritis ad me. Hoc erit in die judicii, quando omnes stabunt ante tribunal Christi, qui tunc illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium, atque de omni verbo otioso exiget rationem, nil indiscussum relinquens. Verumtamen, an omnia ista fient vocali locutione, vel mentali dumtaxat, exstat in […] habeo de vobis judicare, insinuat quod judicium distulit usque ad secundum adventum, quia in primo venit salvare, non reprobare seu condemnare.
paras.en: [[8:26|Many things I have to speak|Multa habeo de vobis loqui]] of you, rebuking and making public your works, [[8:26|and to judge of you|et judicare]], reproving you yourselves, unless you are converted to me. This will be at the day of judgment, when [[Rom 14:10|we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ|omnes stabunt ante tribunal Christi]][[2 Cor 5:10||]], who then [[1 Cor 4:5|will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts|illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium]], and will exact an account [[Matt 12:36|every idle word|de omni verbo otioso]], leaving nothing undiscussed. But whether all these things will be done by spoken words or by mental ones only remains in […] [a line of the scan is unreadable here] *I have to judge of you* suggests that he put off the judgment until the second coming, since at the first he came to save, not to reprove or condemn[[John 3:17||]].

paras.t: Denique, quoniam paulo ante jam dixit, Ego non judico quemquam; nunc vero asseruit, Multa habeo de vobis judicare; ne Judæi objicerent, Verba tua sibi invicem contraria sunt et mendosa, subdidit: Sed qui me misit, videlicet Pater eternus, verax est in se ipso, tanquam essentialiter veritas exemplaris, prima ac pura, verax quoque in verbis et promissis; et ego quæ audivi ab eo, hoc est veritatem quam ab ipso accepi, hæc loquor in mundo, id est, hominibus prædico, idcirco non mentior. Audire autem magis proprie competit Christo secundum humanitatem quam divinitatem. Nam, ut homo, audivit a Patre, id est, ex interna Patris inspiratione, aure cordis percepit, advertit ac didicit quidquid scit. Est enim locutio interior, qua interiori auditu percipitur, qua Deus et angeli loquuntur hominibus. Unde et Zacharias ait: Angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur. Nihilo minus, audire competit Christo secundum divinitatem, immaterialiter et vere incomprehensibiliter. Sic enim audire Filii, est per generationem a Patre accipere totam sapientiam Patris.
paras.en: Further, since a little before he had said, [[8:15|I judge not any man|Ego non judico quemquam]], but now asserted, *Many things I have to judge of you*, lest the Jews object, Your words contradict one another and are false, he added: [[8:26|But he that sent me, is true|sed qui me misit, verax est]], namely the eternal Father, true in himself, as essentially the exemplar truth, first and pure, true also in words and promises; [[8:26|and the things I have heard of him|et ego quæ audivi ab eo]], that is, the truth which I received from him, [[8:26|these same I speak in the world|hæc loquor in mundo]], that is, I preach to men; therefore I do not lie. To hear belongs more properly to Christ according to the humanity than according to the divinity. For as man he heard from the Father, that is, by the inward inspiration of the Father he perceived with the ear of the heart, attended to and learned whatever he knows. For there is an inward speech, perceived by inward hearing, by which God and the angels speak to men. Hence Zacharias too says: [[Zach 2:3|the angel that spoke in me went forth|Angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur]]. None the less, to hear belongs to Christ according to the divinity, immaterially and truly incomprehensibly. For so the Son's hearing is to receive from the Father by generation the whole wisdom of the Father.

paras.t: Et non cognoverunt Judæi, quia Patrem suum eis dicebat Deum, sumendo Deum personaliter, non essentialiter. Per quod Evangelista declarat ruditatem et cæcitatem illorum. Carnales enim erant et animales, non percipientes ea qua Dei sunt.
paras.en: [[8:27|And they understood not that he called God his Father|Et non cognoverunt Judei, quia Patrem suum eis dicebat Deum]], the Jews, taking God personally, not essentially. By this the Evangelist declares their rudeness and blindness. For they were carnal and [[1 Cor 2:14|the sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God|animales, non percipientes ea quæ Dei sunt]].

paras.t: Dixit ergo eis Jesus, hoc est illis quos novit convertendos ad se. In hac enim turba fuerunt nonnulli electi, quibus prædixit ordinem conversionis eorum. Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, id est, postquam erexeritis et confixeritis me in patibulo crucis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum Christus, Filius Dei. Mox enim dum Christus spiritum tradidisset, visis mira[…] fiebant in cœlo et in terra ab hora sexta usque nonam, multi compuncti sunt corde, et confitebantur Jesum fuisse verum et sanctum. Unde legitur in Luca: Omnis turba eorum qui aderant, viso terræmotu et his quæ fiebant, percutientes pectora sua revertebantur. Similiter in die Pentecostes et postea, multa millia Judæorum per prædicationem Apostolorum conversa sunt, in tantum quod etiam multa turba sacerdotum obediebat fidei.
paras.en: [[8:28|Jesus therefore said to them|Dixit ergo eis Jesus]], that is, to those whom he knew would be converted to him. For in this crowd there were some elect, to whom he foretold the order of their conversion. [[8:28|When you shall have lifted up the Son of man|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis]], that is, after you have raised me and fastened me on the gibbet of the cross, [[8:28|then shall you know that I am he|tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]], the Christ, the Son of God. For as soon as Christ had given up the spirit, when the wonders […] [a line of the scan is unreadable here] that were done in heaven and on earth from the sixth hour until the ninth had been seen, many were struck to the heart, and confessed that Jesus had been true and holy[[Matt 27:54||]]. Hence we read in Luke: [[Luke 23:48|And all the multitude of them that were come together to that sight and saw the things that were done returned, striking their breasts|Omnis turba eorum qui … aderant … percutientes pectora sua revertebantur]] [Denis: “All the multitude of them that were present, seeing the earthquake and the things that were done, returned striking their breasts”]. Likewise on the day of Pentecost and afterwards many thousands of the Jews were converted by the preaching of the Apostles[[Acts 2:41||]], so much so that [[Acts 6:7|a great multitude also of the priests obeyed the faith|multa turba sacerdotum obediebat fidei]].

paras.t: Et a me ipso facio nihil, id est, nil penitus ago nisi per virtutem mihi a Patre collatam, a quo habeo quidquid sum et habeo secundum utramque naturam; sed sicut docuit me Pater, id est secundum sapientiam mihi a Patre communicatam, hæc loquor quæ loquor. Doceri autem magis convenit Christo in quantum est homo, quam secundum divinitatis naturam, quamvis et secundum hanc aliquo modo sibi conveniat. Filius enim Dei, qui ad hoc nostram assumpsit naturam, et inter nos conversari dignatus est, ut nos ad superbenedictæ Trinitatis cognitionem perduceret (juxta illud: Scimus quoniam Filius Dei venit, et dedit nobis sensum ut cognoscamus Deum verum), divina et incomprehensibilia qua in sua puritate capere non valemus, dignatus est nobis exprimere modo humano, nobis proportionato et contemperato. Sicque emanationes divinarum Personarum ad intra æternas ac simplicissimas, reseravit per verba præteriti, præsentis futurique temporis, qua tamen aliquam imperfectionem includunt ac innuunt in eo cui attribuuntur. Sed dum talia ad Deum transferimus; debemus omnino auferre ab eis quidquid imperfectionis includunt. Itaque, dum Filius secundum naturam divinam dicit se audisse, vel quod Pater docuit eum, non debemus putare quod Filius sit aliquid aliud quam sapientia ipsius, vel quod sit secundum se quasi insipiens et indoctus, vel ante fuerit genitus, et postea doctus; sed ideo Pater dicitur eum docuisse, quoniam generando eum, communicavit ei omnem sapientiam suam, quæ est una numero in tribus Personis. Verum in omnibus locutionibus talibus, cavendum est ne aliquid potentialitatis aut dependentiæ æstimetur esse in Filio vel Spiritu Sancto: quoniam unaquaque divina hypostasis, est actus purus ensque simpliciter perfectum; et emanatio qua est in Deo, non est nisi effluxio lucis a luce, actus ab actu, et Dei a Deo. In qua nullo modo non esse præcedit esse, sed est ibi processio entis perfecti ab ente perfecto.
paras.en: [[8:28|and that I do nothing of myself|Et a me ipso facio nihil]], that is, I do nothing at all except by the power given me by the Father, from whom I have whatever I am and have according to both natures; [[8:28|But as the Father hath taught me|sed sicut docuit me Pater]], that is, according to the wisdom communicated to me by the Father, [[8:28|these things I speak|hæc loquor]] which I speak. To be taught belongs to Christ more in so far as he is man than according to the nature of the divinity, though according to this too it belongs to him in some way. For the Son of God, who for this took our nature and deigned to dwell among us[[Bar 3:38||]], that he might lead us to the knowledge of the superblessed Trinity (according to that: [[1 John 5:20|And we know that the Son of God is come: and he hath given us understanding that we may know the true God|Scimus quoniam Filius Dei venit, et dedit nobis sensum ut cognoscamus Deum verum]]), deigned to express to us in a human way, proportioned and tempered to us, the divine and incomprehensible things which we cannot grasp in their purity. And so he disclosed the eternal and most simple inward processions of the divine Persons by words of past, present and future time, which yet include and suggest some imperfection in the one to whom they are attributed. But when we transfer such things to God, we must take away from them altogether whatever imperfection they include. So when the Son according to the divine nature says that he has heard, or that the Father taught him, we must not think that the Son is anything other than the Father's wisdom, or that he is in himself as it were unwise and untaught, or was begotten first and taught afterwards; but the Father is said to have taught him because in begetting him he communicated to him all his wisdom, which is numerically one in the three Persons. But in all such expressions we must beware lest any potentiality or dependence be thought to be in the Son or the Holy Ghost: since each divine hypostasis is pure act and being simply perfect; and the procession that is in God is nothing but the outflowing of light from light, act from act, and God from God. In which in no way does not-being go before being, but there is the procession of perfect being from perfect being.

paras.t: Et qui me misit, mecum est. Pater enim inseparabiliter est in Filio secundum utramque ejus naturam. Est quippe in Filio secundum quod Filius est Deus, per identitatem essentiæ; sed in quantum est homo, est Pater in eo per specialissimam inhabitationem et singularissimam gratiam, intimam ac inseparabilem gratiæ unionem atque beatificam fruitionem. Et non reliquit me solum, quoniam inseparabiliter adest mihi. Cujus causa, vel potius signum, subjungitur :
paras.en: [[8:29|And he that sent me, is with me|Et qui me misit, mecum est]]. For the Father is inseparably in the Son according to both his natures. For he is in the Son, in so far as the Son is God, by identity of essence; but in so far as he is man, the Father is in him by a most special indwelling and most singular grace, by the intimate and inseparable union of grace and by beatific enjoyment. [[8:29|and he hath not left me alone|Et non reliquit me solum]], since he is inseparably present to me. The cause of this, or rather the sign, is added:

paras.t: Quia ego quæ placita sunt ei facio semper. Filius etenim Dei, secundum naturam divinam fecit indesinenter quæ complacent Patri, a principio mundi, quoniam operatio Patris ac Filii ad extra est indivisa, estque amborum una voluntas atque potestas: unde quidquid facit unus, facit et alius, et summe complacet alteri. Propter quod supra locutus est Christus: Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor. Porro, secundum naturam assumptam fecit Filius a principio incarnationis qua complacent Patri, quia obedientissimus fuit voluntati divinæ, et in nullo discordabat voluntas humana a divina in Christo. Propter quod ait in Psalmo: In capite libri scriptum est de me ut facerem voluntatem tuam; Deus meus, volui, et legem tuam in medio cordis mei. Et infra testatur: Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio. Factus est enim obediens usque ad mortem, secundum Apostolum. Et quoniam incarnatio Verbi ordinata fuit ad humani generis redemptionem, fecit Christus jugiter qua sunt placita Patri, quoniam totum quod gessit, ad nostram salutem. secundum Patris prædispositionem affectuosissime ordinavit. Hine Pater ait per Isaiam de Christo: Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea, dedin spiritum meum super eum. Hoc quoque sciendum, quod Filius Dei secundum naturam divinam agit, non facit, æternaliter qui placita sunt Patri: quia cum Patre spirat Spiritum Sanctum, contemplatur et amat Patrem amore debito, diligitque Spiritum Sanctum amore gratuito, secundum Richardum.
paras.en: [[8:29|for I do always the things that please him|Quia ego quæ placita sunt ei facio semper]]. For the Son of God according to the divine nature has done unceasingly from the beginning of the world the things that please the Father, since the outward working of the Father and the Son is undivided, and they have one will and power: hence whatever one does, the other does too, and it supremely pleases the other. For which reason Christ said above: [[John 5:17|My Father worketh until now; and I work|Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor]]. Further, according to the nature assumed the Son did from the beginning of the incarnation the things that please the Father, since he was most obedient to the divine will, and in nothing did the human will in Christ disagree with the divine. For which reason he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 39:8|In the head of the book it is written of me|In capite libri scriptum est de me]] [[Ps 39:9|That I should do thy will: O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart|ut facerem voluntatem tuam; Deus meus, volui, et legem tuam in medio cordis mei]]. And below he testifies: [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]. For he [[Phil 2:8|becoming obedient unto death|Factus est enim obediens usque ad mortem]], according to the Apostle. And since the incarnation of the Word was ordered to the redemption of the human race, Christ did continually the things that please the Father, since everything he did he ordered most lovingly to our salvation according to the Father's foreordaining. Hence the Father says through Isaias of Christ: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him: my elect, my soul delighteth in him: I have given my spirit upon him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea, dedi spiritum meum super eum]]. This too must be known, that the Son of God according to the divine nature acts, not makes, eternally the things that please the Father: since with the Father he breathes forth the Holy Ghost, contemplates and loves the Father with due love, and loves the Holy Ghost with free love, according to Richard [of St Victor].

paras.t: Quomodocumque autem accipiatur quod ait Salvator, Ego quæ placita sunt ei facio semper, certum est quod factio ista non est causa a priori, hoc est causa agens principaliter seu meritorie, quod Pater est cum Filio, nec eum solum reliquit. Nam Pater est cum Filio :ternaliter, antei omnem factionem seu operationem ad extra, loquendo de Filio secundum naturam divinam. Secundum naturam vero humanam, inseparabiliter unitus fuit Christus Patri totique supergloriosissimas Trinitati, antei omnem operationem ac meritum ejus, loquendo de prioritate naturæ, non temporis. Itaque factio beneplaciti Patris, est causa a posteriori, vel signum, quod Pater est cum Filio, nec eum solum reliquit. Concordia namque in opere, unionis et amoris exstat indicium.
paras.en: But however what the Saviour says, *I do always the things that please him*, is taken, it is certain that this doing is not the cause a priori, principally or meritoriously, of the Father's being with the Son and not leaving him alone. For the Father is with the Son eternally, before all doing or outward working, speaking of the Son according to the divine nature. And according to the human nature Christ was inseparably united to the Father and the whole supremely glorious Trinity before all his working and merit, speaking of priority of nature, not of time. So the doing of the Father's good pleasure is the cause a posteriori, or the sign, that the Father is with the Son and has not left him alone. For agreement in work is a sign of union and love.

paras.t: Hæc tam profunda, pulchra ac divina illo loquente, multi Judeorum audientium ea crediderunt in eum. Erat enim docens sicut potestatem habens, unicusque magister, qui non solum aures implevit intellectumque excitavit, sed etiam gratiam intelligendi infundere potuit, et infudit.
paras.en: [[8:30|When he spoke these things, many believed in him|Hæc … illo loquente, multi … crediderunt in eum]], when he spoke such deep, beautiful and divine things, many of the Jews who heard them believed in him. For [[Matt 7:29|he was teaching them as one having power|Erat enim docens sicut potestatem habens]], the only master, who not only filled the ears and stirred the understanding, but could pour in the grace of understanding, and did.

paras.t: Dicebat ergo Jesus ad eos qui crediderunt ei Judæos. Superius dixi, quod licet secundum Augustinum distinctio sit inter credere in Christum, et credere Christo tamen evangelista Joannes talem distinctionem non observat. Quum enim dixisset, Multi crediderunt in eum, de eisdem protinus addidit, Dicebat Jesus ad eos qu: crediderunt ei Judæos. Si vos manseritis in sermone meo, id est, perseveranter credideritis, speraveritis, dilexeritis atque feceritis qua prædico, jubeo, vel consulo, vere non ficte discipuli mei eritis, mihi acquiescendo ac obediendo. Verum enim discipulum oportet acquiescere ac parere.
paras.en: [[8:31|Then Jesus said to those Jews, who believed him|Dicebat ergo Jesus ad eos qui crediderunt ei Judæos]]. I said above that, though according to Augustine there is a distinction between believing in Christ and believing Christ, yet John the evangelist does not observe such a distinction. For when he had said, *Many believed in him*, he at once added of the same men, *Jesus said to those Jews who believed him*. [[8:31|If you continue in my word|Si vos manseritis in sermone meo]], that is, if you persevere in believing, hoping, loving and doing what I preach, command or counsel, [[8:31|you shall be my disciples indeed|vere non ficte discipuli mei eritis]], truly, not feignedly, by assenting to me and obeying me. For a true disciple must assent and obey.

paras.t: Et cognoscetis veritatem, id est, me qui sum via, veritas et vita, cognoscetis in futuro per speciem, quem nunc cognoscitis per fidem. Perseverantia quippe meretur hoc premium seu coronam. Unde infra promittit Jesus: Manifestabo ei me ipsum. Nunc enim cognoscimus per speculum in ænigmate; tunc autem facie ad faciem. Vel, Cognoscetis veritatem, id est, ea qua spectant ad fidem, videlicet testimonia Scripturæ atque præcepta legis divinæ, quæ nunc per fidem aliqualiter cognoscere incepistis, in processu temporis plenius cognoscetis per dona Spiritus Sancti, et merito juste conversationis, qua specialem a Deo illuminationem meretur, quemadmodum scriptum est: Fili, concupiscens sapientiam, conserva justitiam, et Deus præbebit illam tibi. Vel, Cognoscetis veritatem, id est, qua cognoscitis in via imperfecte solaque fide, cognoscetis in patria perfecte claraque specie, utpote superbenedictam Trinitatem, Verbi incarnationem, et cetera qua sola nunc fide cognoscuntur. Propter quod dicit Apostolus: Nunc cognosco ex parte, tunc autem cognoscam sicut et cognitus sum.
paras.en: [[8:32|And you shall know the truth|Et cognoscetis veritatem]], that is, me, who am [[John 14:6|the way, and the truth, and the life|via, veritas et vita]], you shall know in the future by sight, whom you now know by faith. For perseverance merits this reward or crown. Hence below Jesus promises: [[John 14:21|and will manifest myself to him|Manifestabo ei me ipsum]]. For [[1 Cor 13:12|We see now through a glass in a dark manner: but then face to face|Nunc enim cognoscimus per speculum in ænigmate ; tunc autem facie ad faciem]] [Denis: “we know now …”]. Or, *you shall know the truth*, that is, the things that concern the faith, namely the testimonies of Scripture and the precepts of the divine law, which you have now begun to know somewhat by faith, you shall know more fully in course of time through the gifts of the Holy Ghost and by the merit of a just life, which merits a special enlightenment from God, as it is written: [[Ecclus 1:33|Son, if thou desire wisdom, keep justice, and God will give her to thee|Fili, concupiscens sapientiam, conserva justitiam, et Deus præbebit illam tibi]]. Or, *you shall know the truth*, that is, what you know imperfectly on the way and by faith alone you shall know perfectly in the fatherland and by clear sight, namely the superblessed Trinity, the incarnation of the Word, and the other things now known by faith alone. For which reason the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 13:12|Now I know in part: but then I shall know even as I am known|Nunc cognosco ex parte, tunc autem cognoscam sicut et cognitus sum]].

paras.t: Et veritas, id est formata seu caritativa cognitio veritatis sub fide cadentis, nunc liberabit, id est, liberos faciet vos a servitute peccati ac dæmonis, et in resurrectione liberabit a servitute pœnæ et mortalitatis: quando, ut ait Apostolus, ipsa creatura liberabitur a servitute corruptionis, et immutabuntur electi. Hinc Salomon ait: Per fidem purgantur peccata; et Deus in Psalmo, Protegam eum, quoniam cognovit nomen meum. Quid enim est purgari a vitiis et defendi a Deo, nisi a servitute peccati et diaboli liberari? Ista veritas, id est veritatis notitia, liberat per modum causæ formalis informantis ac meritoriæ, sicut scientia liberat ab ignorantia; veritas autem quæ Christus est, liberat tanquam causa efficiens, gratiam influens. Nihilo minus Christus ut homo liberat, ut causa meritoria extrinseca; sed cognitio veritatis, ut causa meritoria intrinseca seu inhærens. Verumtamen est servitus caritatis, a qua nulla redimitur creaturæ, quoniam vere libertati non derogat: imo Deo servire, regnare est. Et sicut dixit beatissima Agatha, Summa ingenuitas est servitus Christi.
paras.en: [[8:32|and the truth|Et veritas]], that is, the formed or charitable knowledge of the truth that falls under faith, now [[8:32|shall make you free|liberabit vos]], that is, shall make you free from the slavery of sin and of the devil, and in the resurrection shall free you from the slavery of punishment and mortality: when, as the Apostle says, [[Rom 8:21|the creature also itself shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption|ipsa creatura liberabitur a servitute corruptionis]], and the elect shall be changed[[1 Cor 15:51||]]. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 15:27|By mercy and faith sins are purged away|Per fidem purgantur peccata]] [Denis's reading]; and God in the Psalm, [[Ps 90:14|I will protect him because he hath known my name|Protegam eum, quoniam cognovit nomen meum]]. For what is it to be purged from vices and defended by God, but to be freed from the slavery of sin and the devil? This truth, that is, the knowledge of the truth, frees by way of a formal informing and meritorious cause, as knowledge frees from ignorance; but the truth which is Christ frees as an efficient cause, pouring in grace. None the less Christ as man frees as an extrinsic meritorious cause; but the knowledge of the truth, as an intrinsic or inherent meritorious cause. Yet there is a slavery of charity, from which no creature is redeemed, since it does not take away true freedom: nay, to serve God is to reign. And as the most blessed Agatha said: The highest nobility is the service of Christ.

paras.t: His auditis, Judæi, qui de generis sui nobilitate tumebant, indignati sunt, et responderunt ei: Semen Abrahæ sumus, id est filii tanti tamque liberi Patriarcha, et nemini servivimus unquam. Secundum expositores communiter, falsum dicunt, quoniam patres eorum servierunt in /Ægypto, in Babylone, et in propria terra diversis nationibus, ut patet in libro Judicum. Judæi quoque qui ista dixerunt, servierunt Romanis. Nec curo eos a mendacio excusare, qui Christo summæ veritati contradixerunt. Tamen, quia Christus non redarguit eos in hoc quod asserebant, Nemini servivimus unquam, possit forsitan dici quod loquebantur de servitute naturali. Quod enim nationibus servierunt, fuit propter peccata eorum. Quomodo tu dicis nobis, Liberi eritis? Hoc enim Christus dixit quantum ad sensum, dicendo, Veritas liberabit vos. Tanquam dicerent: In verbo tuo supponitur quod simus servi: quod ita non est. Carnales nempe putabant Jesum de temporali et exteriori libertate profari. Ideo Jesus exponit eis de qua locutus sit libertate, prout recitat Evangelistæ.
paras.en: Hearing these things, the Jews, who were swollen with the nobility of their race, were indignant, and [[8:33|They answered him: We are the seed of Abraham|responderunt ei: Semen Abrahæ sumus]], that is, sons of so great and so free a Patriarch, [[8:33|and we have never been slaves to any man|et nemini servivimus unquam]]. According to the expositors commonly, they say what is false, since their fathers were slaves in Egypt, in Babylon, and in their own land to divers nations, as appears in the book of Judges[[Judg 3:8||]]. The Jews too who said these things were slaves to the Romans. Nor do I care to excuse from lying men who contradicted Christ, the supreme truth. Yet since Christ did not rebuke them in their asserting *we have never been slaves to any man*, it could perhaps be said that they were speaking of natural slavery: for their serving the nations was because of their sins. [[8:33|how sayest thou: you shall be free|Quomodo tu dicis nobis, Liberi eritis?]]? For Christ said this as to the sense, in saying, *the truth shall make you free*. As though they said: In your word it is supposed that we are slaves: which is not so. For, carnal as they were, they thought Jesus was speaking of temporal and outward freedom. So Jesus explains to them of what freedom he spoke, as the Evangelist relates.

paras.t: Respondit eis Jesus: Amen, amen dico vobis, quia omnis qui facit peccatum mortale: de veniali namque non loquitur. quoniam caritatis libertatem non tollit, servus est peccati, id est, peccato subjicitur, a vitio vincitur, secundum impetum pravæ inclinationis movetur quasi ab extraneo, quemadmodum servus movetur a domino cui subjicitur. Unde Petrus asserit: Iniqui servi sunt corruptionis; a quo enim quis victus est, hujus et servus est. Et Apostolus hortatur: Non regnet peccatum in vestro mortali corpore, ut obediatis concupiscentiis ejus. Denique serviendo peccatis servitur diabolo, et ab eo quasi a domino, peccator ligatur, agitatur ac regitur. Ideo dicit Apostolus: Resipiscant a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem. De hujusmodi liberatione locutus est Isaias: Jugum oneris ejus, et virgam humeri ejus et sceptrum exactoris ejus superasti. — Est ergo beata et appetenda libertas, qua ab hujuscemodi vinculis liberamur, de quibus et Salomon fassus est: Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et vinculis peccatorum suorum constringetur. Est quoque infelix libertas, qua est vera ac miserabilis servitus, per quam a vinculis legis divinæ et jugo sanctæ obedientiæ nos ipsos eruimus, sicut cantatur in Psalmo in persona impiorum: Dirumpamus vincula eorum, et projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum. Et in Jeremia Dominus ait populo Judeorum: sæculo confregisti jugum meum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam.
paras.en: [[8:34|Jesus answered them: Amen, amen I say unto you: that whosoever committeth sin|Respondit eis Jesus: Amen, amen dico vobis, quia omnis qui facit peccatum]], mortal sin: for he is not speaking of venial sin, since it does not take away the freedom of charity, [[8:34|is the servant of sin|servus est peccati]], that is, is subject to sin, is overcome by vice, is moved by the drive of a wicked inclination as by something foreign, as a slave is moved by the master to whom he is subject. Hence Peter asserts: [[2 Pet 2:19|they themselves are the slaves of corruption. For by whom a man is overcome, of the same also he is the slave|Iniqui servi sunt corruptionis; a quo enim quis victus est, hujus et servus est]] [Denis: “the wicked are slaves of corruption …”]. And the Apostle exhorts: [[Rom 6:12|Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, so as to obey the lusts thereof|Non regnet peccatum in vestro mortali corpore, ut obediatis concupiscentiis ejus]]. Further, by serving sins one serves the devil, and by him as by a master the sinner is bound, driven and ruled. So the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:26|And they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive at his will|Resipiscant a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem]]. Of this kind of deliverance Isaias spoke: [[Is 9:4|For the yoke of their burden, and the rod of their shoulder, and the sceptre of their oppressor thou hast overcome|Jugum oneris ejus, et virgam humeri ejus et sceptrum exactoris ejus superasti]]. There is, then, a blessed and desirable freedom, by which we are freed from such bonds, of which Solomon too confessed: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capiunt impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringitur]] [Denis: “… and shall be bound with the bonds of his sins”]. There is also an unhappy freedom, which is a true and wretched slavery, by which we tear ourselves from the bonds of the divine law and the yoke of holy obedience, as is sung in the Psalm in the person of the wicked: [[Ps 2:3|Let us break their bonds asunder: and let us cast away their yoke from us|Dirumpamus vincula eorum, et projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum]]. And in Jeremias the Lord says to the people of the Jews: [[Jer 2:20|Of old time thou hast broken my yoke, thou hast burst my bands, and thou saidst: I will not serve|A sæculo confregisti jugum meum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti: Non serviam]].

paras.t: Servus autem non manet in domo in æternum; filius manet in æternum. Hoc frequenter sic est in hominibus, quod servus conducticius non manet in domo domini sui toto tempore vitæ suæ: et quamvis interdum permaneat, non tamen habet jus naturale ad hoc. Filius vero manet in domo parentum quamdiu vivit, si velit, quoniam habet jus naturale ad hoc; et post mortem parentum possidet domum. Sed iste non est sensus a Christo intentus. Est igitur intellectus :
paras.en: [[8:35|Now the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the son abideth for ever|Servus autem non manet in domo in æternum; filius manet in æternum]]. This is often so among men, that a hired servant does not stay in his master's house the whole time of his life: and though he sometimes stays, yet he has no natural right to it. But a son stays in his parents' house as long as he lives, if he will, since he has a natural right to it; and after the parents' death he possesses the house. But this is not the sense Christ intended. The meaning therefore is:

paras.t: Servus autem servitute peccati, non manet in domo, id est in Ecclesia militanti (de qua dicitur: Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei, qua est Ecclesia Dei vivi, columna et firmamentum veritatis), in æternum: quoniam licet modo ad tempus mali commisceantur bonis in Ecclesia, finaliter tamen, præsertim in die judicii, separabuntur ab invicem loco et premio, quando hi ibunt in supplicium æternum, hi vero in vitam eternam. Nunc quoque qui in peccato mortali est, quamdiu hujusmodi est, non manet spiritualiter in Ecclesia, quia per caritatem non unitur membris Ecclesiæ, nec ad mystici corporis pertinet actualiter unitatem. Si tamen est de numero electorum, pertinet ad mysticum corpus Christi secundum predestinationem divinam, et convertetur, æternaliterque manebit in domo Dei. Nam antequam moriatur, incorporabitur Christo atque Ecclesiæ, et sic pertinget ad triumphantis Ecclesiæ perpetuam mansionem. Denique servus servitute timoris pure servilis, non manet in domo seu congregatione electorum fidelium in sæternum, nisi ad servitutem amoris se transferat. Talis enim non est in caritate, nec aliquid promeretur, quamvis qua agit, ex genere bona sint. Filius manet in æternum. Certum est quod Christus Dei Filius naturalis et unicus, maneat in domo Ecclesiæ triumphantis in æternum. Militanti quoque spopondit: Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi. Et ad Hebræos Apostolus dicit: Christus tanquam filius in domo sua, quæ domus sumus nos. Potest ergo universaliter accipi, ut sit sensus: Filius enim quicumque a servitute peccati liber et alienus, quin spiritum adoptionis accipit, in quo clamat, Abba (Pater), manet in domo Ecclesiæ in æternum, quia per fidem et caritatem quibus nunc manet in Ecclesia militanti, perveniet ad visionem et fruitionem per quas sine fine manebit in Ecclesia triumphanti.
paras.en: *The servant*, by the slavery of sin, *abideth not in the house*, that is, in the Church militant (of which it is said: [[1 Tim 3:15|thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth|Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi, columna et firmamentum veritatis]]), *for ever*: since, though now for a time the wicked are mixed with the good in the Church, yet in the end, above all at the day of judgment, they will be separated from one another in place and reward, when [[Matt 25:46|these shall go into everlasting punishment: but the just, into life everlasting|ibunt hi in supplicium æternum: justi autem in vitam æternam]] [Denis: “these … but those into life everlasting”]. Now too he who is in mortal sin, so long as he is so, does not abide spiritually in the Church, since he is not united by charity to the members of the Church, nor belongs actually to the unity of the mystical body. Yet if he is of the number of the elect, he belongs to the mystical body of Christ according to divine predestination, and will be converted, and will abide eternally in the house of God. For before he dies he will be incorporated into Christ and the Church, and so will reach the everlasting dwelling of the Church triumphant. Further, the servant by the slavery of purely servile fear does not abide in the house or congregation of the faithful elect for ever, unless he passes over to the service of love. For such a one is not in charity, nor merits anything, though what he does is good in kind. *The son abideth for ever*. It is certain that Christ, the natural and only Son of God, abides in the house of the Church triumphant for ever. To the Church militant too he promised: [[Matt 28:20|behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]]. And to the Hebrews the Apostle says: [[Heb 3:6|But Christ as the Son in his own house: which house are we|Christus tanquam filius in domo sua, quæ domus sumus nos]]. So it can be taken universally, the sense being: Every son, free from and a stranger to the slavery of sin, who receives [[Rom 8:15|the spirit of adoption of sons, whereby we cry: Abba (Father)|spiritum adoptionis filiorum, in quo clamamus: Abba (Pater]], abides in the house of the Church for ever, since by the faith and charity by which he now abides in the Church militant he will come to the sight and enjoyment by which he will abide without end in the Church triumphant.

paras.t: Est autem et servus servitute caritatis qui manet in domo in æternum: cui dicitur, Euge, serve bone, intra in gaudium Domini tui. Et est filius sola vocatione et nomine, qui non manet in domo ir æternum, juxta illud: Filii regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores; et illud, Filios enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me.
paras.en: There is also a servant by the service of charity, who abides in the house for ever: to whom it is said, [[Matt 25:21|Well done, good|Euge, serve bone]] … [[Matt 25:21|Enter thou into the joy of thy lord|intra in gaudium domini tui]]. And there is a son by calling and name only, who does not abide in the house for ever, according to that: [[Matt 8:12|But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into the exterior darkness|Filii regni ejicientur in tenebras exteriores]]; and that, [[Is 1:2|I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me|Filios enutrivi et exaltavi, ipsi autem spreverunt me]].

paras.t: Si ergo Filius Dei naturalis, qui solus est inter mortuos liber, et libere potuit dicere, Venit ad me princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam; vos liberaverit a servitute peccati, non corruptibilibus auro et argento, sed pretioso sanguine suo; vere liberi eritis, id est ab omni violenta atque extranea dominatione immunes, et soli Deo per caritatem subjecti, imo et Filio naturali per gratiam adoptionis conformeæ, quoniam filiatio adoptiva, naturalis filiationis est similitudo. Hac libertas in prædestinatis nunc inchoatur per recessum a corruptione peccati, et in futuro perficietur atque complebitur, quando natura humana perfecte reformabitur, ablatis ab ea universis malis, poenis ac miseriis propter originale peccatum inductis: quæ utique sunt grave jugum, de quo habetur in Ecclesiastico: Occupatio magna creata est hominibus, et jugum grave super omnes filios Adam, a die exitus de ventre matris eorum usque in diem sepulturæ in matrem omnium. In resurrectione ergo futura, consequentur electi merito Christi perfectam in anima et corpore integritatem, libertatem, et incorruptionem, qua facit proximum esse Deo, ut Sapiens ait. Propter quod etiam dicit Apostolus: Salvatorem exspectamus, qui reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ.
paras.en: [[8:36|If therefore the son shall make you free|Si ergo Filius Dei naturalis, qui solus est inter mortuos liber, et libere potuit dicere, Venit ad me princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam ; vos liberaverit]], the natural Son of God, who alone is [[Ps 87:6|free among the dead|inter mortuos liber]], and could freely say, [[John 14:30|for the prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not any thing|Venit ad me princeps mundi hujus, et in me non habet quidquam]], shall make you free from the slavery of sin, [[1 Pet 1:18|not redeemed with corruptible things, as gold or silver|non corruptibilibus auro et argento]], [[1 Pet 1:19|But with the precious blood of Christ|sed pretioso sanguine]] his own; [[8:36|you shall be free indeed|vere liberi eritis]], that is, exempt from all violent and foreign lordship, and subject to God alone by charity, nay, conformed also to the natural Son by the grace of adoption[[Rom 8:29||]], since adoptive sonship is a likeness of natural sonship. This freedom is begun now in the predestined by withdrawing from the corruption of sin, and in the future will be perfected and completed, when human nature is perfectly reformed, all the evils, punishments and miseries brought in by original sin being taken from it: which are indeed a heavy yoke, of which it is had in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 40:1|Great labour is created for all men, and a heavy yoke is upon the children of Adam, from the day of their coming out of their mother's womb, until the day of their burial into the mother of all|Occupatio magna creata est omnibus hominibus, et jugum grave super filios Adam, a die exitus de ventre matris eorum usque in diem sepulturæ in matrem omnium]]. At the future resurrection, then, the elect will obtain by the merit of Christ perfect integrity, freedom and incorruption in soul and body, [[Wis 6:20|And incorruption bringeth near to God|incorruptio autem facit esse proximum Deo]] [Denis: “which maketh to be near to God”], as the Wise Man says. For which reason too the Apostle says: [[Phil 3:20|we look for the Saviour|Salvatorem exspectamus]] … [[Phil 3:21|Who will reform the body of our lowness|qui reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ]].

paras.t: Sed si vere liberi erunt quos Filius Dei liberavit, ergo omnes liberi erimus, quia pro omnibus mortuus est Christus. Et respondendum, quod Christus liberavit omnes sufficienter, id est, quantum in se est. Propter quod ait: Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Solos vero prædestinatos liberavit efficaciter. Hi enim finaliter consequuntur fructum, virtutem ac meritum dominicæ passionis, sicque veraciter liberi fiunt. Verumtamen ista libertas non aufert fidelibus servitutem exteriorem et subjectionem corporalem sub principibus terræ. Ideo enim jubet Apostolus: Cui tributum, tributum; cui vectigal, vectigal. Itemque: Servi, subditi estote dominis carnalibus cum omni timore.
paras.en: But if those whom the Son of God has freed shall be free indeed, then we shall all be free, since [[2 Cor 5:15|Christ died for all|pro omnibus mortuus est Christus]]. The answer is that Christ freed all sufficiently, that is, as far as lies in him. For which reason he says: [[John 10:15|and I lay down my life for my sheep|Animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]. But he freed the predestined alone effectively. For these finally obtain the fruit, power and merit of the Lord's passion, and so are made truly free. Yet this freedom does not take from the faithful outward service and bodily subjection under the princes of the earth. For this is why the Apostle commands: [[Rom 13:7|tribute, to whom tribute is due: custom, to whom custom|Cui tributum, tributum; cui vectigal, vectigal]]. And again: [[Eph 6:5|Servants, be obedient to them that are your lords according to the flesh, with fear|Servi, … dominis carnalibus cum … timore]] [Denis: “Servants, be subject to your carnal masters with all fear”].

paras.t: Scio quia filii carnales Abrahæ estis; sed quæritis me interficere. Superius dixit Evangelista, quod multi crediderunt in Jesum, et quod Jesus locutus est eis, Si manseritis in sermone meo, vere discipuli mei eritis, et cetera nunc commemorata: quomodo ergo nunc ait ad eos, Quæritis me interficere? Dicendum, quod inter prædictos credentes erant aliqui non credentes, ad quos sermo iste dirigitur. Sepe enim Scriptura loquitur quasi ad eosdem, et tamen ad diversos referri oportet: sicut ait Apostolus, In omnibus divites facti estis in illo, ita quod nihil vobis desit in ulla gratia; et post pauca quasi eisdem locutus est: Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio, nonne carnales estis? Sed hoc refertur ad alios. Simili modo ait Psalmista: Quum occideret eos, quærebant eum, et revertebantur, et diluculo veniebant ad eum. Qui enim occidebantur, non revertebantur diluculo. Ideo vero quæritis me interficere, quia sermo meus non capit in vobis, id est, corda vestra non apprehendit, convertendo illa ad me, nec operatur in vobis propter vestram malitiam, qui meam prædicationem humiliter non auditis, neque reverenter suscipitis. Beati quorum mentes capit et furatur sermo divinus, transferendo animas audientium extra se usque in Deum.
paras.en: [[8:37|I know that you are the children of Abraham: but you seek to kill me|Scio quia filii carnales Abrahæ estis ; sed quæritis me interficere]], carnal children. Above, the Evangelist said that many believed in Jesus, and that Jesus said to them, *If you continue in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed*, and the rest now recalled[[8:30||]][[8:31||]]: how then does he now say to them, *You seek to kill me?* It must be said that among those believers spoken of there were some unbelievers, to whom this speech is directed. For Scripture often speaks as though to the same people, and yet it must be referred to different ones: as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 1:5|in all things you are made rich in him|In omnibus divites facti estis in illo]], [[1 Cor 1:7|So that nothing is wanting to you in any grace|ita ut nihil vobis desit in ulla gratia]]; and a little after he spoke as though to the same: [[1 Cor 3:3|For, whereas there is among you envying and contention, are you not carnal|Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio, nonne carnales estis]]? But this is referred to others. In like manner the Psalmist says: [[Ps 77:34|When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned, and came to him early in the morning|Quum occideret eos, quærebant eum, et revertebantur, et diluculo veniebant ad eum]]. For those who were slain did not return early in the morning. [[8:37|because my word hath no place in you|quia sermo meus non capit in vobis]]: for this reason you seek to kill me, that is, it does not lay hold of your hearts, turning them to me, nor work in you, because of your malice, who do not hear my preaching humbly nor receive it reverently. Blessed are they whose minds the divine word lays hold of and steals away, carrying the souls of the hearers out of themselves even into God.

paras.t: Ego quod vidi apud Patrem meum, loquor, id est, veritatem quam in Patre cognovi, quem videndo omnia æternaliter video, vobis annuntio. Vel, Quod vidi apud Patrem, id est, me ipsum, qui sum Verbum quod erat in principio apud Deum, prædico vobis. Quælibet divina nempe Persona conspicit, non solum in se, sed etiam in alia, se ipsam et cuncta creata et creabilia. Et vos quæ vidistis apud patrem vestrum, id est mala quæ diabolo suggerente concepistis, facitis, non resistendo diabolicis tentamentis. Quamvis ergo iniqui non advertant se a diabolo agitari, tentari seu inclinari, dicuntur tamen in diabolo mala videre, quoniam interiori oculo inspiciunt et approbant qua diabolus suggerit, proponens ea cum aliqua persuasione sub specie boni, in tantum ut homo sæpe existimet talia non a diabolo, sed ab angelo inspirata.
paras.en: [[8:38|I speak that which I have seen with my Father|Ego quod vidi apud Patrem meum, loquor]], that is, I announce to you the truth which I have known in the Father, seeing whom I see all things eternally. Or, *that which I have seen with the Father*, that is, myself, who am [[John 1:2|The same was in the beginning with God|Verbum quod erat in principio apud Deum]], I preach to you. For each divine Person beholds, not only in itself but also in the other, itself and all things created and creatable. [[8:38|and you do the things that you have seen with your father|Et vos quæ vidistis apud patrem vestrum, facitis]], that is, the evils which you conceived at the devil's suggestion, by not resisting the devil's temptations. Though the wicked do not notice that they are driven, tempted or inclined by the devil, they are yet said to see evils in the devil, since with the inward eye they look upon and approve what the devil suggests, putting it forward with some persuasion under the appearance of good, so much so that a man often thinks such things inspired not by the devil but by an angel.

paras.t: Responderunt et dixerunt ei: Pater noster Abraham est. Quasi dicant: faciendo opera patris tam sancti, non erramus, nec increpari meremur, sed potius tu, qui nobis improperas quod opera facimus quæ scimus facta ab illo. Dicit eis Jesus: Si filii Abrahæ estis secundum perfectam rationem proprietatemque filii, cujus est patri assimilari, id est, si filii Abrahæ estis, non solum carnales per seminis propagationem, sed insuper spirituales per morum mutationem, opera Abrahæ facite, mansuete, patienter, caritative atque humiliter conversando ut Abraham, qui testimonio libri Genesis probatur fuisse valde mansuetus, patiens, caritativus et humilis. Maxime tamen Salvator intendit hortari Judæos ad imitandum fidem et obedientiam Abrahæ, qui teste Apostolo, contra spem in spem credidit, et non hæsitavit in fide, et usque ad amantissimi innocentisque filii occisionem paruit Deo.
paras.en: [[8:39|They answered, and said to him: Abraham is our father|Responderunt et dixerunt ei: Pater noster Abraham est]]. As though they said: in doing the works of so holy a father we do not err, nor deserve to be rebuked, but rather you, who reproach us that we do works which we know were done by him. [[8:39|Jesus saith them: If you be the children of Abraham|Dicit eis Jesus: Si filii Abrahæ estis]], according to the perfect nature and property of a son, to whom it belongs to be like his father, that is, if you are sons of Abraham not only carnally by the propagation of seed, but also spiritually by likeness of manners, [[8:39|do the works of Abraham|opera Abrahæ facite]], living meekly, patiently, charitably and humbly like Abraham, who by the testimony of the book of Genesis is proved to have been very meek, patient, charitable and humble. But above all the Saviour means to exhort the Jews to imitate the faith and obedience of Abraham, who, as the Apostle testifies, [[Rom 4:18|Who against hope believed in hope|contra spem in spem credidit]], [[Rom 4:20|staggered not by distrust|non hæsitavit in fide]] [Denis: “staggered not in faith”], and obeyed God even to the slaying of his most beloved and innocent son[[Gen 22:10||]].

paras.t: Nunc autem quæritis me interficere, hominem qui veritatem locutus sum vobis quam audivi a Deo. Hoc, id est simile huic, Abraham non fecit. Non enim voluit ex malitia aliquem innocentem, vel nuntium Dei vera prædicantem, occidere, sed hospitalis fuit et plenus operibus caritatis. Vos facitis opera patris vestri, id est opera vitiosa demoni placita, cujus malitiam imitamini quasi filii ejus.
paras.en: [[8:40|But now you seek to kill me, a man who have spoken the truth to you, which I have heard of God|Nunc autem quæritis me interficere, hominem qui veritatem locutus sum vobis, quam audivi a Deo]]. [[8:40|this Abraham did not|Hoc Abraham non fecit]], *this*, that is, the like of this. For he would not out of malice kill any innocent man, or a messenger of God preaching true things; but he was hospitable and full of works of charity. [[8:41|You do the works of your father|Vos facitis opera patris vestri]], that is, vicious works pleasing to the devil, whose malice you imitate as his sons.

paras.t: Dixerunt itaque ei: Nos ex fornicatione non sumus nati; unum patrem habemus Dcui. Hoc dixerunt de fornicatione spirituali, scilicet idololatria, per quam anima sponsa Verbi separatur a Sponso cœlesti. Unde Dominus loquitur Moysi: Populus iste fornicabitur post deos alienos. Et in Osee habetur: Fornicati sunt a Deo suo. Videntes ergo Judæi quod Jesus loquebatur eis de alio patre quam patre carnali, videlicet de patre qui propter operis qualitatem asseritur pater, voluerunt ostendere quod essent filii Dei, non dæmonis. Itaque dicunt: Nos ex fornicatione, id est ex idololatria, non sumus nati, loquendo de nativitate quæ in operum imitatione consistit, ut possimus dici filii diaboli cui idololatre serviunt, unde et filii ejus dicuntur; unum patrem habemus Deum, creatorem et provisorem nostrum, cujus legem cærimoniasque servamus: de quo Moyses testatur, Numquid non ipse est pater tuus, qui possedit te, et fecit et creavit te? Deum igitur nominant patrem, non solum ratione creationis, sed propter specialem providentiam qua gubernavit populum Israel tanquam electum et peculiarem, et propter cultum latriæ quem ei soli impenderunt. Propter quod in Isaia inducitur: Et nunc, Domine, pater noster es tu, nos vero lutum. Et in Jeremia Dominus contestatur: Factus sum Israeli pater, et Ephraim primogenitus meus.
paras.en: [[8:41|They said therefore to him: We are not born of fornication: we have one Father, even God|Dixerunt itaque ei: Nos ex fornicatione non sumus nati; unum patrem habemus Deum]]. This they said of spiritual fornication, namely idolatry, by which the soul, the bride of the Word, is separated from the heavenly Bridegroom. Hence the Lord says to Moses: [[Deut 31:16|this people rising up will go a fornicating after strange gods|Populus iste fornicabitur post deos alienos]]. And in Osee it is had: [[Osee 9:1|thou hast committed fornication against thy God|Fornicatus es a Deo tuo]] [Denis: “They have committed fornication against their God”]. The Jews, then, seeing that Jesus was speaking to them of another father than their carnal father, namely of a father who is called father by reason of the quality of the work, wished to show that they were sons of God, not of the devil. So they say: *We are not born of fornication*, that is, of idolatry, speaking of the birth that consists in imitating works, so that we could be called sons of the devil, whom idolaters serve, whence they are called his sons; *we have one Father, even God*, our creator and provider, whose law and ceremonies we keep: of whom Moses testifies, [[Deut 32:6|Is not he thy father, that hath possessed thee, and made thee, and created thee|Numquid non ipse est pater tuus, qui possedit te, et fecit et creavit te]]? So they call God father, not only by reason of creation, but because of the special providence by which he governed the people of Israel as chosen and peculiar, and because of the worship of *latria* which they paid to him alone. For which reason in Isaias it is put: [[Is 64:8|And now, O Lord, thou art our father, and we are clay|Et nunc, Domine, pater noster es tu, nos vero lutum]]. And in Jeremias the Lord testifies: [[Jer 31:9|I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn|Factus sum Israeli pater, et Ephraim primogenitus meus]].

paras.t: Dixit ergo eis Jesus: Si Deus pater vester esset eo modo quo dicitis, scilicet per cultum ei placentem, ex caritate procedentem, et operum imitationem, quomodo fuit pater sanctorum Patriarcharum ac Prophetarum, diligeretis utique me, quem ex odio vultis occidere. Ego enim ex Deo processi et veni. Si loquamur de Deo personaliter, tunc Christus processit ex Deo, id est, ex Patre per generationem æternam manavit, juxta illud Michææ: Egressus ejus a principio, a diebus æternitatis; et in Psalmo, Ex utero ante luciferum genui te. Et venit ab eo, id est, per incarnationis mysterium descendit in mundum missus a Patre. Si vero loquamur de Deo essentialiter, sicut loquebantur isti Judæi qui Trinitatis notitia caruerunt, tunc Christus secundum naturam assumptam processit ex Deo Trinitate per animæ suæ creationem et corporis supernaturalem informationem, et venit tanquam minister illius. De quo Deus ait: Ecce intelliget servus meus, et exaltabitur, et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde. Neque enim a me ipso veni, id est propria voluntate dumtaxat, vel voluntate humana, tanquam causa prima ac principali. Nihilo minus Christus secundum quod Deus, misit se ipsum secundum quod homo. Incarnatio enim facta est a tota Trinitate: incarnatio autem est missio Filii. Hoc superius dictum est plenius. Sed ille me misit. Qui autem diligit Patrem, diligit Filium; et qui amat mittentem ac Dominum, amat missum atque ministrum. Quoniam ergo Judæi non dilexerunt Christum Dei Filium, legatum et servum, palam quod nec Patrem vel Deum dilexerunt.
paras.en: [[8:42|Jesus therefore said to them: If God were your Father|Dixit ergo eis Jesus: Si Deus pater vester esset]] in the way you say, namely by worship pleasing to him, proceeding from charity, and by imitation of works, as he was the father of the holy Patriarchs and Prophets, [[8:42|you would indeed love me|diligeretis utique me]], whom out of hatred you wish to kill. [[8:42|For from God I proceeded, and came|Ego enim ex Deo processi et veni]]. If we speak of God personally, then Christ *proceeded from God*, that is, flowed from the Father by eternal generation, according to that of Micheas: [[Mich 5:2|his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity|Egressus ejus a principio, a diebus æternitatis]]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 109:3|from the womb before the day star I begot thee|Ex utero ante luciferum genui te]]. *And came* from him, that is, by the mystery of the incarnation came down into the world, sent by the Father. But if we speak of God essentially, as these Jews spoke, who lacked knowledge of the Trinity, then Christ according to the nature assumed proceeded from God the Trinity by the creation of his soul and the supernatural forming of his body, and came as his minister. Of whom God says: [[Is 52:13|Behold my servant shall understand, he shall be exalted, and extolled, and shall be exceeding high|Ecce intelliget servus meus, et exaltabitur, et elevabitur, et sublimis erit valde]]. [[8:42|for I came not of myself|neque enim a me ipso veni]], that is, by my own will only, or by human will, as first and principal cause. None the less Christ as God sent himself as man. For the incarnation was done by the whole Trinity: and the incarnation is the sending of the Son. This has been said more fully above. [[8:42|but he sent me|sed ille me misit]]. Now he who loves the Father loves the Son; and he who loves the sender and Lord loves the one sent and the minister. Since, then, the Jews did not love Christ, the Son of God, his envoy and servant, it is plain that neither did they love the Father or God.

paras.t: Quare loquelam meam non cognoscitis? id est, cur non intelligitis verba mea? cur ex qualitate prædicationis meæ, ex profunditate et efficacia eloquii mei, non attenditis quod vere sim missus a Deo, et loquens verba illius? Solet enim homo cognosci ex verbis suis: et quoniam nunquam locutus est homo sicut Jesus, debebant auditores illius loquelam ejus pensare, quod non esset nisi divina ac regis Messiæ. Hoc Christus interrogavit increpando Judæos. Moxque respondet instruendo eos: quia non potestis audire sermonem meum: id est, idcirco non intelligitis verba mea, quoniam propter rancorem et displicentiam quam concepistis adversum me eo quod increpem vitia vestra, sic obcæcati induratique estis, quod non potestis æquanimiter audire et recte judicare verba mea; sed statim dum loquor, passiones oriuntur in vobis, et induratur cor vestrum, ne humiliter penset qua prædico. Qui enim odit alium odio magno, quidquid agit vel loquitur ille, displicet odienti. Propter quod legitur in Michæa: Numquid vestrum est scire judicium, qui odio habetis bonum? Et Sapiens ait: Excæcavit eos malitia eorum.
paras.en: [[8:43|Why do you not know my speech|Quare loquelam meam non cognoscitis]]? that is, why do you not understand my words? why do you not notice, from the quality of my preaching, from the depth and power of my speech, that I am truly sent by God and speak his words? For a man is wont to be known by his words: and since [[John 7:46|Never did man speak like this man|nunquam locutus est homo sicut]] Jesus, his hearers ought to have judged of his speech that it was none other than divine and the Messias's, the king's. Christ asked this rebuking the Jews. And at once he answers, instructing them: [[8:43|Because you cannot hear my word|quia non potestis audire sermonem meum]]: that is, for this reason you do not understand my words, that because of the rancour and displeasure you have conceived against me because I rebuke your vices, you are so blinded and hardened that you cannot hear my words with an even mind and judge them rightly; but as soon as I speak, passions arise in you, and your heart is hardened, so that it does not humbly weigh what I preach. For when someone hates another with great hatred, whatever the other does or says displeases him. For which reason we read in Micheas: [[Mich 3:1|Is it not your part to know judgment|Numquid vestrum est scire judicium]], [[Mich 3:2|You that hate good|qui odio habetis bonum]]? And the Wise Man says: [[Wis 2:21|for their own malice blinded them|Excæcavit eos malitia eorum]].

paras.t: Deinde Christus aperte ostendit quid per patrem Judæorum perversorum intellexerit. Vos ex patre diabolo estis, non per creationem vel generationem, ut Manichæi mentiti sunt, sed per malitiæ imitationem. Diabolus enim est pater super omnes filios superbiæ, ut dicitur in Job. Judæi autem valde pomposi fuerunt, præsertim propter generis dignitatem, et quia præ ceteris gentibus legem a Deo acceperunt: unde alios populos reputaverunt pro nihilo. Similiter diabolus est pater super omnes filios invidiæ. Invidia nempe diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum, et imitantur eum qui sunt ex parte illius. Et desideria patris vestri vultis facere, id est, malas affectiones diaboli quas habet in se, quas etiam ingerit vobis, vultis perducere ad effectum, persequendo et occidendo me, ceteraque peccata patrando quæ Apostolus vocat opera carnis, ut sunt furta, adulteria, blasphemia, contentiones, iræ, rixæ, æmulationes, atque similia, quæ ad Galatas Paulus enumerat: de quibus ait Joannes in prima sua Canonica, In hoc apparuit Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera diaboli.
paras.en: Then Christ shows openly what he meant by the father of the wicked Jews. [[8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]], not by creation or generation, as the Manichees lyingly said, but by imitation of malice. For the devil is father over all the children of pride, as is said in Job[[Job 41:25||]]. And the Jews were very pompous, above all because of the dignity of their race, and because before other nations they had received the law from God: whence they counted other peoples as nothing. Likewise the devil is father over all the children of envy. For [[Wis 2:24|by the envy of the devil, death came into the world|Invidia nempe diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum]], [[Wis 2:25|And they follow him that are of his side|et imitantur eum qui sunt ex parte illius]]. [[8:44|and the desires of your father you will do|Et desideria patris vestri vultis facere]], that is, the evil affections of the devil which he has in himself, and which he also thrusts into you, you will to carry into effect, by persecuting and killing me, and committing the other sins which the Apostle calls [[Gal 5:19|the works of the flesh|opera carnis]], such as thefts, adulteries, blasphemy, contentions, anger, quarrels, emulations and the like, which Paul lists to the Galatians[[Gal 5:20||]]: of which John says in his first Canonical Epistle, [[1 John 3:8|For this purpose, the Son of God appeared, that he might destroy the works of the devil|In hoc apparuit Filius Dei, ut dissolvat opera diaboli]].

paras.t: Deinde Christus declarat mala diaboli, et ostendit quare et qualiter Judæi imitati sunt illum. Ille, puta diabolus primus seu Lucifer, homicida erat, id est spiritualis occisor interioris hominis; scilicet animarum primorum parentum, ab initio, id est a principio operum sex dierum, videlicet a tempore formationis Adæ et Eve: quia ut patet in Genesi, serpens, hoc est diabolus per serpentem, decepit Evam, et per illam induxit Adam ad inobedientiam, sicque uterque eorum peccavit mortaliter, et tota posteritas infecta est, et quodammodo interfecta, operante diabolo. Est enim homo exterior, et homo interior, dicente Apostolo: Licet is qui foris est noster homo corrumpatur, tamen is qui intus est renovatur de die in diem. Si ergo homicida est qui vile et corruptibile corpus occidit, auferendo vitam naturæ, quanto amplius homicida censendus est qui animam immortalem, nobilem, Dei imagine refulgentem, interficit, auferendo vitam gratiæ? Unde quicumque pravo exemplo, vel suggestione pestifera, aut alio modo, hominem inducit ad peccatum mortale, homicida vocatur, præsertim quum anima sit principalior pars hominis, per quam ponitur homo in specie, vivificatur, gubernatur, et a brutis distinguitur. Preterea elucescit ex his quod toties homicidium facimus, manusque sacrilegas in nos ipsos injicimus, quoties peccamus mortaliter, quia tot letalia vulnera animabus nostris infligimus. Nec solum homicidam vocat Scriptura, qui corpus interimit animamve occidit; sed etiam, ut ait Joannes in sua Canonica: Omnis qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est.
paras.en: Then Christ declares the evils of the devil, and shows why and how the Jews imitated him. [[8:44|He was a murderer from the beginning|Ille … homicida erat … ab initio]], namely the first devil or Lucifer, that is, a spiritual slayer of the inward man, namely of the souls of our first parents, *from the beginning*, that is, from the beginning of the works of the six days, namely from the time of the forming of Adam and Eve: since, as appears in Genesis, the serpent, that is, the devil through the serpent, deceived Eve[[Gen 3:13||]], and through her led Adam to disobedience, and so each of them sinned mortally, and all their posterity was infected, and in a manner slain, the devil working it. For there is an outward man and an inward man, as the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 4:16|though our outward man is corrupted, yet the inward man is renewed day by day|licet is qui foris est noster homo corrumpatur, tamen is qui intus est renovatur de die in diem]]. If, then, he is a murderer who kills the vile and corruptible body, taking away the life of nature, how much more is he to be judged a murderer who kills the immortal, noble soul, shining with the image of God, taking away the life of grace? Hence whoever by evil example, or pestilent suggestion, or in any other way, leads a man to mortal sin, is called a murderer, above all since the soul is the more principal part of man, by which man is placed in his species, quickened, governed, and distinguished from the brutes. Further, it shines out from this that as often as we sin mortally, so often we commit murder and lay sacrilegious hands on ourselves, since we inflict so many deadly wounds on our souls. And Scripture calls a murderer not only him who kills the body or slays the soul, but also, as John says in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 3:15|Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer|Omnis qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est]].

paras.t: Deinde ponit aliud malum diaboli. Et in veritate non stetit, id est, in veritate justitiæ, in recta ratione, in vera obedientia non permansit. Statim enim ut creatus est, cernens se tantæ excellentiæ et decoris præ aliis angelis, intumuit, aliosque quos potuit sibi attraxit, et contra Creatorem se erigens: In cœlum (inquit) conscendam, supra astra cœli exaltabo solium meum, ascendam super altitudinem nubium, similis ero Altissimo. Fuit equidem creatus in magna perfectione et dignitate, in maxima sapientia, in naturali justitia, imo et in gratia, secundum opinionem probabilem, et per consequens in caritate; sed non stetit in his, victus propria elatione, ex consideratione eminentiæ suæ, et quia pre cunctis angelorum ordinibus eminebat. Sed non vidit Deum per speciem: aliter fuisset confirmatus in bono. Novit tamen Deum esse unum ac trinum: non naturali ingenio, sed per fidem, secundum quosdam. Fuerunt enim angeli omnes creati in fide, secundum Thomam. Hine per Ezechielem apostatæ angelo dicitur: Tu signaculum similitudinis, plenus sapientia et perfectus decore, in deliciis paradisi Dei fuisti; omnis lapis pretiosus operimentum tuum. Tu Cherub extentus et protegens, et posui te in monte sancto Dei. Elevatum est cor tuum in decore tuo, repleta sunt interiora tua iniquitate, et ejeci te de monte sancto Dei, et perdidi te, o Cherub, de medio lapidum ignitorum, et in terram projeci te. De casu quoque angelorum scribitur Judæ primo, et in secunda Petri.
paras.en: Then he puts another evil of the devil. [[8:44|and he stood not in the truth|Et in veritate non stetit]], that is, he did not remain in the truth of justice, in right reason, in true obedience. For as soon as he was created, seeing himself of such excellence and beauty beyond the other angels, he swelled up, and drew to himself the others whom he could, and raising himself against the Creator said: [[Is 14:13|I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God|In cœlum conscendam, super astra Dei exaltabo solium meum]] [Denis: “above the stars of heaven”], [[Is 14:14|I will ascend above the height of the clouds, I will be like the most High|Ascendam super altitudinem nubium, similis ero Altissimo]]. For he was created in great perfection and dignity, in the greatest wisdom, in natural justice, nay in grace too, according to a probable opinion, and consequently in charity; but he did not stand in these, overcome by his own pride, from considering his own eminence, and because he stood out above all the orders of angels. But he did not see God by sight: otherwise he would have been confirmed in good. Yet he knew God to be one and three: not by natural wit, but by faith, according to some. For all the angels were created in faith, according to Thomas. Hence through Ezechiel it is said to the apostate angel: [[Ezech 28:12|Thou wast the seal of resemblance, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty|Tu signaculum similitudinis, plenus sapientia et perfectus decore]]. [[Ezech 28:13|Thou wast in the pleasures of the paradise of God: every precious stone was thy covering|in deliciis paradisi Dei fuisti; omnis lapis pretiosus operimentum tuum]]. [[Ezech 28:14|Thou a cherub stretched out, and protecting, and I set thee in the holy mountain of God|Tu Cherub extentus et protegens, et posui te in monte sancto Dei]].
