Of which judgment it is said below: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world|Nunc judicium est mundi]]. In His first coming, then, Christ came to discern between the elect and the foreknown [that is, those foreseen to be lost], converting the former graciously and lovingly, and justly forsaking the latter. But in His second coming He will come to make the judgment of retribution, of which He said: [[John 3:17|God sent not his Son into the world, to judge the world|Non misit Deus Filium suum ut judicet mundum]]; and, [[John 8:15|I judge not any man|Ego non judico quemquam]]. [[9:39|that they who see not|Ut qui non vident]], that is, the simple and unlearned, such as were the disciples of Christ and this blind man, [[9:39|may see|videant]], that is, may be spiritually enlightened by me, and contemplate me, the light of the world, with the eyes of faith: [[9:39|and they who see|et qui vident]], that is, the Scribes and Pharisees and the rest who are wise in their own eyes[[Is 5:21||]], lettered and prudent, [[9:39|may become blind|cæci fiant]], that is, may be deprived of the light of faith and the other gifts of the grace of the Holy Spirit, and be more grievously darkened than before, on account of their pride and their demerits. With this word of Christ agrees what the just Simeon is read to have foretold: [[Luke 2:34|Behold this child is set for the fall and for the resurrection of many in Israel|Ecce positus est hic in ruinam et resurrectionem multorum in Israel]]. Christ too says elsewhere, in accord with these words: [[Matt 11:25|I confess to thee, O Father|Confiteor tibi, Pater]], [[Matt 11:25|because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones|quoniam abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]].

paras.t: Possunt quoque per non videntes, intelligi peccatores vitiis obfuscati, sed prædestinati, ut Matthæus, Zachæus, Magdalena, qui per Christum illustrati sunt corde; per videntes vero, hi quos inflavit superbia in tantum, ut Christi prædicationem deridere præsumpserint. Tertio, et communius, per non videntes, intelliguntur gentiles, unius veri Dei agnitione carentes; per videntes vero, Judæi, divina lege instructi. In Christi autem adventu et deinceps, cœpit populus Judæorum excæcari, atque gentilitas illustrari, præsertim post passionem, Apostolis ubique docentibus. Propter quod Christus dixit Judæis: Auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, et dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus. Hinc in Isaia ait Christus: Et nunc hæc dicit Dominus formans me ex utero servum sibi, ut reducam Jacob ad eum, et Israel non congregabitur. Et dixit Dominus mihi: Parum est ut sis servus mihi ad suscitandas tribus Jacob; dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ.
paras.en: By *they who see not* may also be understood sinners darkened by vices but predestined, such as Matthew, Zacchaeus and Magdalen, who were enlightened in heart by Christ; and by *they who see*, those whom pride so puffed up that they presumed to deride Christ's preaching. Thirdly, and more commonly, by *they who see not* are understood the Gentiles, who lacked the knowledge of the one true God; and by *they who see*, the Jews, instructed by the divine law. Now at the coming of Christ and from then on, the Jewish people began to be blinded and the Gentiles to be enlightened, above all after the Passion, as the Apostles taught everywhere[[Mark 16:20||]]. For which reason Christ said to the Jews: [[Matt 21:43|the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof|Auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, et dabitur genti facienti fructus ejus]]. Hence Christ says in Isaias: [[Is 49:5|And now saith the Lord, that formed me from the womb to be his servant, that I may bring back Jacob unto him, and Israel will not be gathered together|Et nunc hæc dicit Dominus formans me ex utero servum sibi, ut reducam Jacob ad eum, et Israel non congregabitur]]. And the Lord said to me: [[Is 49:6|It is a small thing that thou shouldst be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob|Parum est ut sis servus mihi ad suscitandas tribus Jacob]]; [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|dedi te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extremum terræ]].

paras.t: Et audierunt quidam ex Pharisæis qui cum ipso erant, hoc est, aliqui Pharisæorum exsistentium cum Jesu quando hæc protulit; et dixerunt ei, ex superbia murmurando: Numquid et nos cæci sumus ea cæcitate quam dicis futuram quibusdam videntibus? hoc est, Numquid et nos cor excæcatum habemus? Suspicabantur enim Pharisæi quod verum fuit, videlicet, quod Jesus more solito tetigit eos.
paras.en: [[9:40|And some of the Pharisees, who were with him, heard|Et audierunt quidam ex Pharisæis qui cum ipso erant]], that is, some of the Pharisees who were with Jesus when He uttered these words; [[9:40|and they said unto him|et dixerunt ei]], murmuring out of pride: [[9:40|Are we also blind|Numquid et nos cæci sumus]], with that blindness which you say is to come upon some who see? That is: Have we too a blinded heart? For the Pharisees suspected what was true, namely that Jesus, as was His way, was getting at them.

paras.t: Dixit eis Jesus: Si cæci essetis, hoc est, si humiliter agnosceretis insipientiam iniquitatesque vestras, et me doctorem justitiæ audiretis, non haberetis peccatum, quoniam vestrum imperfectum confitendo, mereremini indulgentiam et gratiam justificantem. Nunc vero dicitis, Quia, id est quod, videmus, hoc est, quia vos ipsos jactatis doctos ac sapientes, peccatum vestrum manet in vobis insanabile atque damnandum.
paras.en: [[9:41|Jesus said to them: If you were blind|Dixit eis Jesus: Si cæci essetis]], that is, if you humbly acknowledged your folly and your iniquities, and listened to me, the teacher of justice, [[9:41|you should not have sin|non haberetis peccatum]], since by confessing your imperfection you would merit pardon and justifying grace. [[9:41|But now you say: We see|Nunc vero dicitis, Quia videmus]] (*Quia* here means *that*), that is, because you boast yourselves learned and wise, [[9:41|Your sin remaineth|peccatum vestrum manet]] in you, incurable and to be condemned.

paras.t: Vel sic: Si cæci essetis, habendo ignorantiam invincibilem, non haberetis peccatum, quoniam talis ignorantia omnino excusat a culpa. Vel, Si cæci essetis, cæcitate seu ignorantia facti. Ignorantia vero juris affectata non excusat, sed auget peccatum. Ignorantia vero quæ contingit ex negligentia quadam, excusat a tanto, non a toto. Plus igitur peccat qui Scripturas cognoscit, quam alius, ceteris paribus, utpote si ignorantia alterius excusabilis est in toto vel in parte. Propter quod Jacobus protestatur: Scienti bonum et non facienti, peccatum est illi; et Petrus in secunda sua Canonica, Melius erat non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post agnitionem retrorsum reverti. Denique, servus sciens voluntatem domini sui, et non faciens, plagis vapulabit multis; qui autem non cognovit, et fecit digna plagis, vapulabit paucis.
paras.en: Or thus: *If you were blind*, having invincible ignorance, *you should not have sin*, since such ignorance excuses from fault altogether. Or: *If you were blind* with the blindness, that is, the ignorance, of fact [ignorance of a circumstance of the act, as distinct from ignorance of the law]. But affected ignorance of the law [ignorance a man chooses to keep, so as not to be bound] does not excuse, but increases the sin. And ignorance that comes about through some negligence excuses in part, not in whole. He therefore who knows the Scriptures sins more than another, other things being equal, inasmuch as the other's ignorance is excusable in whole or in part. For which reason James declares: [[Jas 4:17|him therefore who knoweth to do good and doth it not, to him it is sin|Scienti bonum et non facienti, peccatum est illi]]; and Peter in his second Canonical Epistle: [[2 Pet 2:21|it had been better for them not to have known the way of justice than, after they have known it, to turn back|Melius erat non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post agnitionem retrorsum reverti]]. And lastly, the servant who knows [[Luke 12:47|the will of his lord|voluntatem domini sui]] and does not do it [[Luke 12:47|shall be beaten with many stripes|plagis vapulabit multis]]; [[Luke 12:48|but he that knew not and did things worthy of stripes shall be beaten with few stripes|qui autem non cognovit, et fecit digna plagis, vapulabit paucis]].

10.title: Elucidatio capituli decimi: Amen, amen dico vobis, qui non intrat per ostium in ovile ovium.
10.title_en: Explanation of the tenth chapter: Amen, amen, I say to you: He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold.

paras.t: Sicut in fine præcedentis capituli patuit, Pharisæi jactabant se esse videntes, hoc est eruditos et dignos aliorum rectores; non tamen credebant in Christum, sed eum negabant. Idcirco Salvator in exordio hujus capituli pandit errorem ac falsitatem illorum per quamdam parabolam, quam ipsemet post pauca partim exponit.
paras.en: As appeared at the end of the preceding chapter, the Pharisees boasted that they were seeing, that is, learned and worthy to be the rulers of others; yet they did not believe in Christ, but denied him. Therefore at the beginning of this chapter the Saviour lays open their error and falsehood by a kind of parable, which he himself explains in part a little later.

paras.t: Ait ergo: Amen, amen dico vobis, o elati Pharisæi, qui non intrat per ostium in ovile ovium, sed ascendit aliunde, ille fur est et latro. Hoc totum in corporalibus rebus ita se habet. Sed ista exponenda sunt spiritualiter secundum sensum a Christo intentum. In locutione quippe parabolica, qualis est ista, sensus principalis ac litteralis non est qui immediate per verba significatur, sed qui per ipsas res vocibus designatas insinuatur.
paras.en: He says then: [[10:1|Amen, amen, I say to you|Amen, amen dico vobis]], O proud Pharisees, [[10:1|He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold|qui non intrat per ostium in ovile ovium]] [[10:1|but climbeth up another way, the same is a thief and a robber|sed ascendit aliunde, ille fur est et latro]]. All this holds thus in bodily things. But these words are to be expounded spiritually, according to the sense Christ intended. For in a parabolic way of speaking, such as this is, the principal and literal sense is not the one signified immediately by the words, but the one conveyed through the very things the words designate.

paras.t: Est igitur intellectus: Qui non intrat spirituali seu corporali introitu, per ostium, id est ordinate per Christum, videlicet secundum Christi voluntatem, licite ac honeste, vel per fidem catholicam atque individuam caritatem, in ovile ovium, hoc est in Ecclesiam, in congregationem fidelium, ad præsidendum gregi dominico, sed ascendit aliunde, id est, sibi ipsi assumit honorem, non vocatus a Deo tanquam Aaron. Idcirco ascendere dicitur, id est superbe intrare, per ambitionem propriam, per aliorum intrusionem, per simoniacam pravitatem, per corruptam et non canonicam electionem, non sequens Christi vestigia, de quo ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus, quod non semetipsum clarificavit ut pontifex fieret, sed qui locutus est ad eum: Tu es sacerdos in æternum.
paras.en: The meaning therefore is this: [[10:1|He that entereth not|Qui non intrat]], by a spiritual or bodily entry, [[10:1|by the door|per ostium]], that is, in due order through Christ, namely according to Christ's will, lawfully and honestly, or through the Catholic faith and undivided charity, [[10:1|into the sheepfold|in ovile ovium]], that is, into the Church, into the congregation of the faithful, to preside over the Lord's flock, [[10:1|but climbeth up another way|sed ascendit aliunde]], that is, takes the honour to himself, not called by God as Aaron was[[Heb 5:4||]]. Therefore he is said to climb up, that is, to enter proudly: by his own ambition, by the intrusion of others, by simoniacal wickedness [simony: the buying or selling of spiritual things, here of church offices], by a corrupt and uncanonical election; not following in the footsteps of Christ, of whom the Apostle says to the Hebrews that he [[Heb 5:5|did not glorify himself, that he might be made a high priest: but he that said unto him|non semetipsum clarificavit ut pontifex fieret, sed qui locutus est ad eum]]: [[Heb 5:6|Thou art a priest for ever|Tu es sacerdos in æternum]].

paras.t: Ille fur est et latro. Furem appellamus qui rapit aliena. Indignus ergo prælatus qui per Christum non intrat ad præsidendum fidelibus, vel quicumque deceptor falsusque doctor credentium, est fur: quoniam populum Dei subtrahit Deo, quoniam suo pestifero documento seu pravo exemplo ac aliis modis, avertit fideles a Deo, et subjugat eos sibi, atque in suum commodum redigit eos, bona eorum consumendo, eorum servitute utendo, et ipsos tanquam mancipia possidendo, quemadmodum de his Pharisæis loquitur Christus: Væ vobis, Scribæ et Pharisæi hypocritæ, quia comeditis domus viduarum. Hujusmodi itaque ascensor ovilis et ovium doctor, seu indignus prælatus et rector, gregem sibi conformat, et maximum damnum infert Christo, cujus prædilectam substantiam, pro qua ipse sanguinem fudit, taliter dissipat. Unde in Ecclesiastico legitur: Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea. Jeremias quoque: Quoniam, inquit, stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt, propterea omnis grex eorum dissipatus est. Denique talis etiam dicitur latro, quoniam gregem fidelium spiritualiter strangulat, vitam gratiæ suffocando in eis, atque diaboli devorationibus eos exponendo, imo ac mortem æternam ducendo. Inducit enim eos ad vitia, quibus occiditur anima, gratiam amittendo et dæmonum dentes incurrendo. Adversarius enim noster diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret.
paras.en: [[10:1|the same is a thief and a robber|Ille fur est et latro]]. We call him a thief who carries off what belongs to others. The unworthy prelate, then, who does not enter through Christ to preside over the faithful, or any deceiver and false teacher of believers, is a thief: since he steals God's people from God, since by his pestilent teaching or bad example and in other ways he turns the faithful away from God, and subjects them to himself, and turns them to his own advantage, consuming their goods, using their service, and possessing them like slaves; as Christ speaks of these Pharisees: [[Matt 23:14|Woe to you scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour the houses of widows|Væ vobis, Scribæ et Pharisæi hypocritæ, quia comeditis domus viduarum]]. Such a climber into the fold, then, and teacher of the sheep, or unworthy prelate and ruler, makes the flock like himself, and does the greatest harm to Christ, whose beloved possession, for which he shed his blood, he so squanders. Hence we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:2|As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers: and what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein.|Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea]]. Jeremias too: [[Jer 10:21|Because the pastors have done foolishly, and have not sought the Lord|Quoniam, inquit, stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt]]: [[Jer 10:21|and all their flock is scattered|propterea omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]]. Lastly, such a one is also called a robber, since he strangles the flock of the faithful spiritually, choking the life of grace in them, and exposing them to be devoured by the devil, nay leading them to eternal death. For he leads them into vices, by which the soul is slain, losing grace and falling between the teeth of the demons. For [[1 Pet 5:8|your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|Adversarius enim noster diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret]].

paras.t: Qui autem intrat præfatum ovile per ostium, id est per Christum, videlicet ordinate, caritative, humiliter, non quærens præesse vel dominari, sed prodesse et auxiliari, non quærens uti propria libertate, sed pro aliorum salute infatigabiliter laborare; pastor est ovium, hoc est fidelium, re et nomine, quoniam verbo et opere pascit, confortat et recreat eos. Tales pastores Deus promisit apud Jeremiam: Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina. Ad hanc veram pastoralem perfectionem hortatur princeps Apostolorum in prima sua epistola, dicens: Seniores, obsecro, pascite qui in vobis est gregem Dei, providentes non coacte, sed spontanee secundum Deum, non turpis lucri gratia, neque ut dominantes in cleris, sed forma gregis facti, et ex animo.
paras.en: [[10:2|But he that entereth in|Qui autem intrat]] the aforesaid fold [[10:2|by the door|per ostium]], that is, through Christ, namely in due order, charitably, humbly, not seeking to be over others or to rule, but to profit and help them, not seeking to use his own freedom, but to labour untiringly for the salvation of others, [[10:2|is the shepherd of the sheep|pastor est ovium]], that is, of the faithful, in fact and in name, since by word and deed he feeds, strengthens and refreshes them. Such shepherds God promised in Jeremias: [[Jer 3:15|I will give you pastors according to my own heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine|Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum, et pascent vos scientia et doctrina]]. To this true pastoral perfection the prince of the Apostles exhorts in his first Epistle, saying: [[1 Pet 5:1|The ancients therefore that are among you, I beseech|Seniores, obsecro]], [[1 Pet 5:2|Feed the flock of God which is among you|pascite qui in vobis est gregem Dei]], [[1 Pet 5:2|taking care of it, not by constraint but willingly, according to God: not for filthy lucre's sake|providentes non coacte, sed spontanee secundum Deum, non turpis lucri gratia]], [[1 Pet 5:3|Neither as lording it over the clergy but being made a pattern of the flock from the heart.|neque ut dominantes in cleris, sed forma gregis facti, et ex animo]].

paras.t: Huic tam fructuoso pastori ostiarius aperit, id est, Spiritus Sanctus divinas veritates revelat, modum regiminis manifestat, et de omnibus necessariis instruit. Unde de ipso infra habetur: Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem. Ipse igitur Spiritus Sanctus admittit, vel potius introducit, timoratum ac diligentem pastorem in sanctuarium sapientiæ sempiternæ, ut discat et sciat quomodo oporteat se conversari in domo Dei; et illic dat ei gustare multitudinem dulcedinis suæ, ita ut rediens ad gregem dominicum sibi commissum, eructet illis memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis divinæ. Sicque de plenitudine sibi collata illuminat et accendit corda suorum. Hac apertione Spiritus Sancti maxime indiget omnis pastor, et tanto amplius, quanto pluribus præest. Quum enim nemo sui ipsius possit operari salutem sine speciali atque continuo auxilio Spiritus Sancti, quomodo poterit suam et aliorum operari salutem, sine ingenti, singulari jugique ope Paracleti? Propterea oportet pastorem frequenter nimis ad Deum recurrere, ejus auxilium cum humili prostratione requirere, ut in omnibus dirigatur, moveatur, et reguletur ab ipso, itemque ut Spiritus Sanctus corda subditorum docibilia faciat, tangat, gubernet. Væ ergo dissolutis et intimoratis prælatis, qui se ad exteriora impudenter effundunt, qui non ponderant quam grave onus ipsis impositum sit, neque præcogitant quam Christo pro se suisque ovibus tribuant rationem. Isti non pensant illud Sapientiæ: Judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet. Ideo bene ait Chrysostomus: Quis est qui desiderat prælationem et curam animarum, nisi qui non timet judicium Dei?
paras.en: [[10:3|To him|Huic]], so fruitful a shepherd, [[10:3|the porter openeth|ostiarius aperit]], that is, the Holy Ghost reveals divine truths, shows the way of governing, and instructs him in all things needful. Hence it is said of him further on: [[John 16:13|when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth|Quum venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem]]. The Holy Ghost himself, then, admits, or rather leads in, the God-fearing and diligent shepherd into the sanctuary of everlasting wisdom, that he may learn and know [[1 Tim 3:15|how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God|quomodo oporteat se conversari in domo Dei]] [Denis: “how he ought to behave himself in the house of God”]; and there gives him to taste the multitude of his sweetness[[Ps 30:20||]], so that, returning to the Lord's flock committed to him, he may utter to them the memory of the abundance of the divine sweetness[[Ps 144:7||]]. And so from the fulness granted him he enlightens and kindles the hearts of his people. Of this opening by the Holy Ghost every shepherd has the greatest need, and the more so the more people he is over. For since no one can work out his own salvation without the special and continual help of the Holy Ghost, how will he be able to work out his own salvation and that of others without the great, singular and constant aid of the Paraclete? Therefore the shepherd must very often run back to God and seek his help with humble prostration, that he may be directed, moved and ruled by him in all things, and likewise that the Holy Ghost may make the hearts of his subjects teachable, touch them and govern them. Woe therefore to lax prelates without the fear of God, who shamelessly pour themselves out on outward things, who do not weigh how heavy a burden is laid upon them, nor consider beforehand what account they are to render to Christ for themselves and their sheep[[Rom 14:12||]][[Heb 13:17||]]. These men do not ponder that saying of Wisdom: [[Wis 6:6|a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule|Judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet]]. So Chrysostom says well: Who is it that desires prelacy and the care of souls, but one who does not fear the judgment of God?

paras.t: Et oves vocem ejus audiunt, id est, electi subditi, qui sunt oves per prædestinationem æternam, talis pastoris doctrinam suscipiunt ac sequuntur. Humiliter enim et devote audiunt et observant verbum sui prælati tanquam vicarii Christi: quemadmodum Apostolus in suis epistolis sæpius gloriatur in Domino de suis discipulis seu populis a se conversis, quod suam prædicationem cum omni attentione et reverentia perceperunt. Quod utique oportet omnem subditum diligenter implere, quoniam prælatis loquitur Christus apud Lucam: Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit.
paras.en: [[10:3|and the sheep hear his voice|Et oves vocem ejus audiunt]], that is, the elect subjects, who are sheep by eternal predestination, receive and follow the teaching of such a shepherd. For they hear humbly and devoutly and keep the word of their prelate as Christ's vicar: as the Apostle in his Epistles often glories in the Lord about his disciples, or the peoples converted by him, that they received his preaching with all attention and reverence[[2 Cor 9:2||]][[Col 2:5||]][[1 Thess 1:2||]][[1 Thess 2:13||]]. Which every subject must indeed fulfil diligently, since Christ says to prelates in Luke: [[Luke 10:16|He that heareth you heareth me: and he that despiseth you despiseth me|Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit]].

paras.t: Et proprias oves vocat nominatim, id est, singulos subditorum suorum determinate cognoscit, ad meliora hortatur, ad felicitatem invitat, omnium mores pensando, quid singulis expediat perpendendo, cunctis familiariter condescendendo, unicuique secundum propriam capacitatem ac indigentiam providendo, subveniendo et influendo, quemadmodum Salomon admonet in libro Proverbiorum: Diligenter agnosce vultum pecoris tui, tuosque greges considera. Quemadmodum enim medicus corporum dispositiones, complexiones, atque morborum diversitates in languido pensat, quatenus unicuique medicamentum suæ dispositioni ac morbo proportionatum apponat (quod enim uni prodesset, obesset alteri); sic prælatus et pastor, quum sit medicus animarum, attendere debet inclinationes, motus et studia singulorum, sicque unumquemque a malo retrahere et ad virtutes provehere per media aptiora: quod non est parum difficile. Propter quod convenienter ait Gregorius: Ars artium est regimen animarum. Et magna valde perfectio, exercitatio, unctio, discretio, exigitur ad bonum prælatum. Unde in Deuteronomio loquitur Moyses: Date ex vobis sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribubus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes.
paras.en: [[10:3|And he calleth his own sheep by name|Et proprias oves vocat nominatim]], that is, he knows each of his subjects individually, exhorts them to better things, invites them to happiness, weighing the ways of all, considering what is expedient for each, condescending familiarly to all, providing for each according to his own capacity and need, helping him and pouring into him; as Solomon admonishes in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 27:23|Be diligent to know the countenance of thy cattle, and consider thy own flocks:|Diligenter agnosce vultum pecoris tui, tuosque greges considera]]. For as a physician of bodies weighs the dispositions, complexions and different diseases in the sick man, so as to give each a medicine proportioned to his disposition and disease (for what would profit one would harm another), so the prelate and shepherd, since he is the physician of souls, must attend to the inclinations, impulses and pursuits of each, and so draw each away from evil and advance him to virtue by the fittest means: which is no small difficulty. Hence Gregory fittingly says: The government of souls is the art of arts. And very great perfection, practice, unction and discretion are required for a good prelate. Hence in Deuteronomy Moses says: [[Deut 1:13|Let me have from among you wise and understanding men, and such whose conversation is approved among your tribes, that I may appoint them your rulers|Date ex vobis sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribubus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes]] [Denis: “Give from among you wise and understanding men … and I will appoint them your rulers”].

paras.t: Et educit eas, de via ad patriam, de carne ad spiritum. Educit insuper eas ad pascua alimoniæ spiritualis, ad panem vitæ et intellectus, ad panem sacramentalem, ad divinorum contemplationem.
paras.en: [[10:3|and leadeth them out|Et educit eas]], from the way to the fatherland, from the flesh to the spirit. He leads them out besides to the pastures of spiritual nourishment, to [[Ecclus 15:3|the bread of life and understanding|panem vitæ et intellectus]], to the sacramental bread, to the contemplation of divine things.

paras.t: Et quum proprias oves emiserit, id est, prædicto modo eduxerit, atque de tenebris ignorantiæ et peccati in lucem veritatis ac splendorem virtutum transtulerit, ante eas vadit, id est, in via Dei ipsas exemplariter præit, et in virtuosa conversatione excedit, faciendo quod docet, et non verbo dumtaxat, sed opere quoque viam monstrando, quemadmodum ad Timotheum Paulus ait: Esto exemplum fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate; profectus tuus manifestus sit omnibus: hæc enim faciens, te ipsum salvum facies, et eos qui te audiunt.
paras.en: [[10:4|And when he hath let out his own sheep|Et quum proprias oves emiserit]], that is, has led them out in the way just said, and brought them over from the darkness of ignorance and sin into the light of truth and the splendour of the virtues, [[10:4|he goeth before them|ante eas vadit]], that is, he goes before them by his example in the way of God, and excels in a virtuous life, doing what he teaches, and showing the way not by word only but by deed as well; as Paul says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 4:12|be thou an example of the faithful, in word, in conversation, in charity|Esto exemplum fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate]]; [[1 Tim 4:15|thy profiting may be manifest to all|profectus tuus manifestus sit omnibus]]: [[1 Tim 4:16|in doing this thou shalt both save thyself and them that hear thee|hæc enim faciens, te ipsum salvum facies, et eos qui te audiunt]].

paras.t: Denique, quum prælatus sit quasi signum ad quod omnium subditorum oculi diriguntur, ideo nihil tantum ædificat subditos, vel tantum confert ad omnem profectum virtutum, ut bona et irreprehensibilis vita pastoris. Frequens namque recursus et quotidianus adspectus in habitum vertitur, atque in cordibus subditorum veram in virtutibus constantiam operatur. Oportet ergo prælatum in virtute et sapientia stabilem esse, ne passionibus agitetur, ne personarum acceptor sit, ne unum præ alio palpet vel tribulet, ne privato amore vel odio corrumpatur; sed Deum semper præ oculis habeat, jugiter formidet, ne per suam imperfectionem aut injustitiam aliquem ex sibi commissis scandalizet. Prælatus quippe est judex et caput sive principium gregis sui. Judex autem, secundum Philosophum, debet esse quasi animata justitia vivaque lex, nusquam ab æquitatis tramite devians. Primum quoque in omni ordine, est mensura et regula posteriorum. Mensuram vero et regulam necesse est esse uniformem ac simplicem: aliter non possent alia per eam mensurari ac regulari. Sit ergo prælatus uniformis, fixus et simplex, non simulator et callidus, sed mitis et humilis.
paras.en: Lastly, since the prelate is as it were a sign to which the eyes of all his subjects are directed, nothing so edifies his subjects, or contributes so much to all progress in virtue, as the good and irreprehensible life of the shepherd. For frequent recourse to it and daily sight of it turn into habit, and work true constancy in virtue in the hearts of the subjects. The prelate must therefore be steady in virtue and wisdom, so as not to be driven by passions, not to be a respecter of persons, not to flatter one or harass one more than another, not to be corrupted by private love or hatred; but let him always have God before his eyes, and fear continually lest by his imperfection or injustice he scandalize any of those committed to him. For the prelate is the judge, and the head or principle, of his flock. Now the judge, according to the Philosopher [Aristotle, Ethics V], ought to be as it were justice alive and a living law, never turning aside from the path of equity. Also the first in every order is the measure and rule of those after it. And a measure and rule must be uniform and simple: otherwise other things could not be measured and ruled by it. Let the prelate therefore be uniform, steady and simple, not a dissembler and crafty, but meek and humble.

paras.t: Et oves illum sequuntur, tanquam ducem prædignum, id est, operibus illius se conformant, ejusque verbis obtemperant, quemadmodum ad Hebræos docet Apostolus: Obedite præpositis vestris, et subjacete illis; ipsi enim pervigilant tanquam rationem pro animabus vestris reddituri. Bonus ergo pastor bonas efficit oves, oviumque vitia et defectus maxime accidunt ex negligentia atque insufficientia præsidentis. Propter quod maximum Dei donum est, habere virtuosum prælatum. Unde videmus quod in veteri Testamento, tempore judicum et regum, quando judex vel rex bonus fuit, populus Israel Domino ministravit; sed rege vel judice impie conversante, populus quoque communiter vixit inique, insistendo frequenter idololatriæ. Quia sciunt vocem ejus, id est, doctrinam ejus per approbationem cognoscunt.
paras.en: [[10:4|and the sheep follow him|Et oves illum sequuntur]], as a most worthy leader, that is, they conform themselves to his works and comply with his words; as the Apostle teaches the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:17|Obey your prelates and be subject to them. For they watch as being to render an account of your souls|Obedite præpositis vestris, et subjacete illis; ipsi enim pervigilant tanquam rationem pro animabus vestris reddituri]]. The good shepherd, then, makes good sheep; and the vices and failings of the sheep come chiefly from the negligence and inadequacy of the one who presides. Therefore it is a very great gift of God to have a virtuous prelate. Hence we see that in the Old Testament, in the time of the judges and kings, when the judge or king was good, the people of Israel served the Lord; but when the king or judge lived wickedly, the people too commonly lived wickedly, often giving themselves to idolatry. [[10:4|because they know his voice|Quia sciunt vocem ejus]], that is, they recognize his teaching by approving it.

paras.t: Alienum autem, id est seductorem pestiferumque doctorem, schismaticum sive hæreticum, vel impium Christianum, non sequuntur, id est, ejus doctrinis non acquiescunt, nec opera sequuntur; sed fugiunt ab eo, id est, animo illum detestantur, vel etiam interdum corpore se elongant ab ipso, ne cum perverso pervertantur. Qui enim tetigerit picem, inquinatur. Et Apostolus: Exite, inquit, de medio illorum, et immundum ne tetigeritis. Quia non noverunt per approbationem et imitationem, vocem alienorum, id est verba fallacium.
paras.en: [[10:5|But a stranger|Alienum autem]], that is, a seducer and pestilent teacher, a schismatic or heretic, or a wicked Christian, [[10:5|they follow not|non sequuntur]], that is, they do not assent to his teachings nor follow his works; [[10:5|but fly from him|sed fugiunt ab eo]], that is, they detest him in mind, or even at times keep away from him in body, lest with the perverse they be perverted[[Ps 17:27||]]. For [[Ecclus 13:1|He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled|Qui enim tetigerit picem, inquinatur]]. And the Apostle: [[2 Cor 6:17|Go out from among them|Exite, inquit, de medio illorum]], he says, [[2 Cor 6:17|and touch not the unclean thing|et immundum ne tetigeritis]]. [[10:5|because they know not|Quia non noverunt]], by approving and imitating, [[10:5|the voice of strangers|vocem alienorum]], that is, the words of deceivers.

paras.t: Totum hoc intelligendum est de ovibus, non solum secundum præsentem justitiam, sed et secundum prædestinationem divinam, et de auditu seu fuga vel cognitione finali. Certum est enim quod multi electi ad tempus errant, et hæreticorum vel aliorum deceptorum doctrinas advertunt; sed finaliter pœnitent, et in Christi sermone diem claudunt extremum. Similiter multi præsciti, ad tempus verba bonorum advertunt pastorum, et alienorum vocem abhorrent; sed non perseverant usque in finem, nec implent illud Apostoli: Doctrinis variis et peregrinis nolite abduci; et, Optimum est gratia stabiliri cor. Vel loquitur Christus de ovibus formaliter, hoc est, in quantum sunt oves, non materialiter. Formaliter enim de eis loquendo, non errant, quemadmodum arbor bona non potest facere fructus malos.
paras.en: All this is to be understood of the sheep not only according to present justice, but also according to divine predestination, and of hearing, or flight, or knowledge in the end. For it is certain that many of the elect err for a time, and give ear to the teachings of heretics or other deceivers; but in the end they repent, and close their last day in the word of Christ. Likewise many of the foreknown [that is, those foreseen to be lost] give ear for a time to the words of good shepherds and shrink from the voice of strangers; but they do not persevere to the end, nor fulfil that saying of the Apostle: [[Heb 13:9|Be not led away with various and strange doctrines|Doctrinis variis et peregrinis nolite abduci]]; and, [[Heb 13:9|it is best that the heart be established with grace|Optimum est gratia stabiliri cor]]. Or Christ speaks of the sheep formally, that is, inasmuch as they are sheep, not materially. For speaking of them formally, they do not err, just as [[Matt 7:18|A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit|arbor bona malos fructus]].

paras.t: Hoc proverbium, id est similitudinem istam, vel sermonem hunc parabolicum, dixit eis Jesus. Illi autem Pharisæi non cognoverunt quid loqueretur eis, id est, quid per verba prædicta significaret. Certi enim fuerunt quod intentio ejus finalis non erat de pecoribus. Dixit ergo eis iterum Jesus, qui novit ignorantiam illorum. Exposuit ergo proverbium istud pro parte. Expositio namque non intelligentibus est necessaria.
paras.en: [[10:6|This proverb|Hoc proverbium]], that is, this likeness, or this parabolic speech, [[10:6|Jesus spoke to them|dixit eis Jesus]]. [[10:6|But they understood not what he spoke|Illi autem Pharisæi non cognoverunt quid loqueretur]] to them, the Pharisees, that is, what he meant by the words said. For they were sure that his final intention was not about cattle. [[10:7|Jesus therefore said to them again|Dixit ergo eis iterum Jesus]], who knew their ignorance. So he explained this proverb in part. For an explanation is necessary for those who do not understand.

paras.t: Amen, amen dico vobis, quia ego sum ostium ovium, hoc est porta, secundum proprietatem quamdam, per quam electi intrant in societatem Ecclesiæ militantis, et deinceps ad consortium Ecclesiæ triumphantis. Christus quoque est ostium per quod intramus ad Patrem, nunc per fidem et gratiam, tunc vero per speciem. Propter quod ait: Ego sum via, et veritas et vita; nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me. Itemque Apostolus: Per ipsum, inquit, accessum habemus ad Patrem; et rursus, Per ipsum offeramus hostiam laudis Deo semper. Christus ergo est ostium, quia per ejus Baptismum, per ejus passionem et gratiam, per ejus auxilium, incorporamur Ecclesiæ, ad patriam devenimus, Deo immediate unimur. Propterea Petrus testatur: Neque enim datum est hominibus aliud nomen sub cœlo, in quo oporteat eos salvos fieri. Dicitur autem Christus ostium, per similitudinem quamdam, quomodo dicitur agnus, leo, petra, lucerna.
paras.en: [[10:7|Amen, amen, I say to you, I am the door of the sheep|Amen, amen dico vobis, quia ego sum ostium ovium]], that is, the gate, by a certain likeness, through which the elect enter into the fellowship of the Church militant, and thereafter into the company of the Church triumphant. Christ is also the door by which we enter to the Father, now by faith and grace, but then by sight. Therefore he says: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me|Ego sum via, et veritas et vita; nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me]]. And the Apostle: [[Eph 2:18|by him we have access both in one Spirit to the Father|Per ipsum, inquit, accessum habemus ad Patrem]][[Rom 5:2||]], he says; and again, [[Heb 13:15|By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise always to God|Per ipsum offeramus hostiam laudis Deo semper]]. Christ, then, is the door, because by his Baptism, by his passion and grace, by his help, we are incorporated into the Church, come to the fatherland, and are united to God immediately. Therefore Peter bears witness: [[Acts 4:12|there is no other name under heaven given to men, whereby we must be saved|Neque enim datum est hominibus aliud nomen sub cœlo, in quo oporteat eos salvos fieri]]. Christ is called the door by a certain likeness, as he is called lamb[[John 1:29||]], lion[[Apoc 5:5||]], rock[[1 Cor 10:4||]], lamp[[Apoc 21:23||]].

paras.t: Omnes quotquot venerunt, fures sunt: et latrones. Non absolute de omnibus loquitur Christus, quia superius laudavit Joannem Baptistam et Moysen: sed de quibusdam pseudoprophetis qui non longe ante Christi adventum venerunt, quales fuerunt Theodas et Judas Galilæus, de quibus scribitur in Actibus Apostolorum; vel de omnibus qui sine Christo, hoc est sine Dei verbo, venerunt, non missi a Deo, sed proprio sensu se ingerentes. De qualibus Dominus ait per Jeremiam: Ipsi currebant, et ego non misi eos. Sed non audierunt eos oves, id est, finaliter ipsis non consenserunt, quamvis forte ad tempus decepta sint.
paras.en: [[10:8|All others, as many as have come, are thieves and robbers|Omnes quotquot venerunt, fures sunt: et latrones]]. Christ does not speak absolutely of all, since above he praised John the Baptist and Moses[[John 5:35||]][[John 5:46||]]: but of certain false prophets who came not long before Christ's coming, such as were Theodas and Judas of Galilee, of whom it is written in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 5:36||]][[Acts 5:37||]]; or of all who came without Christ, that is, without the Word of God, not sent by God, but thrusting themselves forward by their own mind. Of such the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 23:21|I did not send prophets, yet they ran|Ipsi currebant, et ego non misi eos]] [Denis: “They ran, and I did not send them”]. [[10:8|and the sheep heard them not|Sed non audierunt eos oves]], that is, did not finally consent to them, though perhaps they were deceived for a time.

paras.t: Ego sum ostium (sicut nunc dictum est). Per me si quis introierit, id est, qui secundum doctrinam et vitam meam conversatus fuerit, qui per fidem et gratiam meam congregationi fidelium se junxerit, si quis mihi intima caritate inhæserit, salvabitur, hoc est, æternam beatitudinem consequetur, nuncque a peccatis purgabitur: aliter Christus non esset Salvator. Unde in Actibus Petrus disseruit: Per gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi credimus salvari.
paras.en: [[10:9|I am the door|Ego sum ostium]] (as has just been said). [[10:9|By me, if any man enter in|Per me si quis introierit]], that is, whoever has lived according to my teaching and life, whoever has joined himself to the congregation of the faithful by faith and my grace, whoever has cleaved to me with inward charity, [[10:9|he shall be saved|salvabitur]], that is, he shall obtain eternal beatitude, and is now cleansed from sins: otherwise Christ would not be the Saviour. Hence Peter declared in the Acts: [[Acts 15:11|by the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, we believe to be saved|Per gratiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi credimus salvari]].

paras.t: Et ingredietur, et egredietur, id est, in latitudine caritatis et spiritus libertate versabitur, quia lex Christi est lex amoris, et ubi Spiritus Domini, ibi libertas. Itaque ingredietur, redeundo ad propriam conscientiam, examinando se ipsum, atque interioribus virtutum theologicarum actibus insistendo; et egredietur de habitu virtuoso in opus meritorium, de cognitione ad operationem, de via ad patriam. Egredietur quoque ad proximos, illis misericorditer condescendendo, consulendo, subveniendo, quemadmodum dicit Apostolus: Alter alterius onera portate; et, Non quæ sua sunt singuli considerantes, sed quæ aliorum. Egredietur demum quotidie, levando se super se, ut sit conversatio sua in cœlis, omnibusque terrenis ac sensibilibus rebus transcensis, sola cœlestia, spiritualia et æterna contempletur, amet, recogitet, omnia arbitrans ut stercora propter eminentem scientiam Christi.
paras.en: [[10:9|and he shall go in and go out|Et ingredietur, et egredietur]], that is, he shall live in the breadth of charity and in liberty of spirit, since the law of Christ is the law of love, and [[2 Cor 3:17|where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty|ubi Spiritus Domini, ibi libertas]]. So he shall go in, returning to his own conscience, examining himself, and applying himself to the inward acts of the theological virtues; and he shall go out from the virtuous habit into meritorious work, from knowledge to action, from the way to the fatherland. He shall go out also to his neighbours, condescending to them in mercy, counselling and helping them; as the Apostle says: [[Gal 6:2|Bear ye one another's burdens|Alter alterius onera portate]]; and, [[Phil 2:4|Each one not considering the things that are his own, but those that are other men's.|Non quæ sua sunt singuli considerantes, sed quæ aliorum]]. He shall go out, lastly, daily, lifting himself above himself[[Lam 3:28||]], that his conversation may be in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], and, passing beyond all earthly and sensible things, may contemplate, love and ponder heavenly, spiritual and eternal things alone, counting all things as dung for the excellent knowledge of Christ[[Phil 3:8||]].

paras.t: Et pascua, id est spiritualia alimenta, copiose inveniet in præsenti et in futuro. Nunc enim quotidie reficitur corpore et sanguine Salvatoris, incremento virtutum, consolatione interna, rivis sapientiæ, ceterisque donis et charismatibus Spiritus Sancti. His bonis anima se ipsam diligenter custodiens, ut Sponso suo cœlesti se incontaminatam exhibeat, feliciter impinguatur et confortatur, ita ut cibum fastidiat corporalem omnemque consolationem carnalem et sæcularem. Porro in patria inveniet pascua illa uberrima, quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt: ubi Deus est omnia in omnibus, omnesque Beati de ejus fruitione contentantur et superdulcissime satiantur.
paras.en: [[10:9|and shall find pastures|et pascua inveniet]], that is, spiritual food, abundantly, in the present and in the future. For now he is fed daily with the body and blood of the Saviour, with increase of virtues, with inward consolation, with streams of wisdom, and with the other gifts and charisms of the Holy Ghost. With these goods the soul that guards itself diligently, so as to show itself undefiled to its heavenly Spouse, is happily fattened and strengthened, so that it loathes bodily food and all fleshly and worldly consolation. Further, in the fatherland it shall find those richest pastures [[1 Cor 2:9|That eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man|quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt]][[Is 64:4||]]: where [[1 Cor 15:28|God may be all in all|Deus est omnia in omnibus]], and all the Blessed are content with the enjoyment of him and are filled with surpassing sweetness.

paras.t: Fur non venit, id est, seductor indignusve pastor non accedit fideles, nisi ut furetur, hoc est, oves Christi subtrahat Christo, et officium sibi indebitum præsumptuose usurpet. Quamvis enim dicat se hoc non intendere, tamen male agendo et debita omittendo, hoc facit. Et mactet, et perdat, id est, spiritualiter occidat, atque ad sempiternum perducat interitum. Tales sunt negligentes prælati, carnales, avari et ambitiosi: quibus Dominus ait per Ezechielem: Væ pastoribus qui pascebant semetipsos. Lac comedebatis, et lana operiebamini, gregem autem meum non pascebatis; ego Dominus requiram gregem meum de manu eorum.
paras.en: [[10:10|The thief cometh not|Fur non venit]], that is, the seducer or unworthy shepherd does not approach the faithful, [[10:10|but for to steal|nisi ut furetur]], that is, to steal the sheep of Christ from Christ, and presumptuously to usurp an office not due to him. For though he may say that he does not intend this, yet by doing evil and leaving undone what he ought, he does it. [[10:10|and to kill and to destroy|Et mactet, et perdat]], that is, to slay spiritually, and to bring to everlasting ruin. Such are negligent prelates, carnal, avaricious and ambitious: to whom the Lord says by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 34:2|Woe to the shepherds of Israel, that fed themselves|Væ pastoribus qui pascebant semetipsos]]. [[Ezech 34:3|You ate the milk, and you clothed yourselves with the wool, and you killed that which was fat: but my flock you did not feed|Lac comedebatis, et lana operiebamini, gregem autem meum non pascebatis]]; [[Ezech 34:10|I will require my flock at their hand|requiram gregem meum de manu eorum]].

paras.t: Ego veni, in mundum per incarnationem, et in publicum per prædicationem, ut oves vitam gratiæ habeant in præsenti, et abundantius habeant, id est, plenam felicitatem seu vitam gloriæ sortiantur in patria. De qua abundantia abundantique gloria cecinit Isaias: Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea, gratiarum actio et vox laudis; itemque, Lætitia sempiterna super capita eorum, gaudium et lætitiam obtinebunt, et fugiet dolor et gemitus.
paras.en: [[10:10|I am come|Ego veni]], into the world by the incarnation, and into public by preaching, [[10:10|that they may have life|ut oves vitam gratiæ habeant]], the sheep, the life of grace, in the present, [[10:10|and may have it more abundantly|et abundantius habeant]], that is, may obtain full happiness, or the life of glory, in the fatherland. Of this abundance and abundant glory Isaias sang: [[Is 51:3|Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of praise|Gaudium et lætitia invenietur in ea, gratiarum actio et vox laudis]]; and again, [[Is 51:11|joy everlasting shall be upon their heads, they shall obtain joy and gladness, sorrow and mourning shall flee away|Lætitia sempiterna super capita eorum, gaudium et lætitiam obtinebunt, et fugiet dolor et gemitus]][[Is 35:10||]].

20.title: PROSECUTIO EXPOSITIONIS PRÆSENTIS VICESIMI CAPITULI : QUUM SERO ESSET DIE ILLA, UNA SABBATORUM.
20.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this twentieth chapter: When it was late that same day, the first of the week

paras.t: HOC loco describit Evangelista quintam Christi apparitionem, factam in die Paschæ, et etiam sextam, quæ facta est præsente Thoma, in octava Paschæ. Quinquies enim apparuit Christus in die Paschæ : Primo, Magdalenæ, quemadmodum in Marco legitur : Surgens Jesus mane prima sabbati, apparuit primo Mariæ Magdalene. Secundo, mulieribus redeuntibus a sepulcro, juxta illud Matthæi : Ecce Jesus occurrit illis, dicens, Avete. Tertio, Petro, quamvis locus ignoretur; creditur tamen quod redeunti a monumento. Quarto, duobus discipulis euntibus in Emmaus, secundum quod recitat Lucas. Quinto, undecim Apostolis in conclavi, sicut nunc contestatur Joannes.
paras.en: In this place the Evangelist describes the fifth appearance of Christ, made on the day of the Pasch, and also the sixth, which was made with Thomas present, on the octave of the Pasch. For Christ appeared five times on the day of the Pasch. First, to Magdalen, as is read in Mark: [[Mark 16:9|But he rising early the first day of the week, appeared first to Mary Magdalen|Surgens Jesus mane prima sabbati, apparuit primo Mariæ Magdalene]]. Second, to the women returning from the sepulchre, according to that of Matthew: [[Matt 28:9|behold, Jesus met them, saying: All hail|Ecce Jesus occurrit illis, dicens, Avete]]. Third, to Peter[[Luke 24:34||]][[1 Cor 15:5||]], though the place is unknown; yet it is believed that it was as he returned from the tomb. Fourth, to the two disciples going to Emmaus, as Luke recounts[[Luke 24:13||]]. Fifth, to the eleven Apostles in the closed room, as John now bears witness.

paras.t: Quum sero esset, hoc est hora vespertina, et nocte incipiente, die illa, in qua apparuit Magdalenæ, una sabbatorum, id est, quæ dies fuit una dierum illius hebdomadæ, qui omnes dicebantur sabbata, quia festivi, et fores, id est januæ, essent clausæ, ubi erant discipuli, hoc est Apostoli, et etiam alii, secundum Lucam, congregati propter metum Judæorum : in quo patet eorum infirmitas, qui timebant eos qui corpus potuerunt occidere. Dicunt quidam, quod Apostoli erant dispersi in die propter metum Judæorum, sed de sero conveniebant ad locum unum. Evangelista vero nunc dicit, quod erant congregati propter metum prædictum. Lucas quoque habet, quod mulieres regressæ a monumento, nuntiaverunt quæ audierunt illis undecim : quod fuit clara die, quia post hoc Petrus et Joannes cucurrerunt ad monumentum. Ex quibus patet, quod discipuli etiam in die sederunt collecti januis clausis, propter metum Judæorum : imo minus audebant exire diebus quam noctibus.
paras.en: [[20:19|Now when it was late|Cum ergo sero esset]], that is, at the evening hour, as night was beginning, [[20:19|the same day|die illo]], on which He appeared to Magdalen, [[20:19|the first of the week|una sabbatorum]], that is, the day which was one of the days of that week, all of which were called sabbaths because they were festal, [[20:19|and the doors were shut, where the disciples were|et fores essent clausæ, ubi erant discipuli]], that is, the Apostles, and others too, according to Luke[[Luke 24:33||]], [[20:19|gathered together, for fear of the Jews|congregati propter metum Judæorum]]: in which their weakness is plain, who feared those who could kill the body[[Matt 10:28||]]. Some say that the Apostles were scattered by day for fear of the Jews, but in the evening came together to one place. But the Evangelist now says that they were gathered together for the said fear. Luke also has it that the women, returning from the tomb, told what they had heard to the eleven[[Luke 24:9||]]: which was in broad day, since after this Peter and John ran to the tomb[[Luke 24:12||]]. From which it is plain that the disciples sat gathered with the doors shut even by day, for fear of the Jews: indeed they dared go out less by day than by night.

paras.t: Venit Jesus ostio clauso, per penetrationem dimensionum. Corpora enim glorificata omnia penetrant per dotem subtilitatis, secundum quosdam : non tamen sine grandi miraculo, prout Thomas super quartum Sententiarum satis demonstrat. Quemadmodum igitur Jesus exivit uterum Matris, ea integra remanente, sic intravit et exiit domum non apertam, divina omnipotente virtute. Et stetit in medio discipulorum. Ipse namque est mediator, doctor reconciliatorque noster, ideo competebat ei esse in medio, sicut et ante passionem locutus est : Ego in medio vestrum sum. Magister quippe virtutum, medium semper elegit, quia in medio virtus consistit. Quomodo autem factum sit quod nunc refert Joannes, Lucas plenius edocet : quo legitur, quod quum Jesus cognitus fuisset a duobus discipulis in fractione panis, et disparuisset, illi surgentes regressi sunt in Jerusalem eadem hora, inveneruntque undecim congregatos, et eos qui cum illis erant, quibus dixerunt quomodo Jesus apparuisset eis in via, et qualiter eum cognoverunt : quibus ista narrantibus, venit Jesus, et stetit in medio discipulorum.
paras.en: [[20:19|Jesus came|venit Jesus]] with the door shut, by penetration of dimensions [[that is, two bodies occupying the same place]]. For glorified bodies penetrate all things by the endowment of subtlety, according to some: yet not without a great miracle, as Thomas amply shows on the fourth book of the Sentences. As therefore Jesus came forth from His Mother's womb while she remained intact, so He entered and left the unopened house by the almighty power of God. [[20:19|And stood in the midst|et stetit in medio]] of the disciples. For He is our mediator, teacher and reconciler, and so it befitted Him to be in the midst, as He also said before the passion: [[Luke 22:27|I am in the midst of you|Ego in medio vestrum sum]]. For the Master of the virtues always chose the mean, since virtue consists in the mean. How what John now relates came about, Luke teaches more fully: where it is read that when Jesus had been known by the two disciples in the breaking of bread and had vanished[[Luke 24:30||]], they rose up and returned to Jerusalem the same hour, and found the eleven gathered together, [[Luke 24:33|and those that were with them|et eos qui cum illis erant]], to whom they told how Jesus had appeared to them on the way and how they knew Him[[Luke 24:35||]]: and as they were telling these things, Jesus came and stood in the midst of the disciples[[Luke 24:36||]].

paras.t: Et dixit eis : Pax vobis. Quod docuit Christus, hoc fecit. Præcepit autem discipulis : In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite : Pax huic domui. Hinc ipse domum ingrediens in qua erant carissimi sui electissimique discipuli, ait : Pax vobis. Rursus, sic eos salutavit, quoniam paulo ante, in qua nocte tradebatur, disseruit : Pacem relinquo vobis. Quod igitur tunc reliquit, nunc attulit, dedit et auxit. Discipuli quoque pace maxime indigebant, quoniam multipliciter conturbati erant, ac territi, videlicet propter præteritam Christi passionem, propter Judæorum crudelitatem, et proprii cordis quamdam hæsitationem de Christi resurrectione, de cujus veritate nondum fuerant roborati. Insuper sic salutavit discipulos, quoniam pax est maximum bonum, omnique Christiano præcipue appetendum : per quam homines fiunt filii Dei, quemadmodum scriptum est : Beati pacifici, quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur. Propter quod ait Dionysius, quod omnia appetunt pacem, et propter hanc agunt omne quod agunt. Ex quo concluditur, quod pax est vel ipsa beatitudo, vel proxima ad beatitudinem dispositio.
paras.en: [[20:19|and said to them: Peace be to you|et dixit eis: Pax vobis]]. What Christ taught, that He did. For He commanded the disciples: [[Luke 10:5|Into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace be to this house|In quamcumque domum intraveritis, primum dicite : Pax huic domui]]. Hence He Himself, entering the house in which were His dearest and most chosen disciples, says: Peace be to you. Again, He so greeted them because a little before, on the night He was betrayed, He had said: [[John 14:27|Peace I leave with you|Pacem relinquo vobis]]. What He left then, therefore, He now brought, gave and increased. The disciples too were in the greatest need of peace, since they were troubled and frightened in many ways: by the passion of Christ now past, by the cruelty of the Jews, and by a certain hesitation of their own hearts about Christ's resurrection, of whose truth they had not yet been made firm. Moreover, He so greeted the disciples because peace is the greatest good, to be sought above all by every Christian: through which men become sons of God, as it is written: [[Matt 5:9|Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.|Beati pacifici: quoniam filii Dei vocabuntur.]]. Wherefore Dionysius says that all things seek peace, and for its sake do all that they do. From which it is concluded that peace is either beatitude itself, or the disposition nearest to beatitude.

paras.t: Christus autem præsertim nunc loquitur de pace interna, quæ est tranquillitas animi, utpote quies a motibus propriis inordinatis, videlicet a timore immoderato, a tristitia sæculi, quæ secundum Apostolum, mortem operatur, a dolore rationem impediente. Non enim optavit discipulis quietem ab exterioribus persecutionibus ad tempus, quos in medio luporum erat missurus, sed ut in omni turbatione extrinseca conservarent pacem internam. Propterea ad Hebræos monet Apostolus : Pacem sequimini et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit.
paras.en: But Christ is here speaking chiefly of inward peace, which is tranquillity of mind, namely rest from one's own disordered motions: from immoderate fear, from the sorrow of the world, which, according to the Apostle, worketh death[[2 Cor 7:10||]], from grief that hinders reason. For He did not wish His disciples rest from outward persecutions for the time, since He was about to send them into the midst of wolves[[Matt 10:16||]], but that amid every outward disturbance they might keep inward peace. Hence the Apostle admonishes the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:14|Follow peace with all men and holiness: without which no man shall see God|Pacem sequimini et sanctimoniam, sine qua nemo Deum videbit]].

paras.t: Et quum hoc dixisset, ostendit eis manus et latus, forte et pedes : imo et pedes, ut infra ex verbis Lucæ evangelistæ patebit. In his quinque vulnerum remanserunt cicatrices, in testimonium identitatis corporis passi, resuscitati, et glorificati, itemque in signum victoriæ Salvatoris. Ostendit ergo discipulis manus perfossas, et latus lancea perforatum, ut scirent quod ipse esset qui paulo ante pendebat in ligno, et quod idem numero corpus resumpsisset. — Multa hoc loco omittit Joannes, quæ recitat Lucas; ea quoque quæ Lucas omisit, supplevit Joannes. Itaque Luca testante, Christus discipulis dixit : Videte manus meas et pedes meos; palpate et videte, quoniam spiritus carnem et ossa non habet, sicut me videtis habere. Et alia multa in hac apparitione dicta et facta recitat Lucas.
paras.en: [[20:20|And when he had said this, he shewed them his hands and his side|Et cum hoc dixisset, ostendit eis manus et latus]], perhaps the feet too: indeed the feet too, as will appear below from the words of Luke the Evangelist. In these the scars of the five wounds remained, in witness of the identity of the body that suffered, was raised and was glorified, and also as a sign of the Saviour's victory. He showed the disciples, then, the pierced hands and the side opened by the lance, that they might know that He was the one who a little before hung on the wood, and that He had taken again the body numerically the same. — Many things John omits in this place which Luke recounts; and what Luke omitted, John supplied. So, by Luke's witness, Christ said to the disciples: [[Luke 24:39|See my hands and feet, that it is I myself. Handle, and see: for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as you see me to have|Videte manus meas et pedes meos; palpate et videte, quoniam spiritus carnem et ossa non habet, sicut me videtis habere]]. And Luke recounts many other things said and done in this appearance[[Luke 24:36||]].

paras.t: Gavisi sunt ergo discipuli, viso Domino dominorum, qui in femore suo scriptum habet : Rex regum et Dominus dominantium. Gaudium nempe est diffusio animi in conceptione boni, oriturque ex unione potentiæ cum bono convenienti. Quoniam ergo discipuli viderunt Jesum, summum et convenientissimum bonum, quem maxime diligebant, de cujus passione vehementer dolebant, cujus beatitudini cordialiter congratulabantur : ideo viso eo, ultra quam æstimari posset aut exprimi, lætabantur. Gavisi sunt autem propter Jesum, et propter se ipsos : quia magistro suo intime congaudebant ; et de suo profectu exhilarati sunt, videntes se non esse deceptos sequendo Jesum, propter quem omnia sua reliquerunt, et multa perpessi fuerunt ac patiebantur.
paras.en: [[20:20|The disciples therefore were glad, when they saw the Lord|Gavisi sunt ergo discipuli, viso Domino]] of lords, who hath on His thigh written: [[Apoc 19:16|KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]]. For joy is the expansion of the mind in the conceiving of a good, and arises from the union of a power with a fitting good. Since, then, the disciples saw Jesus, the highest and most fitting good, whom they loved most, for whose passion they grieved vehemently, in whose beatitude they heartily rejoiced with Him: therefore, seeing Him, they were glad beyond what could be reckoned or expressed. They rejoiced for Jesus' sake and for their own: because they rejoiced inwardly with their Master; and they were cheered at their own advancement, seeing that they had not been deceived in following Jesus, for whom they had left all they had[[Matt 19:27||]], and had suffered and were suffering much.

paras.t: Dixit ergo eis iterum : Pax vobis. Siquidem viso Domino Jesu, conturbati fuerunt atque conterriti, juxta Lucam : ideo repetit, Pax vobis. Quæ etiam repetitio, confirmationis indicium est, dilectionisque signum, et admonitio discipulorum ut pacem jugiter appetant, præcipueque exquirant. Vel, ideo bis ait, Pax vobis, quia optavit eis pacem gratiæ in præsenti, et pacem gloriæ in futuro. Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos : id est, quemadmodum Pater misit me ex vera caritate et pietate, ad prædicandum Evangelium vitæ Judæis, a quibus multas persecutiones, et tandem amarissimam perpessus sum mortem, quorum tamen hominum nonnullos converti; sic ego nunc mittam vos ad prædicandum evangelicam legem Judæis ac gentibus, ex caritate et pietate ad vos, et item ad illos, a quibus multa adversa et mortem sustinebitis, quosdam vero eorum convertetis.
paras.en: [[20:21|He said therefore to them again: Peace be to you|Dixit ergo eis iterum: Pax vobis]]. For on seeing the Lord Jesus they were troubled and terrified, according to Luke[[Luke 24:37||]]: therefore He repeats, Peace be to you. This repetition too is a token of confirmation and a sign of love, and an admonition to the disciples to seek peace constantly and to pursue it above all. Or, He says Peace be to you twice because He wished them the peace of grace in the present and the peace of glory in the future. [[20:21|As the Father hath sent me, I also send you|Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos]]: that is, as the Father sent Me out of true charity and loving-kindness to preach the Gospel of life to the Jews, from whom I suffered many persecutions and at last a most bitter death, and yet some of whom I converted; so I now will send you to preach the law of the Gospel to Jews and Gentiles, out of charity and loving-kindness towards you and likewise towards them, from whom you will endure many adversities and death, but some of whom you will convert.

paras.t: Hæc quum dixisset, insufflavit, et dixit eis : Accipite Spiritum Sanctum. Postquam Salvator dixit discipulis, Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos, infudit discipulis Spiritum Sanctum, quia officium prædicationis quod eis commisit, sine speciali gratia Spiritus Sancti expleri non valuit. Oportet enim ut prædicator verbi cœlestis, in se ipso abundet caritatis fervore, et sapientia divinorum, quatenus ignita proferat verba, motiva et penetrativa, sitque sententiosus, discretus et instructivus in sermonibus suis. Denique, per corporalem illam insufflationem et inspirationem, evidenter signavit superintellectualem atque æternam processionem seu spirationem qua Spiritus Sanctus ab ipso procedit, prout plenius probat Anselmus in libro de Processione Spiritus Sancti. Rursus, dicendo, Accipite Spiritum Sanctum, insinuavit se per auctoritatem dare Spiritum Sanctum : quod nequaquam sic esset, nisi Spiritus Sanctus ab ipso procederet. Sed nonne Apostoli ante hanc horam habuerunt Spiritum Sanctum? Habuerunt utique, non autem tam copiose et efficaciter, seu ad tot tantosque effectus, ut ex hac hora, quia et nunc data est omnibus eis potestas ligandi atque solvendi, sicut mox introducetur.
paras.en: [[20:22|When he had said this, he breathed on them; and he said to them: Receive ye the Holy Ghost|Hæc cum dixisset, insufflavit, et dixit eis: Accipite Spiritum Sanctum]]. After the Saviour had said to the disciples, As the Father hath sent me, I also send you, He poured the Holy Ghost into them, because the office of preaching which He committed to them could not be fulfilled without a special grace of the Holy Ghost. For the preacher of the heavenly word must abound in himself with the fervour of charity and with wisdom in divine things, so that he may utter fiery words, moving and piercing, and be weighty, discerning and instructive in his sermons. Further, by that bodily breathing and inbreathing He plainly signified the supra-intellectual and eternal procession or spiration by which the Holy Ghost proceeds from Him, as Anselm proves more fully in his book On the Procession of the Holy Ghost. Again, by saying, Receive ye the Holy Ghost, He intimated that He gives the Holy Ghost by authority: which would by no means be so unless the Holy Ghost proceeded from Him. But did not the Apostles have the Holy Ghost before this hour? They did indeed, but not so abundantly and effectively, or for so many and such great effects, as from this hour, since now too the power of binding and loosing was given to them all, as will shortly be brought in.

paras.t: Augustinus facit hic grandem quæstionem, cujus se solutionem nescire fatetur. Quærit ergo, cur Christus bis dedit Spiritum Sanctum, semel in terra ante ascensionem, et semel de cœlo post ascensionem. Tangit autem Augustinus quamdam solutionem sub dubio, puta quod ideo, quoniam duo sunt præcepta caritatis. Quam rationem Gregorius et Beda affirmant esse hujus rei causam, videlicet, quod in terra dedit, ut diligatur proximus, deinde de cœlo, ut diligatur Deus. Sed quia per eamdem gratiam utrumque præceptum impletur, nec unum sine alio valet impleri, imo et unus est habitus caritatis qua Deus proximusque diligitur, ideo potest alia ratio assignari. Ut enim Dionysius docet, Natura non procedit a distanti in distans, nisi per medium. Quem processum auctor naturæ Deus sublimis et benedictus, observat frequenter, præsertim quum teste Apostolo, Quæ a Deo sunt, ordinata sunt. Unde et admonet : Omnia decenter et secundum ordinem fiant in vobis. Hinc ergo Christus sapientia Patris, disponens universa suaviter, suos discipulos paulatim ad sublimiora attollens, ac pedetentim ad perfectionem perducens, primo dedit eis Spiritum Sanctum in terra per insufflationem, non in tanta plenitudine, nec in signo tam evidenti ut postea, quatenus per istam ad illam exuberantissimam Spiritus Sancti susceptionem quæ facta est in die sancto Pentecostes, disponerentur.
paras.en: Augustine here raises a great question, the solution of which he confesses he does not know. He asks, then, why Christ gave the Holy Ghost twice, once on earth before the ascension and once from heaven after the ascension. Augustine touches, though doubtfully, on one solution: namely that it was because there are two precepts of charity. This reason Gregory and Bede affirm to be the cause of the matter: that He gave the Spirit on earth that our neighbour may be loved, and then from heaven that God may be loved. But since both precepts are fulfilled by the same grace, and one cannot be fulfilled without the other, and indeed there is one habit of charity by which God and neighbour are loved, another reason can be assigned. For as Dionysius teaches, nature does not proceed from one extreme to another except through a mean. This procedure God, the sublime and blessed author of nature, frequently observes, especially since, as the Apostle witnesses, [[Rom 13:1|those that are ordained of God|Quæ a Deo sunt, ordinata sunt]]. Whence he also admonishes: [[1 Cor 14:40|let all things be done decently and according to order|Omnia decenter et secundum ordinem]] among you. Hence Christ, the wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]], ordering all things sweetly[[Wis 8:1||]], raising His disciples little by little to higher things and leading them step by step to perfection, first gave them the Holy Ghost on earth by breathing, not in such fullness nor with so evident a sign as afterwards, so that by this they might be disposed for that most overflowing reception of the Holy Ghost which took place on the holy day of Pentecost.

paras.t: Quorum remiseritis peccata, eos legitime absolvendo, et divinæ virtuti, quæ sola dimittit peccata ut causa principalis, instrumentaliter vi clavium cooperando, remittuntur eis a Deo, saltem quoad culpam, non tamen semper aut totaliter quantum ad pœnam. Tamen, per orationem sacerdotis virtutemque clavium, et per pudorem ac contritionem confitentis, aliquid pœnæ dimittitur, tanto utique amplius, quanto pudor et contritio fuerint fortiores. Possent enim esse tam magni, quod tota pœna dimitteretur. Et quorum peccata retinueritis, id est, non dimiseritis, sed retinenda judicaveritis, eo quod non vere pœniteant, nec dignos se præbeant ad indulgentiam obtinendam, retenta sunt, id est, Deus illa imputabit hominibus talibus. Oportet itaque ut judicium Ecclesiæ conformetur divino judicio, servando videlicet rectum processum, et debitum clavium usum. Unde ultimo Ecclesiasticæ hierarchiæ capitulo, ait Theologus : Sacerdotes hierarchicis sibi collatis virtutibus uti oportet, prout Deitas moverit eos. Agens enim instrumentale non sortitur efficaciam, nisi secundum quod a principali causa movetur. Propter quod profitetur Apostolus : Secundum potestatem quæ data est mihi in ædificationem, et non in destructionem.
paras.en: [[20:23|Whose sins you shall forgive|Quorum remiseritis peccata]], by lawfully absolving them, and cooperating instrumentally by the power of the keys with the divine power, which alone forgives sins as principal cause, [[20:23|they are forgiven them|remittuntur eis]] by God, at least as to the guilt, though not always or wholly as to the punishment. Yet by the prayer of the priest and the power of the keys, and by the shame and contrition of the penitent, something of the punishment is remitted, and the more so the stronger the shame and contrition are. For they could be so great that the whole punishment would be remitted. [[20:23|And whose sins you shall retain|Et quorum retinueritis]], that is, do not forgive, but judge must be retained, because they do not truly repent nor show themselves worthy to obtain pardon, [[20:23|they are retained|retenta sunt]], that is, God will impute them to such men. The judgement of the Church, therefore, must be conformed to the divine judgement, by keeping a right procedure and the due use of the keys. Whence in the last chapter of the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy the Theologian [[that is, Dionysius]] says: Priests must use the hierarchical powers conferred on them as the Godhead moves them. For an instrumental agent has no efficacy except as it is moved by the principal cause. Wherefore the Apostle professes: [[2 Cor 13:10|according to the power which the Lord hath given me unto edification and not unto destruction|Secundum potestatem quæ data est mihi in ædificationem, et non in destructionem]].

paras.t: Itaque Christus nunc ait et confert universis Apostolis, quod ante passionem Petro singulariter dixit : Quodcumque, inquiens, ligaveris super terram, erit ligatum et in cœlis ; et quodcumque solveris super terram, erit solutum et in cœlis. Ideo autem Petro tanquam principaliori inter Apostolos et capiti universalis Ecclesiæ, hoc dictum est singulariter, ut quum sit ordo in Ecclesia, hæc potestas credatur primo ac principaliter residere in summo Pontifice, S. Petri vicario, atque ab ipso derivari in archiepiscopos et episcopos, et ab ipsis tanquam a mediis, in simplices sacerdotes. Verumtamen, quamvis omnis sacerdos in sua ordinatione ligandi ac solvendi potestatem recipiat, quum secundum Thomam, realiter idem sint character sacerdotalis, et potestas prædicta, quæ etiam clavis vocatur; non tamen habet hujus potestatis exsecutionem, nisi ei subjiciatur materia, scilicet homines super quos sibi jurisdictio detur, seu cura animarum committatur a superiore, qui sicut dat eam inferiori, sic potest eam ei auferre in toto vel parte, legitima causa occurrente.
paras.en: So Christ now says to, and confers on, all the Apostles what before the passion He said to Peter singly: [[Matt 16:19|whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth, it shall be bound also in heaven|Quodcumque … ligaveris … et in cœlis]]. It was said to Peter singly, as the chief among the Apostles and head of the universal Church, so that, there being order in the Church, this power may be believed to reside first and principally in the supreme Pontiff, the vicar of St Peter, and to be derived from him to archbishops and bishops, and from them, as intermediaries, to simple priests. Nevertheless, although every priest receives in his ordination the power of binding and loosing, since according to Thomas the priestly character and the said power, which is also called the key, are really the same, yet he does not have the exercise of this power unless matter is subjected to him, namely men over whom jurisdiction is given him, or the care of souls is committed to him by a superior; who, as he gives it to the inferior, so can take it from him in whole or in part, when a lawful cause arises.

paras.t: Præterea, Christus dicendo discipulis, Quorum remiseritis peccata, etc., manifeste ostendit se esse verum Deum, qui solus potest tantam conferre potestatem hominibus, quæ nec angelis data est. Decuit autem ut postquam Deus assumpsit humanam naturam, homines ab illo acciperent divinam virtutem, et supernaturalem quamdam deificationem : quod maxime datum est sacerdotibus, per hoc quod sunt dispensatores sacramentorum novæ legis, in quibus gratia continetur et datur. Omnibus quoque fidelibus datur deificatio talis, per diversa dona et gratiam Spiritus Sancti, secundum quod in epistola canonica Petri inducitur : Maxima et pretiosa nobis promissa donavit, ut per hæc efficiamini divinæ consortes naturæ. — Postremo, de hac materia, et quid sit clavis, et quomodo sacerdos evangelicæ legis dicatur peccata dimittere, an scilicet aliquid cooperando, vel dumtaxat ostendendo, de verbis quoque Hieronymi circa hoc, plurima dixi super Matthæum : quæ non sunt hoc loco repetenda, quamvis ista sine illis plene intelligi nequeant.
paras.en: Further, Christ, by saying to the disciples, Whose sins you shall forgive, etc., plainly showed Himself to be true God, who alone can confer on men so great a power, one not given even to the angels. And it was fitting that, after God had assumed human nature, men should receive from Him a divine power and a certain supernatural deification: which is given above all to priests, in that they are dispensers of the sacraments of the new law, in which grace is contained and given. Such deification is also given to all the faithful, through the divers gifts and grace of the Holy Ghost, as is set down in the canonical epistle of Peter: [[2 Pet 1:4|he hath given us most great and precious promises: that by these you may be made partakers of the divine nature|Maxima et pretiosa nobis promissa donavit, ut per hæc efficiamini divinæ consortes naturæ]]. — Lastly, on this matter, what the key is, how the priest of the Gospel law is said to forgive sins, whether by cooperating in some way or only by declaring, and on Jerome's words about it, I said a great deal on Matthew[[Matt 16:19||]]: which is not to be repeated here, though these things cannot be fully understood without it.

paras.t: Dedit itaque Christus Apostolis eorumque successoribus divinam et admirabilem potestatem, qua alios possunt solvere et ligare, a regno excludere, et in illud inducere. Sed videant ministri Ecclesiæ ut tanta virtute digne utantur, exsistendo in gratia, causasque confitentium sapienter pensando ac discernendo, et privatum amorem ac odium, ceterasque inordinatas affectiones penitus repellendo : quoniam si indignos absolvant, vel dignos ligent, dicetur de eis illud Ezechielis : Interfecerunt animas quæ non moriuntur, et vivificabant animas quæ non vivunt.
paras.en: So Christ gave the Apostles and their successors a divine and wonderful power, by which they can loose and bind others, shut them out of the kingdom and bring them into it. But let the ministers of the Church see that they use so great a power worthily, being in grace, weighing and discerning wisely the cases of those who confess, and wholly casting out private love and hatred and other disordered affections: for if they absolve the unworthy or bind the worthy, that word of Ezechiel will be said of them: [[Ezech 13:19|to kill souls which should not die, and to save souls alive which should not live|Interfecerunt animas quæ non moriuntur, et vivificabant animas quæ non vivunt]] [[that is, They killed souls which do not die, and quickened souls which do not live]].

paras.t: Thomas autem unus ex duodecim, hoc est unus Apostolorum, qui ante passionem Christi erant duodecim, quando Judas fuit unus illorum ; vel, Unus ex duodecim, quia dum Joannes evangelium præsens descripsit, successit Mathias in locum Judæ, sicque Thomas fuit unus Apostolorum, qui Mathia electo fuerunt duodecim; qui dicitur Didymus : quod interpretatum est dubius, quia de Christi resurrectione præ ceteris fuit incredulus ; non erat cum eis, quando venit Jesus. Huic videtur contrarium quod Lucas habet, duos discipulos regressos a castello Emmaus invenisse congregatos undecim, quorum unus exstitit Thomas. Respondet Augustinus, quod Thomas adfuit redeuntibus illis duobus : quibus loquentibus, Thomas propter aliquam causam exivit, et interim apparuit Christus. Potest etiam dici, quod iste sit sensus verborum Lucæ : Invenerunt congregatos undecim, id est Apostolos, qui pro tunc undecim erant, quamvis non fuerunt omnes collecti. Est quoque consuetudo Scripturæ, ut aliquid attribuatur toti communitati, quia majori vel principaliori ejus competit parti.
